### Batch eleven (24 Nov): per-member summonstones
- **Cause.** Each side has ONE summon entry (`bs + 0x754 + 40*side`), built at the battle start by `FUN_0888C4C8` -> `FUN_08890BB8(entry, side, stone)` with
  the slot fighter's stone (record `+0x10 + 0xC6*set + 0xBA`, set = record byte `+0x773`). Every member of the side (partners, members swapped in) summoned that stone.
- **Fix** (`sum_track`, `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_SIDESTONE=1`: old). The entry is rebuilt with `FUN_08890BB8` for whoever is about to summon: a partner with the request
  bit (actor `+0x5B3` & 0x10) when the slot fighter has none, else the slot fighter (`[SUMSTONE] ... entry rebuilt for partner/slot fighter ...: stone A -> B`).
  - After a rebuild the request waits 30 controller frames (`PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_STONEWAIT`) before the step sees it (`slotactor_hook`): presented the same
    frame, the use was spent but no summon started (`stone5a/b`).
  - Hold: the entry stays the partner's while his request waits (up to 180 frames; his request bit is kept set meanwhile, the game clears it within a few frames) and, once his use is spent (his summon started), for 600 frames more
    (`PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_STONEHOLD`, about 20 s). Neither the entry's words nor the manager change while a summon plays (`stone7e`, a debug dump of both),
    so the hold is timed. While it lasts the slot fighter's request waits; like a press during a running summon in retail, it is not queued.
  - Test aid `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_TESTSTONE=<slot stone>,<partner 0 stone>` writes those stones into side 1's records; `FORCESUMMON` keeps the partner's request
    bit set for up to 90 frames.
- **Verified** (`tools_dbg/sumtest.py`, `SUM_DIRECT=party_battle_walk.txt`, 3v3, `TESTSTONE=15,18`, `FORCESUMMON=0:700`, `FORCESUMMON_SLOT=1:26,1:50`, `~/dissidia/tt/stone8b`):
  the partner's request at 23.4 s rebuilds the entry 15 -> 18, his use is spent at 24.4 s and his summon is on screen (`stone7b`, shot at 24 s); the slot
  fighter's request at 26 s waits; at 44.4 s the entry goes back to 15; his request at 50 s goes through and Odin's Zantetsuken plays (shot at 51 s).
- Stone ids 0..0x0B are AUTO summons: a forced request with an AUTO stone is not taken by the step (as in retail), so the tests use manual stones.

### Batch thirteen (25 Nov): the big summon orb after a swap (cause: the use booking)
TODO "the big retail orb not refreshing after a swap". **The orb is right; the booking of who has summoned was wrong.**
- **How the orb works (battle overlay, decoded this round).** The summon manager (`FUN_08A220F4`, this = manager) owns a HUD object at manager + 256.
  - It holds one orb record per side at HUD + 356 + 52 * side.
  - The record's effect handle sits at +8. The debug log below shows it as "+4" because its base is 4 bytes early.
  - The per-frame step `FUN_08A06370` (`FUN_08A06524` / `FUN_08A06684` / `FUN_08A0676C`) creates the orb effect when `FUN_08A06A18` says the side can summon. That check goes through `FUN_0889120C`, the gate that reads the slot fighter's uses (+0x10CE). It deletes the effect when the side can't.
  - So the orb follows the CURRENT slot fighter's uses by itself. A refill path exists too: item 0xEF in `FUN_08A220F4` calls `FUN_08A07320(manager + 256, side)` -> `FUN_08A0641C`, which re-creates the effect, then sets the uses to 1. It is not needed.
- **Cause.** `sum_track` booked a member as "summon used" whenever his uses read 0. After a KO rebuild, the partner's actor reads 0 for a moment. Test `~/dissidia/tt/orb2`: the CPU's partner (char 30) was booked "summon used" at 46.6 s without summoning. He then came into the slot with 0 uses, so the game showed no orb, which was correct for 0 uses.
- **Fix** (`tagteam.cpp`). `stock_hook` records each use the game's summon step really spends in `g_sum_spent_real` (side, character). The tracker books a member as spent only on such a spend. `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_SUMUSED_ANYZERO=1` gives the old behaviour.
- **Tested** (headless, `sumtest.py`, `sp_cpu_walk.txt`, side 1 given stones 15 / 18 with `TESTSTONE=15,18`):
  - `tt/orb3`: the CPU slot fighter summons at 25 s (orb gone). KO at 45 s, and the partner enters with his own use: `slot fighter char 31 -> 30, summon uses 0 -> 1`. The game re-creates the orb at 46.67 s; screenshots show the orb on Vaan's panel.
  - `tt/orb5`: the partner summons at 24.4 s (a real spend, booked). KO at 40 s, and he enters with his use spent: `uses 1 -> 0`. The game removes the orb at 41.67 s.
- Debug aid: `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_ORBLOG=1` logs every change of both orb records (`[ORBLOG]`).

### Batch fourteen (25 Nov): desync at frame 0 / 1 between Android and PC (analysis + diagnostics)
- **What is compared** (`netplay.cpp collect`): 66 values at the start of every delivered lock-step frame: the battle clock, per fighter (slot 0 and 1) 13 fields (pos, body, script, motion time, HP block), the assist gauge, 17 FNV-1a hashes of the fighter struct in 256-byte blocks (guest pointers and viewer-only bits masked), and the number / characters of the fighters on the stage. Only the first mismatch was printed, so a log could not tell a fixed difference from a growing one.
- **Frame 1 (`rp6_2v2_1122_2255`)**: 11 fields differ, `body.x/y/z` in 199..409 ulp of both fighters while `pos` and HP agree. Cause: clang for ARM fuses `a * b + c` (FMA), the PC build rounds twice (VFPU matrix code in the runtime). Fixed 23 Nov ("Batch three", `runtime/CMakeLists.txt`). Evidence it holds across arm64 / x86_64: `rp6_laguna_1124_1352.log` (RP6) against `desk_laguna_1124_1352.log` (desktop) compare equal for frames 0..997 (the later desync there is the Laguna / rand bug, fixed).
- **Remaining float sources checked**: the game's own code is the lifted MIPS (`generated/batch_*.cpp`, one operation per statement, so no contraction even with clang's default `-ffp-contract=on`; float to int goes through `psp_sat_f2i`); the VFPU math is PPSSPP's table code (no libm sin / cos); the libm `sin` / `cos` / `atan2` / `pow` calls in the runtime are camera, HUD and savedata-dialog code, not simulation. Added `-ffp-contract=off` to the phone's zig build (`android_build.py device_build`) and the setup app build (`build_setup_app.py`).
- **Frame 0 (`rp6_desync_1122_2242`)**: 16 fields differ, all blocks of fighter 0 from 0x100 up (and 0xE00..0x1000 of fighter 1), none of the gameplay fields. Fighter 0's and fighter 1's block 0xF00 hash equal here and differ on the other machine: that looks like data a fresh heap has not been given (uninitialised words, the other machine had already played a battle), not a different simulation. Not proven: the other log is missing, no other log shows it (the 22 Nov 2v2 log agrees at frame 0, all later cross-arch logs too).
- **Diagnostics added** (nothing changes in the game): (1) the first THREE mismatching frames are printed in full (field names with both values), so a fixed difference (same fields every frame) can be told from drift (more fields each frame); (2) at frames 0 and 1 of every battle each machine logs `[NETSYNC] this build: <arch>, fused multiply-add on/off, <compiler>` and `[NETDUMP0] frame= fighter= block=` lines with every word of both fighters (as hashed: pointers and viewer-only bits are zero). `PSPRECOMP_NETSYNC_F0DUMP=0` turns the dump off. Next time: take BOTH players' `run.log`, then `grep NETDUMP0 a.log > a; grep NETDUMP0 b.log > b; diff a b` names the words (block offset + word index) that differ at frame 0 / 1.
- **If it is leftover memory**: zero those words at the battle start on both machines (or mask them in `viewer_mask`) once the diff names them.
- **Env flags**: `PSPRECOMP_NETSYNC_F0DUMP=0` (no dump). The three-frame reporting has no switch (log only).
- **Tested** (host, 25 Nov, `~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttdsy`): two copies with different saves, `mp_test.py --menu-mode team2 --fill`: `r1` 1486+ frames 0 mismatched on both, the `[NETDUMP0]` lines of A and B identical (68 each); `r2` (`PSPRECOMP_NET_PERTURB=100` on A) prints DESYNC for frames 101, 102, 103 only. `[NETSYNC] this build: x86_64, fused multiply-add off`. Single player `tagteam_test.py --baseline`: RESULT PASS. The FMA probe was checked with g++ `-mfma -ffp-contract=fast` (reports ON) / `off` (off).
- **Not tested**: arm64 against x86_64 live (the desktop with the Android emulator was off, 192.168.2.131 unreachable; the emulator runs translated code anyway). Please collect on a new Android + PC session: both `run.log` files of the same battle (`last_run.log` on Android), taken right after the battle.


### Batch fifteen (25 Nov): menus flow back (user, RP6: "back does not return to the previous tag menu")
- **Cause.** The chain is Battle Mode / Communications list > Mode Select > Party Select > CPU Select > setup screen (+ Battle Lobby, opened by the flow). Retail's Circle went
  straight from Party Select back to the list (Mode Select skipped), and Circle on the setup screen left the lobby behind. Also, `tag_row_confirm` took Circle for a confirm
  on the Tag Team Battle row (the sub-list's pad test is true for Circle: `PSPRECOMP_MENU_SUBLOG=1`, Circle = "sub args 1"), so Circle at the list opened the Mode Select again
  (a loop with the Mode Select's own Circle).
- **Fix** (`PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_MENUBACK_OLD=1` = old). Single player: Circle on the setup screen's list (no dialog; not in the Free-for-all) reopens the Battle Lobby
  (`g_lob_flow`, settings kept), Circle in that lobby goes back to Party Select (one injected Circle for retail's screen; Cross = done as before; a lobby opened with Select
  still closes with Circle/Cross); footer says so. `menu_settings.cpp`: after a tag mode was chosen (`g_ms_flow`), when the same group's list comes back (gap > 0.25 s) the Mode
  Select opens again (SP and Communications; Circle there clears the flow and goes to the list); the confirm test ignores the sub-list's Circle.
- **Tested** (host, one copy, `~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttmback/ctl.py`, screenshots in `o4`/`o7`/`o8`/`o9`): Team 2 vs 2 forward: Mode Select > Party Select > CPU Select > Lobby > setup;
  back: setup > Lobby (stage change kept) > CPU Select > Party Select > Mode Select > list (cursor on Tag Team Battle) > main menu. Free-for-all: players > setup > CPU Select >
  Party Select > Mode Select. Duel: Party Select > Mode Select. Communications: Mode Select > Group Battle room screen, Circle > Mode Select > list. Not run: two-copy online.
- **Follow-up (25 Nov, user test of the merged back flow).** (1) Back out past the lobby (setup > Battle Lobby > CPU / Party Select) and forward again skipped the lobby: `g_lobby_pending` was
  consumed once. Now backing out of the lobby (and out of the Free-for-all players screen) sets `g_rearm`; when the setup screen has been gone for 0.5 s the lobby (FFA: the players screen) is pending again
  (`[TTLOBBY] the setup screen is back after backing out: the lobby again`). (2) After a Mode Select choice the list cursor showed Quick Battle (Party) for a moment: the confirm writes that row for retail,
  and the retail list was visible until the next menu came. The Mode Select is now redrawn frozen (cursor on the chosen row, `g_ms_hold`) over the list from the sub-list's tick until the next screen
  (the layer lives 450 ms after the last draw: `ge_draw_set_game_layer_ttl`, psp_ge_draw.cpp; the retail list was visible for a few frames after the confirm). `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_MENUBACK_OLD=1` = old for (1), `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_MSHOLD_OFF=1` = old for (2).
  Tested (host, `~/dissidia/tt/s2/ffamenu`, shots `r2b_*`, `s1..s3`): 2v2: setup > lobby > Circle > CPU Select > Cross > lobby again; Mode Select click: 60 frames at ~30 ms: Mode Select straight to the Party Select fade, no list frame; FFA too; FFA players > Circle > Circle (CPU Select) > Cross: players screen again.

### Batch sixteen (25 Nov): Free-for-all menus without the scripted walk, picks from the game's own selectors
- **Cause.** Mode Select > Free-for-all injected pad presses by poll count (`g_script_t`: Cross at polls 220 / 340 / 460, five Downs, Cross at 720) to pass Party Select and CPU Select unseen, then showed the players screen with a text list.
  Poll counts depend on frame rate and load (slow Android, online lag), and the user never chose anything in the game's own selector.
- **Fix** (`PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_FFA_SCRIPT=1` = the old scripted walk, `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_FFA_NOPREFILL=1` = walk the screens but keep the players screen's own values). The screens are no longer passed by script: the player walks the
  real Party Select (P1's party) and CPU Select (1st / 2nd / 3rd = P2 / P3 / P4; the 4th / 5th picks are unused). Arriving at the setup screen the players screen opens and is filled by `ffa_prefill`:
  P1 main / tag-in = the party's first two members (`screen + 0x788`, 8 bytes apart), P2..P4 mains = the CPU Select picks, kept by the setup screen object at `screen + 0x8B4` + 8 * i (charId, 0 = empty; found by diffing two screen dumps,
  `PSPRECOMP_TTSP_SCRDUMP=<file>` dumps the screen object once). P2 is always on (random when empty); an empty P3 / P4 slot is Off (FFA of 3 = two picks). Strength / tag-in values stay as set.
  Nothing depends on timing now except the short injected confirm after the Mode Select (existing for every mode). Circle on the players screen goes back (setup > CPU Select > Party Select > Mode Select, from Batch fifteen) and coming forward
  again fills the players from the new picks (the re-arm of the follow-up above). Footer: "Circle: back to the selectors".
- **Not done.** The players screen still has its list picker (Cross on a field) for later changes and for the tag-in column; a full replacement would open the game's CPU Select from the players screen (needs the screen object's
  selector state restored, i.e. calling retail's CPU Select open step on demand: not located). Online FFA is unchanged (the room's players). Not tested: Android, online two copies, FFA 3 through to the battle in this route.
- **Tested** (host, one copy, `~/dissidia/tt/s2/ffamenu/ctl.py`, 30 fps): FFA 4: Party A (Jecht, Squall...) + CPU picks Vaan / Laguna / Kain: players screen shows them (`e1_players.png`), lobby, Enter, loading screen Jecht vs Vaan, battle with
  both extras spawned, `[FFA] player P3: LAGUNA`, `P4: KAIN`. FFA 3 (two picks): P4 Off on the players screen and in the lobby panel (`e2_players.png`, `e2_lobby2.png`); lobby > Circle > players > Circle > setup > Circle > CPU Select > Cross: filled again.


### Batch twenty-one (25 Nov): free-for-all audit, every other fighter is a foe (tree ttffafoe, branch tt-ffafoe)
- **Audit.** In a free-for-all (`foes()` = any two fighters) the game still has two sides, so a test written as `side_of(a) == side_of(b)` treats two FFA opponents on one side as friends. All 190 `side_of` tests in tagteam.cpp were read. Already right (verified below, no change): `hitreg_hook`
  (FRIENDLYBLOCK uses `foes`), the damage booking (`afd424_hook` ATTR, HP step `real`), the BRV steal HUD channels, the reactions / break (`booked_extra_victim`, `booked_friendly_slot_handler`, `react_with_opponent`: the break bonus goes to the attacker's handler), the lock cycle, `aim_fix`, `ai_target` / score AI, the KO rules (`ffa_keep`).
  Wrong (same-side fighter treated as a friend): (1) **EX force**: `xgauge_hit_orbs` gave an extra no orbs for a hit on a same-side fighter; (2) assist aim (`assist_aim_follow` `good`) and `aim_fix`'s Assist Off `valid` never aimed at a same-side opponent; (3) the Assist Off call-in / hit-switch / wall-hit
  checks (`ao8_hit_switch`, `ao8_hit_test`, `ao9_wall_pass`, `ao_pick_foe`, Assist Off holds in `assist_off_*`), the chase pair (`chase_pair_start`, the cycle's pick), the mate's foe (`MATE` take-over) and the call-in slow-motion release; (4) the small panel's lethal glow (`hud_lethal`).
  All now use `xfoes(a, b)` (= `foes`, `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_FFAFOES_OLD=1`: the old side test). 2v2 / 3v3 are unchanged (`xfoes` = side test there).
- **Test aids** (log only). `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_HITAUDIT=1`: every registered hit logs `[HITAUDIT] attacker -> victim: victim BRV / HP before and 10 ticks later, BROKEN, attacker BRV / HP / EX, others that changed`. `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_HPM_ALL=1` (with `_HPMATRIX=<action>`): the matrix runs all 12 ordered pairs
  of the four fighters (`_HPM_PAIRS=0..9,a,b` picks pairs: 0 slotH>slotC, 1 slotH>extraP, 2 slotH>extraE, 3 slotC>slotH, 4 slotC>extraP, 5 slotC>extraE, 6 extraP>slotH, 7 extraP>slotC, 8 extraP>extraE, 9 extraE>slotH, a extraE>slotC, b extraE>extraP).
  Recipe (`~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttffafoe/run.sh NAME SECS "ENV"`, FFA 4 clones): `HITAUDIT=1 HPMATRIX=10000 (BRV) or 10089 + HPM_VBRV0=1 (HP) HPM_ALL=1 HPM_GAP=7 HPM_WRONGFOE=1 HPM_NODOWN=1 HPM_AI=1 BT_NO_FREEZE=1`
  (not without `_NODOWN`: the matrix's stand-still list makes the victims `is_down`, every hit is then DEADHIT).
- **Seen** (`~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttffafoe/ai1, ai2`, 125 s each): BRV hits of every pair, cross-side and same-side (extraP > slotH, slotC > extraE, extraE > slotC, slotH > extraP): the victim loses what the attacker gains, nobody else changes; a break (`BROKEN`) of an extra and of a slot fighter, the
  break bonus to the attacker (slotC 3000 -> 5036 when it broke slotH); HP hits (extraP > slotH 9844 -> 7564, slotH > extraP 4787 -> 1787, extraE > extraP 9844 -> 4787) take the victim's HP and the attacker's BRV; a lethal hit by a same-side fighter on the human (`ko4`): -800 KO, `side 0 has nobody left: the battle is decided`
  (the human's fall ends the battle, as designed). `[HUDBREAK] ... break report on the big panel dropped: the team mate was broken` appears for same-side hits: the filter is right (the slot fighter was not broken). EX force (`exN` / `exO`, same run with `_FFAFOES_OLD=1`): extraP > slotH: attacker EX 2000 -> 2150 per hit now, 2000 -> 2000 before.
- **Not checked / left:** the EX force of a SLOT fighter's hit on a same-side extra (retail's orb path, no way to see it in the 10-tick window); summons; the result screen's tally and ranking for 3 / 4 fighters (still open, see above); online FFA with 3+ humans (no two-copy run here: the changed code is battle-state only and
  runs identically on both copies, but it was not compared: `[NETSYNC]` not run).

### Batch seventeen (25 Nov): 3v3 second partner: wrong model, swap / KO pick, silent banter (tree tt3v3, branch tt-3v3p2)
- **Wrong model (cause found).** The fighters' graphics objects (`actor +0x394`) are entries of a table of 192 x 0x13C bytes (`*(0x089D5F94) + 28`). `FUN_0886D0D8(name)`
  finds the template entry by the info row's picture name ("P_GST200_1P") and gives the caller the first entry whose word +12 is 0 (a copy of the template). A new
  fighter's entry keeps +12 == 0 until a later step fills it (retail makes one fighter at a time; Gabranth, Cloud: still 0 after the constructor), and the late extras are made
  in one frame, so the NEXT extra got the SAME entry: two actors on one graphics object, the later one's model drawn for both (enemy Gabranth as Kain / Jecht; the earlier
  agent's "Jecht model, Terra's moves" and the RP6 Batch twelve screenshot). 2v2 never showed it: the last-made extra has no successor. Found with `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_GFXOBJ=1|4`
  (`[GFXOBJ]` / `[GFXTAB]`: +0x394 per extra, shared entries; the ctor's own file objects were right) and `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_MODELAUDIT=1`.
- **Fix** (`gfxclaim_hook` on `0x0886D0D8`, `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_GFXCLAIM_OLD=1`: old): entries it handed out stay held (+12 = 1 during later calls) so none is given twice; log `[GFXCLAIM]`.
  Test aids added: `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_TESTPART="24,13;15,22"` (k-th start partner of team 0 ; team 1 by character), `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_LINEUP=all|<extra index>` (extras frozen in a row /
  one near the human, to look at their models), `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_WATCH_SPAWN=<n>:<hex off>`.
- **Verified** (host, `party_battle_walk.txt`, `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_3V3=1 SP_PARTNER=1 TESTPART=24,13;15,22`, `~/dissidia/tt/s2/tt3v3`): before, `after the spawns: x1(c22)=08C068B0 x2(c24)=08C068B0`
  and the lined-up Gabranth looked like Kain (`p_all.png`, `r6/f16.png`: three Jecht-like figures); after, every extra has its own entry (`b2`), lineup `v10.png` shows Kain, Gabranth
  (armour, cape) and Squall each with their own model.
- **Other one-extra-per-side places** (audit of `g_extra` users): the HUD tick, the overhead panels and the Assist Off call were fixed in Batch six. Now: the clone-only SELECT swap
  (`swap_partner_pick`, partners take turns; `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_SWAPLAST=1` old) and the KO take-over (`te`, the FIRST living partner comes in, as the party order lists them, not the last;
  `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_KOLASTMATE=1` old). 2v2 has one partner: unchanged. Not changed: debug-only paths that use `g_extra[0]` / `[g_nextra-1]` (HPMATRIX, swap probes).
  Not tested here: the KO order and the swap rotation in a played 3v3 (logic only, `[TAGTEAM] swap: N living partners, taking extra k`).
- **Silent second banter line.** The host reproduces the RP6 25 Nov case (`rp6_jecht_banter_1125_1533.log`): in a 3v3 start the line of the second (and often third) entrant is "loaded" but
  the game's start (`FUN_0889F8D4`, from `FUN_08B0D938`) makes no ATRAC stream (no `[ATRAC] id=..` line, sound pool slot object ignoring the start): the previous entrant's line was freed
  in the SAME frame the new one is loaded and played ("entrance of X cut short by the entrance of Y"). Now the previous line is stopped (`FUN_08B0D9B0`) and freed first and the new line is
  loaded 8 frames later (`g_intro_pend_*`, log "the new line follows in 8 frames"; `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_INTRODEFER_OLD=1` old; `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_INTROFREE_OLD=1` for the added stop in `intro_free`).
  Host runs `bn_old` / `bn2` / `bn3`: ATRAC set-up missing for the 2nd (and 3rd) line; `bn4` (fixed): all four lines have `[ATRAC] id=1 ...` before "intro line playing". Not heard (no audio
  capture): the check is the stream being made. The HLE also logs a failed `sceAtracSetDataAndGetID` now.
- **Regression**: `PSPRECOMP_CLOUD=0 python3 tools/tagteam_test.py --work ~/dissidia/work_tt3v3 --baseline` PASS (`~/dissidia/tt/s2/tt3v3/reg2`).

## Report an issue (25 Nov, branch report-issue)

Settings > Debug > **Report an issue** (first row; PC and Android, release builds; `PSPRECOMP_REPORT_OLD=1` hides it). A sub-page: What went wrong (text,
the existing Edit machinery: host keyboard / Android IME through SDL text input, the on-screen keyboard with a pad or touch), Short title (optional), Include memory dump
(default On), Files to send (the list, in the row's description), Send report (Back = cancel), Status.

- Code: `runtime/src/psp_report.cpp` + `include/psp_report.h` (collect, zip, sign, upload; worker thread), `src/report_key.h` (the pre-shared key, committed on purpose:
  the first entry of `keys` in the service config; the service rate-limits), the page in `psp_settings.cpp` (PAGE_REPORT), `psp_report::set_ram` in main.cpp,
  `note_gpu` in the event loop, game facts through `psp_report::set_state_hook` (framerate.cpp: in_battle, mode, frame rate). It is in RUNTIME_SOURCES, so the setup app's
  on-device compile has everything (zlib + `psp_http` + mbedTLS as the cloud sync uses; the URL opens with `SDL_OpenURL`: xdg-open / ShellExecute / open / an ACTION_VIEW intent).
- The zip (<= 24 MB, deflate): report.json (title, description, `system`: version, git commit, OS, device model, Android version / API, CPU, GPU + driver, renderer,
  resolution, game id / region, mods, texture packs, changed debug / tag team switches, in-battle flag, uptime), last_run.log + run.log + setup.log (tail 8 MB), settings.ini,
  env.txt, crash* files, and ram.bin (the used part of the PSP's 128 MB, from address 0; left out when it does not fit). NEVER cloud.ini / cloud/; lines that look like
  tokens / passwords are blanked; the home folder is replaced by `~` and the user name when it is a path component.
- Upload: POST `<base>/v1/report` (`PSPRECOMP_REPORT_URL` overrides the base; default https://party.schindlershadow.com/dissidia-report), headers X-Report-Time and
  X-Report-Sig = HMAC-SHA256(key, "<time>\n<sha256 body>"). Answer `{ok, issue_url}`: the browser opens the issue and a toast says "Issue #N opened". Errors (403 clock, 413,
  429, network) show the server's text; the zip is then saved in `<game folder>/reports/report-<time>.zip` and the path is shown. `PSPRECOMP_REPORT_NO_OPEN=1` skips the browser (tests).
- Tests: `runtime/tests/run_report.sh` (SHA / HMAC vectors, scrub, a real build + signed upload to report_service.py on port 18791 with `make_issue` faked, checks the stored zip,
  403 for a wrong key / old time). Menu run with the game: see the coordinator notes in the commit message / report.
### Batch (25 Nov): Report an issue in both installers (tree ttsetrep, branch tt-setupreport)

- **What**: "Report an issue" in the PC setup (Linux + Windows, `setup/setup_main.cpp`) and the Android setup app (Java UI + engine). Always on the start page (and on the Logs page / the problem page);
  offered first on the failure page ("Not finished" / "Stopped") and, after a run that never ended, at the next start (PC: page "Last run stopped"; Android: a dialog). Page: What went wrong (text: on-screen
  keyboard / host keyboard on PC, an EditText on Android), What is sent (the files list, system info, never ISO / cloud.ini / saves, home paths + user name -> `~`, token-looking lines blanked),
  Send. On success the issue opens in the browser (PC `SDL_OpenURL`, Android `ACTION_VIEW`) and the page says "Issue #N opened"; on failure the zip is saved (PC `<pref dir>/reports/`, Android
  `files/reports/`, with Share / Save as file) and the page shows where. The failing step + reason (`failure`, `last_step`, `last_line` / `last_lines`) go into report.json and the description.
- **Shared code**: `runtime/src/psp_report.cpp` is the one implementation (scrub, zip, SHA / HMAC, system facts, upload). New: `psp_report::set_product(Product)` (name "installer", version, files to send,
  free-space folder, save dir, extra facts: OS, device, Android version, CPU, RAM, free space, installer version), `build_zip_file`. Build flags `PSP_REPORT_STANDALONE` (no game) and `PSP_REPORT_NO_HTTP`.
  The key is only in `src/report_key.h`. PC setup links psp_report + psp_http (+ mbedTLS when the bundle has it, + the embedded CA bundle) + zlib (`setup/CMakeLists.txt`). The Android engine compiles psp_report.cpp
  without upload (system libz) and exposes `Engine.reportPreview / reportBuild / reportSign` (the HMAC is computed natively from report_key.h); `ReportClient.java` does the HTTPS POST (HttpURLConnection).
  The service marks these reports (`system.product == installer` -> "Sent from the installer's Report an issue button").
- **Crash / kill detection (Android)**: `BuildRunner` flushes setup.log per line (a kill leaves the log) and keeps `files/build.running` while a plan runs; found at the next start with no runner = the app was killed
  or crashed -> the dialog offers the report (the facts include Android's `last_exit_reasons`: low memory kill, native crash ...). PC: `install.running` in the pref dir. The setup app's own Java crash report
  dialog now also offers "Report an issue". `res/xml/network_security_config.xml` allows cleartext http only to 10.0.2.2 / 127.0.0.1 / localhost (tests); everything else is HTTPS.
- **Tests (never the real service)**: `tools/report_service/local_service.py STORE [PORT]` (real service code, temp config, `make_issue` faked, port 18792 here). PC: `psprecomp_setup --report "text" --dir D
  [--report-step S]` (no window) -> issue 9001, zip holds setup.log scrubbed (`~`, `token= <removed>`), no cloud.ini; real window under Xvfb driven with xdotool: Welcome -> Report -> type -> Send -> "Issue #9002 opened" (browser
  skipped with `PSPRECOMP_REPORT_NO_OPEN=1`), and with the service down: "Not sent" + the saved zip path. Android (AVD dissidia_16k on the desktop, ssh -R 18792, `files/report_url.txt` = `http://10.0.2.2:18792`):
  Report page, typed text, Send -> "Issue #9003 opened" (zip: update.log + report.json with device / Android 15 / RAM / free space / last_exit_reasons), first try over cleartext was refused by Android (now allowed for 10.0.2.2),
  service unreachable -> "Not sent" + saved zip + share / save; `build.running` marker + restart -> "The last build did not finish" dialog. Emulator killed and verified gone. Logs / shots: `~/dissidia/tt/s2/setupreport/`.
  `runtime/tests/run_report.sh` (the game's report test) still passes.
- **Not verified**: HTTPS from the PC setup (no mbedTLS on this host: the bundle build has it; the code path is the game's), Windows build, the real GitHub service, the Failed page flow with a real failing install
  (screenshots only), an arm64 phone. `PSPRECOMP_REPORT_URL` overrides the service on PC; on Android `files/report_url.txt`.

### Batch nineteen (25 Nov): Assist Off partner returns where it left; call line vs banter audio (tree ttassist, branch tt-assistfix)
- **Partner return (Assist Off call).** The partner that plays the call leaves (PLACE to 5000,5000 while its assist X acts) and used to be put at X's last spot ("round 8 hand-over", `[AO8] hand-over`),
  never where it left from. Now `ao8_finish` returns it to the spot it left from: x / y / z, facing (+0x9C, +0x320, model yaw), stand state (script 1) or air state (102) when it left
  airborne (`game_airborne` read before the PLACE), so the fall speed gathered while parked is dropped. A spot that is off known floor now (nothing sampled within 1.5 m) becomes the nearest known
  floor within 12 m; an unusable departure value becomes a spot next to the caller. A call ended by a hit on the assist keeps the hand-over (the partner takes the hit at the assist's place, as
  before). Log: `[AO8] .. partner P leaves from (x,y,z) yaw .. returns to (..): exactly where it left from`, then `partner P now at (..)`.
  `PSPRECOMP_TTCAM_AO8HANDOVER=1`: the round 8 hand-over; `_AO8BACK=1`: the older PLACE-only return. **Design note:** the round 8 text quotes the user ("The assist disappears and the CPU is
  back where it was before the call") and the agent read it as a complaint, building the hand-over; the 22 Nov TODO then asks for the exact return, which is what this does.
  Host runs (`~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttassist/a3`, clones, `ASSIST=0 FORCECALL=1:14,1:26,0:34`): three returns, departure == return to 3 decimals, first frames after it at the spot (the AI moves from there).
  Two copies, Assist Off online (`mp_ao.py mpao1`, team2, fill, `FORCECALL=1:14,0:26`): both copies print the same departure / return lines, `[NETSYNC] frames compared 1497, mismatched 0`.
- **Call line vs banter audio.** Not reproduced as an actual cut: the new SAS trace (`PSPRECOMP_SAS_TRACE=1` now logs `[SAS] CUT SetVoice|KeyOn|KeyOff v= addr= size=: N% played` for a clip stopped
  or overwritten while it plays) shows no call line (one SAS clip, 7.9 - 10.4 KB, ~0.9 - 1.2 s at its pitch) cut in 5 call-ins (`b2`, `b3`, `b4`: KO call-ins during / after the start banters,
  `KOLIST=cpu:9,human:9.5,partner:10 CALLIN_DELAY=1 SP_PARTNER=1`); the intro line (ATRAC, pool slot) and the call line (SAS) are different engines, not one slot. Two real overlaps are closed:
  (1) the entrant's intro line used to start at the pose 1.2 s after the call line, so a clip longer than the warp-in (slow device / long clip) was talked over by the louder stream: the intro line now
  waits until 2.1 battle seconds after the call line request (`g_callline_t`, `g_intro_play_at`, log `intro line waits for the call line`, battle ticks only: same on every machine);
  (2) a second entrance within 4 s could take the registry slot of the first call line's `_a` bank (`sndreg_make_room` tier 2): banks of a call line requested < 4 s ago are taken last (tier 3).
  `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_CALLHOLD_OLD=1`: both old. **Not verified by ear / on a device.**
- **Regression**: `PSPRECOMP_CLOUD=0 python3 tools/tagteam_test.py --work ~/dissidia/work_ttassist --baseline` PASS (`~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttassist/reg1`).

### Batch twenty (25 Nov): lag when a new player is tagged in (tree ttlag, branch tt-taglag)

- **Measure first**: `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_HITCH=<ms>` (default off) logs `[HITCH] frame N (battle t=..) took X ms (game thread cpu Y, file reads ..); steps (wall/cpu ms): ...` for every game frame over the limit (wall time between two
  frame ends), with every `TtStep` of tag team code that ran in that frame (nested steps indented, `@` = start time on the monotonic clock) and the game's file reads in it (`psp_io_read_stats_take`, psp_hle_io.cpp).
  `[LAYERLAP]` lines (tagteam_hud.cpp) split a slow HUD layer frame; `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_HITCH_PROF=1` + `PSPRECOMP_FUNC_TRACE=1` samples the newest dispatched function (polluted by the audio thread, little use).
  Steps added: tt_frame, fx_frame, layer_frame, group_end_step, breakshot_poll, entrance_step, GE_wait, fighter_dtor, leftover_scan, fighter_ctor, LOAD_FILE_GROUP, preload_member ...
- **Findings** (headless Party A, slot 0 KO at 20 s and 40 s, host load ~35, game thread CPU ms): (1) the file reads are NOT the cost (6 reads, 3-4 MB, 0.6 ms, page cache); the cost is `LOAD_FILE_GROUP` = the game's own model build,
  25-40 ms; (2) the rest of `rebuild_begin` (destructor + constructor + the sweep for leftover blocks `leftover_scan`, a 56 MB word pass = 25 ms) 30-60 ms; (3) **the entrance effect** (tagteam_fx.cpp: column of light, glows)
  made the HUD layer frame cost 25-45 ms EVERY frame for the ~0.3 s of the warp-in / pose (the stutter after the call-in: per pixel exp / pow / sin over a 100k+ pixel band, large glows with a sqrt and three divisions per pixel);
  (4) the first run's worst frames were 190 ms (call-in frame) and 8 consecutive 40-48 ms frames in the entrance.
- **Fixes** (all draw / data-file work, nothing that changes game state; `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_FXSLOW=1` / `PSPRECOMP_GLYPH_CACHE_OFF=1` / `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_PRELOAD_OLD=1` = old behaviour):
  * tagteam_fx.cpp: the column's x / y terms are computed once per pixel column / row (lazily from the band's own coordinates, so the picture is the same). menu_layer.cpp: `glow` without a sqrt for pixels outside, `blend` without divisions
    for an empty pixel and one reciprocal otherwise; a rendered-glyph cache for `text` / `serif_caps` (every string was re-rasterised by FreeType per frame and per shadow pass).
  * `preload_member` (tagteam.cpp): the next member's `load_character` runs 1.5 s after the slot fall (single player / any slot call-in; the due time is only ~3 s after the fall) or 5 s before a fallen extra's call-in
    (`PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_PRELOAD_LEAD`, default 5 s) instead of in the call-in frame. Same call, at tag team clock ticks all machines reach together (the due times come from `g_tt_age`), only when no rebuild / late load /
    entrance / EX Burst is running, and the peek (`next_member_char`) is the one the call-in uses; the files are pinned against `unload_departed` for 40 s (`g_ahead`) so the "departed" sweep does not free them before he is on the stage.
    The later `load_character` finds the files loaded ("already loaded") and does nothing.
  * `leftover_scan`: the pass skips a block of 16 words without a word in the candidates' range at once (same result, 25 -> 15 ms).
- **Numbers** (same scenario, frames over 40 ms from battle second 15; old flags = all three opt-outs): old 12 frames, worst 98 ms (cpu 88), call-in frame 97.6 ms, 8 frames of 40-45 ms in the entrance; new 3 frames, worst 56 ms
  (cpu 45): the preload frame 40-48 ms (the model build, now in a calm frame), the call-in frame 56 ms, none in the entrance. Fallen extra (partner:20 / enemy2:32): old worst 147 ms, new 90 ms.
  Logs `~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttlag/{h1,h10,h11,e1,e2,r2}/run_30.log`.
- **Tests**: `tagteam_test.py --baseline` PASS (`~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttlag/reg1`); two-copy online (`mp_slot.py`, slot 0 KO at 20 s, 2392 frames, both copies preload Vaan at the same battle time 36.6 s, slot take at 41.6 s):
  NETSYNC 0 mismatched on both (`~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttlag/s1`).
- **Not done / open**: the remaining call-in frame (rebuild: destructor + constructor + GE wait, 30-60 ms) and the start-of-battle `spawn_fighter` (50 ms) cannot be split without changing frame order; the two file ids of a load
  could be spread over two frames (the own-file bookkeeping would have to append). Not measured on the RP6 / emulator (phone reads may be cold: the preload also warms them). The per-frame HUD layer (clear + publish of up to
  1920x1088 floats) costs a flat 3-5 ms on the host every battle frame: worth a look for phones.

Environment: `PARTNER_CHAR=19` (Tidus) `ENEMY2_CHAR=26` (Tifa) `CLONES=1`, human = the harness' Squall (cannot be set).
- **Video 37cd7536 (assist, player disappears, slow motion forever).** After Jecht's HP hit on Cloud (Tidus' "Slice & Dice" with the 8-hit counter, "CHANGE" banner, violet hexagon) the screen goes dark blue with the call tint, Jecht is gone from the picture and the match stays at the call's slow motion until the clip ends. Host: a forced call just before another slow-motion event (`FORCECALL=0:19` = the second 19, with `EXBAT=s0:20:s1`, so the call's own 66-tick release falls into the burst's start) left **slow-motion channel 6 at 0.40 for the rest of the run** on v0.1.25 (`tt136old/ox0_196`: `[SLOWCH]` ch6 0.40 at 68.8 s, fighters' `step=0.400`; with the retail call `ox1_196`: ch3 stuck at 0.00); 2 of 6 v0.1.25 runs at that timing, a coin flip because the burst start moves with the AI. Head: 0 of 10 at the same timing (`tt136b/hx*`, `hy*`, `z*`), the cause of the lost release is not pinned down (the release is `callfx_step`'s timeout / hit rule; when `g_callfx_rel` is cleared by another path - `g_callfx_gen != g_battle_gen` returns without giving the channel back - nothing releases it). **Fix (head, safety net):** `slow_watchdog()` in `callfx_step`: channels 3..9 that stay below normal speed for 5 s while no call, burst, finish phase or chase runs are released with retail's `FUN_08A620B0` (`[SLOWWATCH]`; `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_NOSLOWWATCH=1` old). Test aid `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_TESTSTICK=<s>` leaves channel 6 at 0.4: released after 5 s (`tt136b/st1`). "Jecht disappears" was **not reproduced** (human always on stage in the old and new runs); with the slow-motion stuck the retail call tint also stays, which matches the dark blue picture.
- **Video 1f311989 (Cloud's HP attack hits Tidus, Jecht loses the HP).** Frames: Jecht broken (BRV 0), `CLOUD > JECHT -3154`, damage text and reaction on Jecht, Tidus' small panel 10274 HP, BRV 1072 -> 1069 while Cloud's BRV 3154 -> 0 (so the attack did register on Tidus) - consistent with one attack registered on BOTH fighters, the HP booked on the attacker's foe (`[HITFOE]`, Batch of 20 Nov, in v0.1.25) = Jecht, while the player expects the fighter the move was aimed at. Host at head (`HPMATRIX=10089 HPM_PAIRS=7` = extraE -> extraP, `HITAUDIT=1`, `tt136b/h7`, `hA`, `hB`): with only Tidus in reach the HP goes to Tidus (9844 -> 6844 ...); the double-registration case with the human beside him and broken (`HPM_ALSO=0`, `SETBRV=slotH:10:0`) shows both registered in the same frame but the harness' HP move did not fire in those windows, so the HP booking for a double registration was **not observed**. v0.1.25 matrix aids number the pairs differently and have no HITAUDIT; the old build was not compared. Not changed (no evidence for a different victim policy; the open question is "area hit on two fighters: HP to the aimed foe (current) or to the nearest").
- **Video 492aecaf (empty sky, loud static).** Picture: both partner panels read KO (Jecht, Tifa), the human plays Tidus; the 3D view is only grey / white / orange sky for 15 s, HUD and the fight go on. Audio (extracted, `ffmpeg`, spectrogram): the whole clip is continuous full-scale broadband noise (RMS ~12000, 0.25 % samples clipped, spectral flatness like white noise; the other clips show music with harmonics), no loops, short gaps at hits. Both are one fault: the camera eye / look-at = NaN, and the game's sound positioning uses the same fighter / lock-block transforms (NaN -> int conversion = full volume garbage). Reproduced on the host **only with a clone partner** (partner = a copy of the human's character) when slot 0 is KO'd and swapped with the mate (`KOLIST=slot0:20 KOLIST_NAT=1`): in ~40 % of runs the camera manager, the slot's lock block (+0x40..+0x78) and the enemy's transform words become the VFPU NaN `7F800001` / `7FC00001` at ~22 s and stay (`CAMDBG` `eye (nan..`, `[CAMNAN]` scan, `tt136b/ko*`, `kod2`); the PCM dump (`PSPRECOMP_AUDIO_DUMP`) goes from music (flatness 0.06-0.3) to noise (0.65-0.85) from that second (`koa.pcm`). No NaN in 8 runs with distinct characters (head 5, v0.1.25 3), none in 6 clone runs without a KO. First writer of the NaN: `FUN_08B3B950` (the camera smoothing, a VFPU lerp); its NaN input comes from a zero-length / uninitialised vector upstream, not found. **ROOT CAUSE FOUND 26 Nov, fixed: see "Batch forty-eight".** **Mitigation (head, still there as a safety net):** (1) `camera.cpp nan_guard` - SetEye's eye / look-at that are NaN / huge are replaced by a view behind the player's fighter (`[CAMNAN] SetEye got NaN`, `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_NOCAMNAN=1` old); (2) `nan_repair_step` - every frame a fighter's transform words (+0..+0xBF) and its lock block (+0x40..+0x7F) that are NaN are put back to the last finite value (`[NANFIX]`, `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_NONANFIX=1` old). Result (clone KO runs, 12 with the fixes): eye never NaN, scene drawn; **the static is only partly gone** (2 of 6 runs still had 3-13 s of noise, the NaN there sits on the enemy's transform and is regenerated each frame after our step; the audio path was not traced). Debug aids: `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_NANWATCH=1` (+ `_NANARM=<s>` watch on the player's lock block +0x40), `CAMDBG` now prints `[CAMNAN]`. Not reproduced with the reporter's real Jecht / Tidus pairing.
- **Other points:** NO CHASE SLOW (section "Human called in: slow motion ends at the first hit") covers the chase slow-down for everybody; "chase ends after one hit" not done; lock-on switching, FOV vs reticle, performance not looked at.
- Regression `PSPRECOMP_CLOUD=0 tagteam_test.py --baseline`: PASS (`tt136b/reg`).

### Batch twenty-six (25 Nov, tree ttfps, branch tt-fpsunlock): "Unlocked" frame rate option
- **Change**: Settings > Frame Rate has a last choice, Unlocked (`fps=1000`, `PSPRECOMP_FPS=1000`). In the fight (30 Hz logic running, clock paced) the vblank wait no longer sleeps (`psp_display_set_unlocked`, floor `PSPRECOMP_UNLOCK_MAX`, default 1000 fps); logic stays 30 Hz by the clock, interpolation by phase, 30 Hz pacing uses the measured frame time. Menus / movies / loading keep the normal pacing. Vsync is the user's setting. Online it advertises 240, so the lock-step battle (30 Hz logic for everyone) is unchanged. Opt-out: `PSPRECOMP_UNLOCK=0` (acts as 240). Details: docs/frame-rate.md "Unlocked frame rate".
- **Test**: `battle_test.py run --direct --fps 1000` with `PSPRECOMP_L30_PACE=clock` (the test script otherwise paces by frame count, where Unlocked is plain 240): 30.0 gameplay frames per second at 60, 120 and Unlocked (`[FPS] 30 Hz logic:` log line), drawn 165-250 fps unlocked on the loaded host (`~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttfps/d{60,120,1000}`); `tagteam_test.py --baseline` PASS (`~/dissidia/tt/s2/reg_ttfps`). Two-copy online and devices not run.

- **Regression**: `PSPRECOMP_CLOUD=0 python3 tools/tagteam_test.py --work ~/dissidia/work_ttassist --baseline` PASS (`~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttassist/reg2`).


### Batch twenty-seven (25 Nov): partner banters before the "vs <enemy>" display, retail-like banter camera (tree ttbanter, branch tt-bantercam)
- **Retail's start** (age in 1/60 s ticks of the battle clock, `~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttbanter/old3`): the human slot fighter's pose 1100 (0 - 2.5 s), the enemy's close-up with its line (2.5 - 5.75 s), the human's second pose 1110 (the "vs <enemy>" shot, text 1.6 s later at 7.0 s), the white fade at 8.0 s, fight / HUD at 8.3 s. The partners used to banter after all of it.
- **What does NOT hold the retail intro** (all tried, vs text / fade still came at 7.0 / 8.0 s): the match pause (fighters' dt 0), a global slow-motion channel, the fighters' frame counters, the global frame step (`FRAME_STEP`), swallowing the flow step `FUN_088887A4`. Holding the flow before it starts (`bs+72 == 0`, `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_BANTERPRE=1`, research) shows a white screen (the scene is drawn only once the flow has started). The intro is a set of update tasks of the battle scene task list.
- **Fix.** When the human slot fighter's intro script changes (1100 -> 1110, `intro script .. -> ..` log) the partners are spawned / loaded / started (the party record is readable already) and the scene task list is run like a drawn-only frame (`task_run_hook`, filter (4, 4)) plus the object manager family (0x08841xxx: the fighters' updates, stopped by the match pause except the banter's fighter) and the camera tasks (08B3C41C / 08B3C43C), with `FRAME_STEP` 0 during the pass (the banter's fighter gets the step back in `actor_dt_hook`). So the retail intro stands still (its camera shot, the vs text, the fade), the banters play (one after the other, 2.5 s each), then `banters over` releases the tasks and the retail intro goes on: its 1110 close-up, "vs Lightning", fade, fight. Extras that came in early stay held (AI gate) until both slot fighters' intro scripts are over (`pre_intro_over`: uses BOTH slot fighters, never the local human's slot, which differs per machine - the first version desynced at the first KO). `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_BANTERLATE=1`: old (after the whole intro); `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_BANTERHOLD=0`: partners early but no task hold. No hold = the old fall back too when the human's intro has no second script (partners then come after the intro as before).
- **Camera.** Retail gives a fighter two shots (`PSPRECOMP_INTROCAM_LOG=2` now logs `[INTROPATH]` every update in the fighter's frame): a LOW wide shot (eye 0.3 m up, ~2.4 m away, fov 22 -> 36), then a front close-up (eye ~1.8 m, look-at the face, fov 23) that keeps pushing in. The banter now does that: 1.0 s low wide shot from the front-right (fov 36 -> 32, pulls up slightly), hard cut, 1.5 s close-up from the front with a small side offset (fov 24 -> 22, eye 1.9 -> 1.6 m, rises 1.55 -> 1.85 m). `PSPRECOMP_BANTER_CAMOLD=1`: the old single static shot. Not verified: that the fov write is exactly applied (the close-up frames waist-up to chest, retail's Lightning close-up is similar).
- **Test aids.** `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_AGESHOTS=<dir>:<from s>:<to s>:<step s>` (existing) with `BT_NOPROBE=1` (new, tools/battle_test.py: the harness' HUD probing collides with the runtime's own captures in the intro); `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_FLOWPROBE=1` (party lists at the first flow calls).
- **Verified (host).** 2v2 (`party_battle_walk.txt`, `SP_PARTNER=1 TESTPART=13;30`, `~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttbanter/mid4`, sheet `mid4_a.png`; before: `old3_a.png`): Jecht / Lightning intro to 5.75 s, Vaan banter 6.0 - 8.4, Cloud banter 8.5 - 10.5, then the retail 1110 close-up, "vs Lightning" at 12.0, fade 13.0, HUD / fight. 3v3 (`v3a`, `TAGTEAM_3V3=1 TESTPART=24,13;15,22`): four banters (Squall, Gabranth, Kain, Cloud) then the vs shot. Squall as human (`sq1`, `quick_battle_walk`): two banters, ok. Two copies online (`mp_bn.py mpbn3`, team2, KO of slot 0 at 20 s): `[NETSYNC] frames compared 1778, mismatched 0` on both (the first version, `mpbn1`, desynced at frame 649 = the KO; BANTERLATE baseline `mpbn2` in sync). `tagteam_test.py --baseline` PASS (`reg2`).
- **Not verified:** device / audio (line timing), 3v3 online, FFA, characters whose intro has other script ids, the opening banter with Assist On in online Communications.

### Batch thirty-one (26 Nov): 3v3 extras with the wrong model (Cloud drawn as Gabranth) - second graphics allocator (tree tt3v3m, branch tt-3v3model2)
- **Not a regression of the early banter spawn.** The earlier run's `TESTPART` ids were right (24 Kain, 13 Cloud, 15 Squall, 22 Gabranth; labels came from the same ids). `TESTPART="24,13;15,22"` with the early spawn and with
  `BANTERLATE=1` gave the same result: all four extras had their own `+0x394` entry (Batch seventeen holds), but the 2nd and 4th extra (Gabranth, Cloud) were drawn with another model: lineup of extra 3 showed Gabranth's
  armour and cape in Cloud's place (`~/dissidia/tt/s2/tt3v3m/cl3`, `cl3late`; `cl0` with Cloud as 3rd extra: correct). The Batch seventeen verification never looked at Cloud.
- **Cause.** Gabranth's and Cloud's P_ entry comes back from `FUN_0886D0D8` unfilled (+12 == 0) and is filled by a later call of the same fighter. Each fighter also makes its assist's model object with
  `FUN_0886D2C4(name)` (from `FUN_0884333C`, name 'P_xxx_1P_A'), a SECOND allocator that takes the first entry with +12 == 0 as well. With four fighters made in one frame the assist calls ran in the wrong order: Squall's
  assist took Gabranth's unfilled entry (it was renamed `P_EHT100_1P_A`, found with `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_GFXOBJ=5|6`: `[GFXOBJ]` shows the name and file object per extra, `6` = memory watch on x1's entry name, ring
  `0886D2C4 > 0886DFC0 > 08869CA0`), Gabranth's assist took Cloud's entry. So Gabranth drew Squall's, Cloud drew Gabranth's model.
- **Fix** (`gfxalloc2_hook` on `0x0886D2C4`, `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_GFXCLAIM2_OLD=1`: old): entries `gfxclaim_hook` handed out that are still unfilled stay held (+12 = 1) during the call, except an entry whose name the asked
  name starts with (the owner's own assist object takes it, as in retail where one fighter is made at a time). Log `[GFXCLAIM2]`; with `GFXOBJ=1+` every claim is logged (`[GFXCALL]`, `[GFXCALL2]`: name, return address).
- **Verified (host, `party_battle_walk.txt`, `TAGTEAM_3V3=1 SP_PARTNER=1 TESTPART="24,13;15,22"`, `~/dissidia/tt/s2/tt3v3m`):** after: every extra's entry carries its own name (`f3`, `GFXOBJ=5`), Cloud beside Jecht with his
  own model (`f3.png`), lineup of all four and the banters correct with the early spawn (`fall.png`) and with `BANTERLATE=1` (`flate.png`). 2v2 (`t2n` new, `t2o` old): same entries / names. `tagteam_test.py --baseline` PASS (`~/dissidia/tt/s2/tt3v3m/reg2`).

### Batch twelve (25 Nov): EX Burst of an extra - effects / camera (tree ttexbx, branch tt-exbextra; NOT FIXED, diagnostics only; host-only)
Report: RP6 `desk_logs/rp6_exb_emperor_1125_1455.log` (enemy extra Emperor, `[XREV]` chance 172.68 s, burst 173.21 -> 186.94 s): burst effects missing / camera wrong for a while, worse for extras.
- **What was checked on the host** (headless, `AGESHOTS_WIN` every 0.5 s, `EXBAT` forced bursts and natural bursts with `GAUGESET=extra..:12:10000`, Terra / Emperor as extra, as human slot, as enemy slot, 30 and 120 fps):
  Terra (extraP / extraE / slot) and Emperor (extra / slot) bursts all play: camera on the burster (the camera-slot lend of "EX Burst camera wrong" works, burst ends 9.3 / 13.7 s like the device's 13.7 s), the burst effects of the opening / quicktime / finish phases are drawn.
  The device's lend lines (`+0xFC` cleared, block into camera slot 4) are the same lines the host prints for a working burst.
- **Only visible difference found**: Emperor's burst background (brown swirling scene with black shards, "Absolute Dominion" stage of the burst) is drawn when Emperor is a SLOT fighter (human or CPU,
  on any stage) and is black when he bursts as an extra (first burst of the battle for him; also natural, `n1`). Terra shows no difference. Not a pool / pack / file problem: the file objects (56 model, 198 D_), the effect pack
  and its bound instance (`holder +52`, handle +32 / instance +40) of an extra Emperor are the same as the slot's; no `FUN_088A9DE8` / `FUN_088AA5B8` effect spawn happens during an Emperor burst in either case
  (`EXBFXLOG=2`), so the background is not an effect-table effect. Ruled out by experiment (all still black): linking the D_ record (`FUN_08843F4C`), keeping the extra's own camera words (+0x180..+0x2C0, incl. its own +0x2A0 = 198)
  instead of the slot fighter's, borrowing the slot fighter's camera slot 0 / 1 instead of 4..7, setting the human flag (byte actor +0x5B0 bit 4, set by `FUN_08B2EF44` at battle start for the human's slot fighter only; it is the
  predicate `FUN_08B2EF74` the class step `FUN_08A3624C` tests before creating the scene objects `ctl +0x228` / `+0x24C` via `FUN_08A3DBD0`; with the flag the objects are created but the screen stays black).
  The only data that differ at the burst start: `entry +0xC` = `*(actor +912) +208` (a per-fighter static node: slotH 08B899D8, slotC 08B89A04, extras 08B8A55C / 08B8A588; written by `FUN_08A40684`).
  Next step: find what draws the brown background (not an effect spawn; likely tied to the slot fighters' per-slot set-up of the loading screen, `FUN_08890BB8(bs+1876+40*i, i, char)` / that node) - e.g. a draw-call diff
  of a slot vs extra Emperor burst frame, or a memory-write watch on the burst scene objects.
- **Not the cause (checked)**: `[OVL] resolve 0x08A35E60 / 0x08A3CA48 -> MISSING` during a burst (hundreds of lines): empty virtual methods (`jr ra; nop`) of the burst classes that function discovery missed; they occur for slot bursts too.
- **Natural vs forced**: `EXBAT` bypasses the chance; natural extra bursts on the host (chance -> `0x13` -> burst) behave the same as forced ones.
- **Not reproduced / unverified**: anything specific to the device (Vulkan renderer, 1080p, long battles with rebuilds); effects of the quicktime phase that differ per input.
- **Debug aids added (diagnostics only, no behaviour change)**: `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_EXBFXLOG=1|2` (`[EXBFX]` / `[EXBFXL]`: every effect spawn with id, node owner, ra, result handle; 2 = also outside bursts),
  `EXBENTRIES=1` (`[EXBENT]` the burst controller's 20 per-character entries, `[EXBLB]` lock-block camera words of burster and slot fighters, `[EXBCTX]` per-fighter context nodes), `EXBSTRUCT=1` (`[EXBSTRUCT]` controller scene words 1 s into a burst),
  `EXBBGLOG=1` (`[EXBBG]` the class step's two conditions), `FILEIDS=1` (`[FILEIDS]` file objects with pack handle / instance at a forced burst), `LOADFILELOG=1` (`[LFG]` every file group load with its caller).
  Runner `~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttexbx/run.sh`, montage script `mont.py`, shots `~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttexbx/shots`.

- **Round 2 (25 Nov, same tree; still NOT fixed)**: GE per-draw trace (`PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_EXBDT=<s>:<prims>` arms the `[DT]` trace from the game; histogram by vertex type per display list) shows what the "brown background" is:
  the **stage / sky geometry** (vertex type `00011A`, world scale 540, ~819 prims per frame) is drawn during a slot Emperor burst and **not at all during an extra Emperor burst** (0 prims; it is drawn again outside bursts, 2802 before the burst).
  Per extra character (ENEMY2_CHAR, forced burst at 15 s, prims counted over 3000 prims from 16.5 s): Lightning clone 1603, Bartz 1638, Kain 1638, Terra 1462 = drawn; **Emperor 0, Jecht 0** = not drawn. So it is not "every extra"; Emperor and Jecht bursts lose the stage.
  Same-character slot present (Emperor extra with Emperor as the enemy slot) -> drawn. Effect scripts (`FUN_0887D868`, `[EXBPART]`) are created and return handles in both cases (the particle script index 3 of the package is only created when the human flag
  predicate `FUN_08B2EF74` is true; with the flag it is created but nothing more is drawn). `FUN_08B2EF44` (called once at battle start for the human's slot fighter only) just sets actor +0x5B0 bit 4 and the lock block's shown byte (`FUN_08B3B310`: +0x125).
  Lock-block camera words: a slot block has a camera-player list built at set-up (+0x27C counts 0 -> 5 / 6 players, +0x274 the list, +0x2A0 = the char's D_ file id); an extra's own block has +0x27C = -1 (no list). Keeping the extra's own words instead of the copy, linking the D_ record, borrowing slot 0 / 1,
  the human flag, and the second load stage of the loading screen (info row flag 0x10; not needed for these chars) did not bring the stage back (all tried, removed again).
  Function-entry counts (`PSPRECOMP_PC_TRACE=1` + `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_EXBFC=<s1>:<s2>:<path>` writes `<path>.1/.2`) were too noisy because the compared runs had different characters.
  Next step: compare the draw call itself (which function submits the 819 `00011A` prims: its gating on the camera / lock-block of the shown slot) between a slot and an extra Emperor / Jecht burst with identical characters on the field (e.g. Emperor as enemy slot AND extra), using EXBFC on the same character set.

- **Round 3 (25 Nov, same tree; FIXED - the black burst background of an extra)**. Cause: the burst background is not the stage and not an effect, it is one of three
  **burst sub-stages** of the stage manager (`S = *0x089D6AC8`, slots `S + 320 + 304 * k`, scene object at slot `+116`): `org99.gmo` (k 0, most characters),
  `org98.gmo` (k 1, Emperor's / Jecht's swirl), `org97.gmo` (k 2, Feral Chaos' pink space), all three in `general_archive/field/field.bin`. The burst start
  `FUN_08A3EE44` picks k from the burster's burst record (actor `+1444` = `FUN_088B70C8(char)`; byte 3 != 0 -> 1, byte 0 == 0x20 -> Feral's rule, else 0) and calls
  `FUN_08892F08(S, k)`; while `S + 1232 != -1` the stage draw `FUN_08892584` draws ONLY that sub-stage (`FUN_08895388` -> `FUN_0886ACCC`) and not the stage.
  The loading screen `FUN_08B177FC` (field.bin open only there) loads only the sub-stages the TWO slot fighters' records ask for (its flags at sp+32..34, the names
  at sp+36..44, `FUN_088934E0(data, size, k)` per flag). An extra whose type no slot fighter has bursts in front of an empty sub-stage: nothing is drawn (black).
  So it depends on the characters: Emperor / Jecht extras next to type-0 slot fighters were black, an Emperor slot on the field loaded org98 (drawn), and the
  reverse (two Emperor / Jecht slot fighters, a type-0 extra) or a Feral Chaos extra was black too.
  Found by holding the field fixed (Squall + clone vs Emperor slot + Terra extra / Terra slot + Emperor extra, forced burst at 15 s) and diffing `EXBFC`
  function counts (only the slot run calls `FUN_0886A24C` etc.), then `EXBFN` call logs of the scene draw `FUN_0886ACCC` (a second scene object drawn from
  `FUN_08895388` only in the slot run) and of `FUN_08892F08` (k = 1 in both runs).
- **Fix** (`subst_hook` on `FUN_088934E0`, tagteam.cpp): when the loading screen loads its first sub-stage, the archive is still open (caller's s4 = sp+16), so the
  sub-stages retail will not load (flag 0) and that are still empty are loaded too, with retail's own calls (k 2 with its `FUN_0889991C(0)` / `FUN_0889350C` /
  `FUN_0889991C(-1)` set-up). Tag battles only (`tag_on()`); costs at most two more small files (org99 / org98 82 KB, org97 163 KB). `[EXBSTAGE]` logs each load.
  **`PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_EXBSTAGE_OLD=1`: old behaviour.** Not game-simulation state (drawing only); both copies of an online battle load the same.
- **Tested** (host, headless, `~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttexbx/r3_*`, montages `m3_*.png`; `[DT]` prims of vertex type 00011A over 3000 prims from 16.5 s, burst at 15 s):
  Emperor extra (Squall + clone vs Terra slot + Emperor extra) **1329** (OLD flag: **0**, black, `m3_B6o.png` vs `m3_B6.png` brown swirl); Jecht extra 1638 (`m3_J6.png`);
  Terra extra next to Jecht (human) + Emperor (enemy) slot fighters (org99 loaded by the fix) 1638 (`m3_C6.png`); Feral Chaos extra (org97, k 2 at 17.2 s) 1638
  (`m3_D6.png`, pink); Emperor slot burst unchanged 1320 (before 1267, `m3_A6.png`). No load failures in the logs.
  Two copies online (`mp/m1`, `mp_test.py --menu-mode team2 --fill`, `FILLCHAR=4,20`, `EXBAT=x0:20,x1:45`: Emperor and Jecht extras burst): both copies load the same
  sub-stages, NETSYNC 2379 / 2385 frames compared, 0 mismatched. Regression `tagteam_test.py --baseline` PASS (`reg3`).
- **Debug aids added**: `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_EXBFN=<hex>[,<hex>..]` (up to 4 EBOOT functions: a0, *a0, a0 +144/+148/+296, a1, a2, ra; overlay functions are
  not hookable at install time), `EXBSCN=1` (`[EXBSCN]` the summon scene set-up `FUN_08A02300` / factory `FUN_08A02E88`: per-side summon objects, not the burst),

### Batch thirty (25 Nov): banter captions, banters last until their line is over, banter camera after 10 s (tree ttbanter2, branch tt-bantercam2)
User play-test of Batch twenty: no subtitles on the partners' lines; the last banter ended too quickly.

  `FUN_08B1209C(sub, textId)` (sub = banter ctx + 160) builds it, `FUN_08B122CC(sub, ticks)` arms it, the intro's per-frame step runs `FUN_08B12248(sub)` (state machine, 08B1234C draws / counts down; 08B122E4 stops);
  `FUN_088F47E0(0x16)` > 0 = the game's captions option is off. Found with `PSPRECOMP_FIRSTCALL` phases around the enemy's retail line (3.3 s) and `CALLLOG` (`text 0x509`, 120 ticks).
  The partners' lines never started it (and the retail ctx step is held with the intro), so `sub_start` does the same calls when a banter's line starts and `sub_step` runs the per-frame step from the tick (battle ticks since the last tick, 0 on a drawn-only frame).

- **Banter length.** The line's own length comes from its data: the runtime now exposes the end sample of the ATRAC track the last `sceAtracSetDataAndGetID` made (`psp_atrac_last_end_sample()`, `psp_atrac_set_count()`, same on every machine);
  length = end sample / 44100. A banter lasts until its line is over + 0.8 s (`kBanterMargin`), never less than the 2.5 s pause (`PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_BANTER_PAUSE`); the release of the held intro follows the last banter (it already waited for `g_entrant`).

Measured: Vaan 1.85 s, Cloud 1.0 / 0.7 s, Squall 2.25 s, Gabranth 2.26 s (so most banters stay at 2.5 s; a long line now extends the banter: with `BANTER_PAUSE=0.8` the 2v2 start ends at 9.57 s instead of 8.2 s).
