### Batch thirty-three (25 Nov): banter camera = retail's own intro shots, retail "vs" shot restored, hard cuts (tree ttbanter3, branch tt-bantercam3)
User play-test: the human's "vs" zoom differed from retail, banters 3 / 4 had other zoom / distance, and the camera drifted off between banters.
- **Cause 1 (vs zoom).** The free camera hold (`g_arm_ticks`, 600 ticks after the battle start) took over the retail "vs" shot because the banters had moved the intro past 600 ticks: the hold camera replaced
  the shot's eye / target and kept the fov at 50 (`[INTROPATH]` after the release: fov 50.0 constant, eye moving on its own, against retail's 49.5 -> 20 zoom). The arming now counts from the battle start minus the ticks the
  partners' banters held the intro (`dissidia_tagteam_intro_delay()`). Checked: after the release the shot is retail's (`p2`: eye fwd 3.34 / fov 50 -> 20 in 30 ticks, push to 1.4, swing out, same numbers as retail `p0`), contact sheets `p6_V.png` (ours) / `p0_V.png` (retail) every 0.1 s: wide stand, zoom in, "vs Lightning", swing, fade at the same offsets.
  The bantercam2 tweak that let banter shots run under the hold camera is reverted (`PSPRECOMP_BANTER_HOLDCAM_OLD` gone).
- **Cause 2 (banter shots were hand-made, and their fov never reached the screen).** Writing the fov into the camera object (`mgr + 0xC0`) at SetEye changes nothing on screen: the game builds its projection before SetEye (a test with fov 12 and 60 gave the same picture). So no banter close-up before
  this batch was ever narrower than the game's 50 degrees. The banter shot's fov is now applied as a view-only focal scale on every perspective projection (`ge_set_fov_scale(k)` in psp_ge_viewport.cpp, k = tan(game fov / 2) / tan(wanted / 2), reset to 1 when the shot is over).
- **Retail's shots.** Measured with `PSPRECOMP_INTROCAM_LOG=2` (`[INTROPATH]` per update: eye / look-at in the fighter's frame, fov, ra 08B3D1A4 = the camera manager update FUN_08B3CA24 calls SetEye for every shot: the shots are per-slot camera modes on the lock blocks with the intro camera data; not reusable for a late extra without re-running that machinery).
  The enemy slot fighter's two shots (Lightning, identical in the Jecht and the Squall intros: `p0`, `q0`): E1 = low wide from his right (eye 1.73 in front / 1.7 right / 0.28 up, look-at 1.35 -> 1.08 in front, 0.91 right, 0.76 -> 0.68 up, fov 36) for 122 ticks, then E2 = front close-up (eye 1.78 -> 1.71 in front, 0.1 right, 1.04 up, look-at 0.81 in front, -0.05, 1.27 -> 1.29, fov 23.1) for the rest (retail: 36 ticks).
  Every banter now plays exactly these numbers (key-frame table in `entr_frame`), relative to the banter fighter's facing, from the banter's own start tick (`g_dissidia_entr_t0`; before, `since` was derived from the end tick and went wrong for banters made longer by their line). Per-character data (retail's human shots differ in height between Jecht and Squall) is not available for late extras: the table is one character's. Side-by-side: retail enemy shot `p0_E.png` vs the same character as a partner `p6_B1.png` (`TESTPART=31;31`).
- **Cuts.** The banter shot has weight 1 from its first tick to its last (no ease in / out, no chain blending from the last shot): the cut between two banters, and back to retail's shot, is a hard cut. 3v3 sheets `t3_a.png` / `t3_b.png` (every 0.1 s): Squall E1 / E2, hard cut to the next fighter's E1, ... one frame (10.53 s in `p6`) after the last banter still shows the frozen retail camera before its first update of the "vs" shot.
- **Verified (host).** Two copies online (`mp_bn.py mp1`, team2, KO at 20 s): `frames compared 1616 / 1615, mismatched 0`, both print `banters over` at 12.07 s. `tagteam_test.py --baseline` PASS (`reg_cam3`). Not seen on a device. Test aid: `PSPRECOMP_BANTER_FOVTEST=<deg>` forces the banter fov.
- **Not done:** per-character shots (needs the lock block / camera data machinery for late extras); the 3v3 late-extra model mix-up noted in Batch twenty-one.

### Batch thirty-four (25 Nov, tree tthpboth, branch tt-hpboth): one HP attack that hits two fighters hurts each of them
- **User decision**: when ONE HP attack registers on two (or more) fighters at once, every fighter hit takes the HP damage, not only the attacker's aimed foe (`[HITFOE]`, 20 Nov, kept the foe and dropped the rest).
- **Change** (`tagteam.cpp`): `hitreg_hook` keeps the old primary victim (the foe when it is among them) and now also records the other victims of the same attack in the same frame (`g_hits2`, `hit_add2` / `hit_secondaries`).
  `hpstep_hook` is a wrapper around the old body (`hpstep_core`): after the step for the primary victim it runs the HP step once more for every other victim (`[HPBOTH]`), each time with the attacker's BRV restored to the value at the hit,
  so every victim takes the full BRV as damage (retail's rule for one victim); the attacker's BRV is spent once (0 afterwards, as with one victim). Each step has its own damage number (`[HPDMG]`, tag HUD), KO handling (hold / KO mark /
  kill camera) and ledger entry. Same code in 2v2, 3v3, FFA and PvE (friendly victims were never registered, `FRIENDLYBLOCK`; fighters with no HP left are `DEADHIT`). Battle state only (no local state): lock-step safe.
  `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_HPAIMONLY=1`: old behaviour (one victim per HP step).
- **Wrong victim with two attackers at once (user correction, video 1f311989: Jecht was hit by Tifa's BRV move, Cloud's HP move hit Tidus, Jecht lost the HP)**: NOT reproduced as a booking fault (below). Hardening: an HP step whose attacker has no
  hit registered in the last 2 frames fell back to the module's default victim (the attacker's foe, here Jecht); it now uses the attacker's last registered hit up to 8 frames old (`[HPLATE]`, `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_NOHPLATE=1` old). Seen once in the
  two-copy run (identical victim, no change). The cause of the video stays open (needs `HITREGLOG=1 HITAUDIT=1` from a device run).
- **Test aids**: `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_HPM_B="<att2>:<vic2>:<action>:<s>"` (+ `_HPM_BDZ` distance, default 8 m) starts a second, independent attack in each matrix window (indices as `_HPM_ALSO`; `[HPMB]`): e.g. `_HPMATRIX=10089 _HPM_PAIRS=3 _HPM_NODOWN=1 _HPM_VBRV0=1 _HPM_B=0:1:10000:0.3`.
- **Tests** (`~/dissidia/tt/s2/tthpboth`, `run.sh NAME SECS "ENV"`): HP attack on two fighters (`_HPMATRIX=10089 _HPM_SWEEP=2 _HPM_ALSO=3 _HPM_NODOWN=1 _HPM_VBRV0=1`, extraP -> slotC with extraE beside): `s_old` (`HPAIMONLY=1`) slotC 9321 -> 6321, extraE untouched;
  `s_new` at 19.03 s: `[HPBOTH]`, slotC 9684 -> 6684 and extraE 9684 -> 6684 (`[HPDMG]` -3000 each), attacker BRV 3000 -> 0 once; again at 23.70 s (-3084 each). Single-victim hits unchanged (`b7`: `[HPBRV]` 3000 on the one victim, no `[HPBOTH]`).
  Two-attacker windows (`b1`..`b7`, `_HPM_B`): each HP hit went to the fighter it registered on; no mis-booking seen. Two copies (`mp1`, `mp_take.py`, team 2v2, KO at 60 s, 100 s): NETSYNC 2993 frames, 0 mismatched on both.
  Regression `PSPRECOMP_CLOUD=0 tagteam_test.py --baseline`: PASS (`reg_hpboth.215202`). Not run: a played 3v3 / FFA multi-victim hit, a lethal second victim, devices.

### Batch thirty-five (25 Nov, tree ttlockind, branch tt-lockind): lock-on indicator (user: "some kind of indicator or effect for when someone locks on to you")
- **What.** View only, nothing in the battle changes (online determinism untouched; the HUD tick reads actors, never writes). Every HUD tick `lockind_update` (tagteam.cpp) lists the living enemies of the player's panel fighter (`hud_panel_fighter`, same as the overhead bars) whose target `+0x2FC` (through `ao8_body_of`) is that fighter and hands them to `tagteam_hud_lockind` (tagteam_hud.cpp). Drawn on the game layer: a pulsing red-orange V chevron over the player's head with "xN" when more than one enemy has him (2v2, 3v3, FFA 3/4, PvE alike: it reads the targets the score AI / retail / the human's own lock set), a faint ring on the floor, and an eye icon (almond, red iris) over each locking enemy, above its overhead bar (offset by overhead style 0..3); an enemy off the screen sideways gets its eye at the screen edge. A newly locked enemy (absent > 30 HUD ticks, so AI re-picks do not flicker it) pops its eye with a short bloom and the player's ring flashes for 0.5 s. All positions are projected with the matrices of the game's last 3D draw (`tagteam_fx_project`), so they follow Settings > Field of View.
- **Option / flags.** Settings > Debug > Tag Team > "Lock-On Indicator" (default on, saved as `tagteam_lockind` in settings.ini, Reset All turns it on). `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_LOCKIND_OFF=1` = off. `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_LOCKIND_SND=1` = a soft cue (the menu cursor sound, `0x088D4BF4` id 1) on a new lock-on; off by default, only run headless (no crash, audibility not checked). Test aids: `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_LOCKIND_FORCE=<mask>` (bit k = k-th foe shown as locked on), `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_LOCKIND_DBG=1` (green cross at each locking foe's body centre, to compare with the retail reticle); `[LOCKIND]` lines with `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_LOG=1`.
- **Reticle vs FOV (issue #136, "FOV puts the lock-on reticle in the wrong place").** Looked at, nothing changed: `camera.cpp apply_fov` already tells the GE the focal ratio (`ge_draw_set_hud_follow_scale`) and the ring is moved about the screen centre. With `PSPRECOMP_FOV=40` (game 50 deg -> 90) the ring without that move sat ~2.1x too far from the screen centre (`d40off`), with it the ring is on the fighter within a few px (`d40on`, `d0` at FOV 0 for comparison; `~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttlockind`). A remaining difference is a ring ~10-20 px above the body-centre cross at +40 (the ring's anchor is higher than 0.9 m, not measured). Not reproduced as a clear bug on the host; the reported case (device, other FOV, 120 fps interpolation, ultrawide) is not covered.
- **Tests (host, `~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttlockind`, `go.sh`, window shots `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_AGESHOTS_WIN`).** 2v2 (`SP_PARTNER=1 TESTPART=13;30`): both enemies (`f3`, "x2"), one (`f1`), none (`f0`), sheet `scen_2v2.png`; natural targets (`n1`: counts 2, 1, 2, 0 in the log); 3v3 (`v3`, natural x3 / x2) and FFA 4 (`ffa`), sheet `scen_3v3_ffa.png`; FOV +40 and -20 (`scen_fov.png`, eyes over the enemies in both). Two-copy online and devices not run.

### Batch thirty-seven (25 Nov, tree ttchase, branch tt-chaseslow): "chases run at fast forward and still don't work" - slow motion for the chasers only
- **Cause.** The "NO CHASE SLOW" option (default on) forced slow-motion channel 1 to 1.0 for the whole battle (`slowset_hook`). The chase controller (FUN_08AB5xxx) times its states with that slow motion (state 2 = 0.05, states 4 / 5 = 0.133), so at 1.0 the chase itself played as fast forward and broke.
- **How retail slows the actors** (traced with the new `[CHSTEP]` log): the slow-motion manager `*0x08A62280` multiplies its channels (idle 2.0) into the global step `0x089D5EAC`; an actor's step is its clock (+0x3C8) x that step (`FUN_08838300`, `actor_dt_hook`). In a retail chase the chaser's clock is raised (15 at 0.133, 40 at 0.05: it runs at normal speed), the chased fighter and everybody else run at the slow step.
- **Fix.** The retail slow motion is left alone. `actor_dt_hook` multiplies the step of every actor that does not belong to the chase (not the two fighters of the chase controller, their assist / call actor, or an actor whose master chain +0x1108 reaches them) by `other / G`, where `other` = 2 x the product of the OTHER channels (so it is what the actor would have had without the chase, channel 1 = 0.05 / 0.133 -> x40 / x15) and G the current global step (it is copied a frame late, so the ratio is taken against the real value, not assumed). `cam_dt_hook` does the same for the camera when this machine's local fighter is not in the chase; the chasers' camera keeps retail's look. Battle state only (chase controller, channel values, the host's option via `noslow_now()`): identical on every machine. Code: `chase_other_scale`, `dissidia_tt_chase_actor_scale` / `_cam_scale` (tagteam.cpp), hooks in framerate.cpp.
- **Option.** Lobby row now "CHASE SLOW": "Chasers only" (default, stored value 1 as before) / "Everyone (retail)" (0: the whole battle slows as in retail). Env: `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_CHASESLOW=1` retail (everyone), `=0` chasers only, `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_CHASESLOW_FORCE1=1` the old forced-1.0 behaviour (with the option on).
- **Not slowed down for the others**: effects / HUD / timers that read the global step directly (the battle clock, particle effects) still slow with the chase; only actors (fighters, assists, shots by master) and the camera of an outside viewer are compensated. (Fixed in "Batch forty-six".)
- **Test aids.** `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_CHASESTEPLOG=1` (`[CHSTEP]`: every fighter's step, clock, channel 1, controller state while a chase runs, IN / out of it); `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_FORCECHASE=slot0|slot1` (absolute attacker, same on every machine) + `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_FORCECHASE_FOE=slot0|slot1` (with `_NOGATE=1`, `_AT=<s>,<s>`).
- **Tested** (headless 2v2, `~/dissidia/tt/s2/chase_run.sh`: forced chase of the human by the enemy partner, the other pair fights with its AI): `s2_chn5` (new) vs `s2_chr5` (`CHASESLOW=1`, retail): in-chase fighters 0.133 / 0.05 (chaser at clock-raised 2.0) in both; outside fighters 2.0 in `chn5` against 0.133 / 0.05 in retail mode; state timeline (2 -> 4 -> 5 -> 7 -> 8) has the retail frame timing (s5 -> s7 0.333 s, s7 -> s8 0.067 s in both). Screenshot sheets `s2_chn6_sheet.png` (new) / `s2_chr6_sheet.png`. Two copies (`~/dissidia/tt/s2/chmp_out/mp1`, 2v2 online with fill, forced slot0 <-> slot1 chases at 20 / 32 / 41.6 s while the extras fight): NETSYNC 2070 / 2078 frames, 0 mismatched; the [CHSTEP] histograms of A and B are identical.
- **Not verified:** a device; a chase started by a real input (forced chases were used); effects started by the others during the chase still run at the slow step.

### Batch thirty-eight (25 Nov, tree ttlockind, branch tt-lockind2): overhead UI from the fighter's top, not in the intro, no floor ring, new-lock screen pulse
User on the merged lock-on indicator: the overhead bar and eye were on Golbez's body; not during banters / intro; why rings of small spheres at the feet; "a screen effect when someone switches targets to you".
- **Anchor.** The old fixed 2.05 m above `+0x80` was low for tall fighters. `fighter_top(actor)` (tagteam.cpp) = highest bone of the model (`*(*(*(A+0x394)+0x0C)+0x0C)`, 256-byte records, matrix at +0x80, translation y at +0x34, live bones) read while the fighter stands idle (script 1 / 2) and cached per actor + model, +0.2 m, clamped 1..9 m; 2.05 until read. Measured (`[LOCKIND] top of`): Shantotto 1.00, Onion Knight 1.47, Lightning 1.70, Jecht 1.88, Exdeath 2.43, Golbez 3.19, Chaos 4.35. Used by the overhead bars (styles 1/2), the eye (+ chevron over the player: top + 0.3), the floating HP number (`hit_floating`) and the PPSSPP overhead panels (style 3, `npanel::update`: top + 0.05, was `OH_HEAD_Y` 2.1). `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_OVERHEAD_FIXED=1` = the old fixed height. Other drawing at a fighter (entrance effect column / ring, `tagteam_fx.cpp`) is an effect on the body, not UI above the head, and was left.
- **Not in the intro.** `intro_done()` (latched per battle): false while `g_pre_hold`, the opening banter queue / banter entrant, until `pre_intro_over()` first holds. Until then no overhead bars / eye / chevron / pulse, no style-3 panels, and the side fighter panels are hidden too (`tagteam_hud_set_intro`; the reserve strip stays). `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_OVERHEAD_INTRO=1` = old (shown in the intro).
- **Floor ring removed** (and its new-lock flash on the floor): the dots under the player's feet. The chevron + "xN" and the eyes stay.
- **Screen pulse.** A new lock-on (30-tick debounce) draws red-orange edge gradients (sides 58 px, top / bottom 35 px) for 0.45 s (0.65 s and stronger when 2+ enemies have the player), brighter on the side the enemy is on (left / right by its screen x, bottom when behind the camera). View only, off with the Lock-On Indicator option, `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_LOCKFX_OFF=1`, `_LOCKFX_SLOW=N` = N times longer (test aid), `[LOCKFX]` log lines.
- **Tests** (`~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttlockind`, FORCE targets): `a1` (Golbez + Lightning vs Jecht, `a1_golbez.png`: bar + eye above Golbez's head), `a2` (3v3 Onion / Shantotto vs Golbez / Exdeath: banters show nothing overhead, `a2_s1.png`; fight `a2_s3.png`), `c1` (Chaos, Exdeath), `c2` (Onion Knight, Shantotto), pulse `p1_s.png` (_SLOW=1000: full-strength edge tint). Not verified: audio, devices, whether top is right in unusual idle poses (flying idle).

## PC setup: mouse clicks did nothing (26 Nov, tree ttsetui, branch tt-setupui)
Cause: psprecomp/setup/setup_main.cpp only handled touch (SDL_FINGER*) events; desktop SDL delivers mouse events, which the wizard never read, so clicks only
"worked" by luck (a window manager / touch-emulating device) - keyboard / pad were the real inputs. Fix: SDL_MOUSEMOTION / BUTTONDOWN / WHEEL handled
(`App::mouse_event`): hover moves the highlighted row and shows the hand cursor (SDL_SYSTEM_CURSOR_HAND; arrow over disabled / info lines), ONE left click acts at
once (on press, same hit-test as touch: row, +/- arrows, Back / Close button), right click = back, wheel moves the selection, SDL_HINT_MOUSE_FOCUS_CLICKTHROUGH
so the focusing click also acts. The on-screen keyboard (Report text, typed path) is clickable too (new `KeyboardDialog::pointer`). Note SDL already maps mouse
event coordinates into the renderer's logical 960x544 space (any window size / HiDPI scale), so they are used as is. Tested under Xvfb + openbox with xdotool
at 960x544 and 640x360. Keyboard / pad paths unchanged.

### Batch thirty-nine (26 Nov, tree ttexrev, branch tt-exrevenge): EX Revenge slow motion that is never given back (4+ fighters)
- **Retail EX Revenge** (not the EX Burst "chance" of rounds 5 / 6, which is slow-motion channel 2 and the per-fighter EX manager FUN_08ACB208): `EX_REVENGE_MANAGER` = a singleton at `*0x08ACA350` (+0 / +32 enable bytes, +8 state: -1 idle / 0 running, +12 timer, +16 OWNER = the fighter who revenges, +28 effect handle). Start `FUN_08AC997C(mgr, fighter)` (from the fighter update FUN_08B3526C: EX button pressed while being hit, then `FUN_08ACA66C` = EX Mode) sets **slow-motion channel 5 to 0.12** (0.002 x 2 x 30), raises the owner's clock, flags owner `+0x5B6` bit 0x10 / the target's 0x20. The per-frame update `FUN_08AC9D7C` counts the timer with the owner's own step and ends it through `FUN_08AC9034` (releases channel 5, restores 0x089D4920 / camera words, clears the flags, mgr +8 = -1). A legit revenge runs 3.1-5.2 s of battle ticks.
- **Cause of the stuck slow motion.** Both the update and the end bail out WITHOUT ending when the owner is gone (owner pointer 0, or its component check FUN_0883739C fails: swapped out / rebuilt / unloaded), so the manager stays "running" for ever and channel 5 stays at 0.12 (everybody at 1/17 speed). Reproduced with the test aid `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_REVENGE_GONE=21` (owner pointer zeroed 1 s into a revenge): `ttexrev/i1` (old, `NOEXREV=1 NOSLOWWATCH=1`) channel 5 0.12 to the end of the run. A real swap / KO of the owner did not reproduce it on the host in 8 tries (`d*`, `e*`, `f*`, `g*`: the KO flow ends the revenge first); the retail code only has one owner slot, so with 4+ fighters a second revenge also overwrote the first owner (flags / clock left behind). The #136 watchdog did not know channel 5 was a revenge: it could cut a legit one that ran 5 s (`d1`: `[SLOWWATCH]` at exactly 25.00 s) and does nothing when a call / burst / chase is "running".
- **Fix** (`tagteam.cpp`, `exrev_*`): `exrev_start_hook` on FUN_08AC997C: a start while another revenge runs first ends the running one with retail's end; `exrev_guard()` (every frame, battle state only, same on every machine) ends a running revenge whose owner is not a fighter of the battle any more / holds another character / the battle restarted / runs past `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_EXREVLEN` ticks (default 480): retail's end when the owner is valid, else by hand (channel 5 released, globals restored, effect killed, flags cleared, manager idle). `slow_watchdog` leaves channel 5 alone while a revenge runs (the guard owns it) and still frees a stuck channel 5 after 5 s when no revenge runs. Log `[EXREV]`. **Opt-out `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_NOEXREV=1`** (old behaviour, watchdog included as before).
- **Test aids.** `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_REVENGE=<role>:<s>[:f],...` (roles slotH / slotC / extraP / extraE, absolute slot0 / slot1 / extra0 / extra1; `:f` forces a start while one runs), `_REVENGE_GONE=<s>`, `_REVLOG=1` (`[EXREV]` manager changes + stale-flag check when idle).
- **Tested** (headless 2v2, `~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttexrev/run.sh`): plain revenge (`b1`: ch5 0.12 for 3.1 s, then idle); owner KO'd / HP 0, slot and extra, same / different characters (`c*`-`g*`, ends cleanly); three overlapping revenges slotC -> extraE -> slotH (`j1`: each earlier one ended with retail's end, last ended 27.03); revenge + EX Burst + forced call (`j3`); owner pointer lost (`i1` stuck, `i2` ended by hand at 21.00 s). Two copies online (`mp_out/m1`, 2v2 + fill, absolute-role revenges at 40 / 44 / 48 / 56 s): NETSYNC 2650 / 2649 frames, 0 mismatched. Regression `tagteam_test.py --baseline`: PASS (`reg_exrev.004951`; the first run failed only on script-change counts under host load 35).
- **Not verified**: a natural swap / rebuild of the owner leaving the manager stuck (only the vanished-owner state was forced); a revenge pressed by a human; devices.
### Batch 3v3b (26 Nov, tree tt3v3b, branch tt-3v3b): 3v3 leftovers audit, 10-character 3v3 match, the GE "Hit command limit" fault
- **10-character 3v3 on the host** (single player, `party_battle_walk.txt`, `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_3V3=1 SP_PARTNER=1 TESTPART="24,13;15,22" RESERVE_SIDES="9,27;33,18,17" KOLIST_NAT=1 CALLIN_DELAY=4`, KOLIST of
  slot / extra falls, runner `~/dissidia/tt/s2/tt3v3b/run.sh`): `a2` (only slot fighters KO'd, 10 falls, decided at 110 s), `a3` (slot AND extra falls: `extra 09DD9B20 (side 1) is down`, the
  fallen extra's body is taken by the next reserve member `CALLIN: ... takes the body of the fallen char`): every fall books, the mate takes the slot, `side 0 has nobody left: the battle is decided` at 110 s, the group battle tally is
  written from the ledger (10 falls), the teardown runs and the save screens follow; no `Hit command limit`, no `FAILED`, no `HANGDUMP`, no `[CLOUD]` line. Panels: the side stacks (`row[s]++` in `tagteam_layer_frame`) take three per side.
- **Audit of the one-extra-per-side places** (`g_extra[0]` / `[g_nextra-1]` users, `g_nextra == 2` style counts, per-side arrays): the HUD tick, overhead panels, Assist Off call, SELECT swap and KO take-over were done in Batches six / seventeen;
  what is left uses `g_extra[0]` only in debug paths (HPMATRIX, SWAPPROBE, HPSCAN, TESTSTONE) - not changed. `g_extra[10]` holds 4 start extras + 6 call-ins, enough for 10 characters (8 extras). `all_fighters()` caps at 6 living fighters
  (2 slots + 4 extras = the 3v3 maximum); a call-in whose predecessor is not yet `is_down` could be the 7th for a few frames and is left out of those hit / lock lists - not changed (callers size their arrays at 6 / 8, `hit_attackers` adds the
  Assist Off stand-ins up to 8). The tally rows follow the party record's member count (the CPU enemy party of the party-walk has 3 rows, so falls by fielded characters without a row are credited to row 0, `5 of the loser's falls not in the ledger`):
  a test-setup effect; with real 5-member parties every character has a row.
- **The GE fault** (`[GE] Hit command limit (4194304) without END`, 21 Nov 10-player run `~/dissidia/tt/net10m/logs/c1b`, 3 of 10 machines). In that log the order is: slot rebuild of char 31 at 31.6 s, `[GE] DrawSync timeout: 1 lists still pending`,
  `Unknown cmd` lines at pcs inside model display lists (`0x04D8C...` = the model pool, CALLed through the character's list), then the runaway list. `GE_MAX_COMMANDS` (4 Mi commands, `psp_ge.h`) is only a guard for a list without END; it is not
  too small, the list is garbage: the destructor frees the old character's model packets and the constructor reuses that memory while the GE still reads the old list. Two limits let the game go on under a busy GE: `render_queue_draw_sync(0)`
  gave up after 500 ms (written for a lost / stalled list), and `rebuild_begin`'s `render_queue_wait_caught_up(3000)` (added 22 Nov, after that log) after 3 s. A 10-player 3v3 battle is slow (~2 fps on that host: FBO pool overflow, many lists),
  so both limits were reached.
- **Fix** (`runtime/src/psp_render_queue.cpp`): the render thread publishes `g_ge_busy` (inside a list run) and `g_ge_activity` (lists run). `DrawSync(0)` waits in 500 ms slices and gives up only when a slice shows no progress
  (a really stalled list, a lost list) or after 30 s; `render_queue_wait_caught_up` extends its limit the same way (30 s). Retail-size battles never wait longer than before (the queue drains in milliseconds).
  `PSPRECOMP_GE_SYNC_OLD=1` = the old fixed 500 ms / 3 s. Log: `[GE] DrawSync: the GE is still working (N ms), waiting` (first 20).
- **Test aid** `PSPRECOMP_GE_SLOW="<ms>:<every>"` (render thread sleeps <ms> after every <every>-th list; `PSPRECOMP_GE_SLOW_FILE=<path>` = only while that file exists, so the loading is not slowed): the 10-character match with
  `800:40` and `3500:25`: old behaviour 42 `DrawSync timeout` lines, one `rebuild ... gave up waiting (3 s) for the GE`; new: 0 timeouts, the waits are logged as `still working` (`s_old` / `h_old` / `h_new` in the work folder).
  **Not reproduced**: no `Unknown cmd` beyond the one that every run has at start (`0xFF` at 0x098A....), no `Hit command limit`, with or without the fix, even with `9000:25` (`j_old`), because the rebuild's wait already finds the GE caught up
  (its lists are stalled waiting for the game thread) - the fault needs a list that is still unstalled at the destructor, which needs the 10-machine load. So the fix is by the log's order of events and the measured valve, not by a before / after of the fault.
- **Still open**: the 10-player rig on real machines (`~/dissidia/tt/net10m/runcase.sh TAG 3v3`) to confirm no `Hit command limit`; other frees of model / effect memory are not behind a GE wait (the departed character's unload, the leftover unload) - they
  rely on DrawSync(0) at the frame end, which now holds.
- **Regression**: `PSPRECOMP_CLOUD=0 python3 tools/tagteam_test.py --work ~/dissidia/work_tt3v3b --baseline` (`~/dissidia/tt/s2/tt3v3b/reg1`): PASS (all checks, with and without the tag team).

Played on after the page: same partners spawned and started. Regression `PSPRECOMP_CLOUD=0 tagteam_test.py --baseline`: PASS (`~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttvs/reg_vs`). No Google Drive sync lines.

### Batch forty-seven (26 Nov, tree ttfftal, branch tt-ffatally): own Free-for-all result screen, every fighter's own tag-in
- **Tag-ins (cause + fix).** Free-for-all had no tag-ins of its own: the fallen extra of a CPU was replaced from the TEAM reserve (game side 0's reserve = the human's party remainder: P3 falling brought in Laguna, the human's tag-in; log
  `CALLIN: LAGUNA takes the body of the fallen char 9`), a fallen CPU slot fighter (P2) was swapped for the extra of its side or held down, and the human's fall ended the battle. Now (single player with the players screen's set-up, `ffa_sp_tags`, helpers next to `dissidia_tagteam_ffa_char_look` in tagteam.cpp):
  every fighter has his own tag-in (P1: the party's second member, P2..P4: the TAG-IN column, None = no tag-in, Random resolved once per battle to a loadable character on no pick / not on stage); P2 and the human: slot call-in of his own tag-in 3.2 s after the fall (`g_ffa_slot_tag`), P3 / P4: the extra call-in (`g_downrec` loop) with the tag-in instead of the team reserve; a fighter with a tag-in pending is "still fighting" in `ffa_keep` (the battle is decided only when nobody has a tag-in left or in flight, `ffa_entrance_inflight`); a fallen slot fighter with a tag-in is no longer replaced by a fighter of his game side. Players are told apart by CHARACTER (`g_ffa_owner`, made from the positions when all fighters stand), because the KO flow moves bodies between slots. LOOK / outfit: the tag-in is loaded with `info_for_char`, which already gives the LOOK entry of any pick incl. the TAG-IN field (seen: `file 550 = P_FIV100_3P` for a CPU main, Laguna's `P_EHT110_3P` GFXCLAIM for a tag-in; CPU mains Alt 2 in the same runs). `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_FFA_TAGIN_OLD=1`: old behaviour. Seen (`~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttfftal/r3`, `r10`): KOLIST partner:10 / enemy2:20 / slot1:30 then the same again: `P3's tag-in TERRA comes in`, `P4's LIGHTNING`, `slot 1 (P2) fell: his tag-in KAIN comes into the slot`, every second fall decides (`side 1 has nobody left`); human KO at 15 s: `LAGUNA` into his slot (`r5`), second KO decides the defeat.
- **Own result screen** (`tagteam_result.cpp`, `tagteam_result.h`; data from tagteam.cpp `ffa_result_build` at `group_decided`). Not bent into retail's Tournament round result any more (the old row writing, `ffa_result_tick`, stays behind `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_FFA_RESULT_OLD=1`). It is drawn on the game layer from the retail result scene's own parts, read from the disc: brown swirl ground (`menu_pk_party_battle_result_gim_0` entry 2), the ornate 1st..4th, medals, glowing digits and Lv numerals (entry 0), VICTORY! / DEFEATED... (`menu/en/menu_lpk_party_battle_result_gim_0` entry 1), the menus' faces, party-colour bands. Per fighter in placing order: placing, face (+ the tag-in who came in), name, Lv, who (You / CPU / player name), outfit (Normal / Alt 1 / Alt 2 / DLC, single player picks), KOs scored (KO ledger, counts up), HP damage dealt (counts up), the faces of those he knocked out, "KO'd by" face; a header "<winner> wins", the banner by whether this machine's player won. Placing: those still in when it was decided first (KOs, damage, HP left), the fallen after by the time of their last fall. The ledger now books same-game-side hits in a Free-for-all and leaves an unknown killer unknown. Shown when the retail result scene is up (menu overlay: win, and online) or the retail end-of-battle list (battle overlay: the single player defeat); it covers retail's screen (opaque base: the swirl is partly transparent) and swallows the pad; Cross runs the counting out, then leaves (white fade, the player's Cross is handed to retail's screen under it until the way back to the players screen takes over).
  **Cues** (found with `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_SELOG=1`, a log of every sound request with its caller): the retail scene plays, per row, menu SE 28, 25, 29 at +0 / +0.47 / +0.93 s (requests 10028 / 10025 / 10029) and the win jingle `400005`, then Cross = SE 1; the scene's requests (callers 0x08B543D0..0x08B57700) are muted while the screen is up and ours play the same ids on our timeline (`[FFARES] cue: sound N`); a defeat has none of the jingle (retail's defeat flow: the defeat BGM + list SEs only); the retail result BGM keeps playing under it.
