### Batch forty-three (26 Nov, tree ttbartz, branch tt-bartzfreeze): the Customization screen froze with the Bartz D1 moves installed

- **Report.** RP6, Bartz > "Check abilities and equipment?" > YES > the tab list, then Cross on Abilities: frozen picture, no more `[FPS]` lines, no pad lines. The log (`rp6_bartz_custom_1123_1056.log`, 9,266 lines) ends with `sceIoLseek(fd=4 ... offset 0x10846800)` and 368 `[atrac3plus] Invalid start bit / Invalid number of transmitted units / Channel unit extension ...` lines (the decoder fed garbage).
- **Cause.** Not the music, not tag team, not the D1 moves themselves. `0x10846800` is the middle of `voice/en/event/up07/up07_103_430ca.at3`, a story voice, not anything the Abilities screen asks for. The screen loads `text/en/mess_pk_customize_ability_0.bin`, which the D1 mod makes bigger (283,344 B, was 281,840), so it is relocated to virtual sectors past the end of PACKAGE.BIN. The user's mods folder also had the 4,282 PNGs of the HD texture pack (`mods/texpacks/recomp-hd/`): `package_mods.cpp` skipped only `textures/`, so each PNG became a NEW package entry and took virtual sectors (and the ones over the index buffer's room were dropped but had already taken theirs). The ability text landed at `0x90846800`, above 2 GiB; the game keeps only 20 bits of a sector, seeks to `0x10846800` (bit 31 lost) and loads a voice file as the text pack. Everything after that is garbage (the ATRAC decoder lines are most likely the music / voice stream chewing on the wrong data; not traced further). It needs both the grown text and a big mods folder: with only the Bartz files the text sits at `0x3E6E3000` and works, which is why it showed up only on the RP6 setup.
- **Reproduced on the host.** Sparse fake PNGs with the sizes from the device log (`mods/texpacks/recomp-hd/*`, 4,281 files, 1.3 GB apparent) next to the Bartz mod folder: same `WARNING: too many NEW entries ... keeping the first 2011 of 4282`, same 2020 overrides, Customization > Bartz > YES > Cross on Abilities gives the same `lseek ... 0x10846800`, a blank screen, `[atrac3plus]` errors after a few seconds, game thread alive but never drawing again (old binary, `~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttbartz/r2`).
- **Fix** (`package_mods.cpp`, `package_mods.h`). (1) `texpacks/` is skipped like `textures/` (never a game path; installed packs are served by name). (2) NEW entries get their virtual sectors after every real override and only when kept (dropped ones no longer take space). (3) `kMaxPackageBytes` = 2 GiB: an override that would not fit below it is skipped (the retail file stays) and a NEW entry is dropped, each with a `[MODS] skip ...` / `dropped NEW entry (no room below 2 GiB ...)` line; the online-pack `add_override` refuses likewise. (4) New log line `[MODS] served files end at package offset N B (the game addresses up to 2147483648 B)` (a `WARNING` instead when over), so the next freeze of this kind shows at the top of the log. `PSPRECOMP_MODS_OLD2GIB=1` = the old layout (texture packs indexed, no limit): reproduces the freeze.
- **Test.** Host unit test `tests/test_package_mods.cpp` (new section: 3 GB of sparse texpacks leave no override, 2.4 GB of NEW entries are cut below 2 GiB while the relocated real override keeps its place) ALL PASSED (build it by hand with `-I runtime/include`, `run_package_mods_test.sh` is stale for the hooks half). Headless game (`tt/s2/ttbartz/*.sh`, driver: start the game with the mods folder, press Cross, Cross, Triangle, Down, Right, Right, Cross, Cross, Cross): with the fix, `r3`: ability text read at `0x3E6E3000`, the Abilities screen, the Offensive Abilities / Bravery / HP lists, then all seven tabs (Abilities, Equipment, Accessories, Summons, Assist, Adjust Level, Shop) open and close, 0 `[atrac3plus]` lines. Bartz mod switched off (`#off#` in `retail_moves.txt`, `r4`): the Customization screen comes up and runs, 0 errors. Only the main menu's Triangle (Customization) entry was driven; the Customization key of the tag menus' Player Select was not tested separately (same screen).
- **Not verified:** on the RP6 itself (the phone's mods folder with the real pack).

### Batch forty-five (26 Nov, tree ttnpause, branch tt-netpause): online pause menu and Forfeit
- **Why**: retail's pause task is never made in an online tag battle (Batch four), so Start did nothing. User decision: Start opens a menu that does NOT pause the game; its purpose is Forfeit.
- **Menu** (tagteam_net.cpp `pause_step`, drawn by tagteam_hud.cpp `pause_menu` in the lobby look: card, navy ribbon, pale / royal-blue bars, the hand): Start opens "PAUSE" with Resume / Forfeit; Forfeit asks "FORFEIT THE MATCH?" with NO (default) / YES. Cross selects, Circle goes back, Start closes. The battle keeps running for everyone. While it is open, and until the buttons held at closing are released, this player's input word is neutral (buttons up, sticks centred) - through the lock-step, so every machine sees the same. Menu state is local view state only.
- **Forfeit**: YES sets frame `g_seq + 30` and sends it as 4 trailing bytes of the input window packet ('TL' v1, older receivers ignore it). Every machine, at that lock-step frame and before the frame's words are delivered, calls `dissidia_tagteam_forfeit_apply` (tagteam.cpp): the player's rows are marked used (nobody comes in for him; `reserve_left` ignores them), every fighter he drives at that frame (slot fighter / extra) is KO'd like the natural KO (KO mark when the side has somebody left, HP 0 otherwise so the retail finish decides), and his streams go to nobody (no more waiting for his input). His own machine leaves at that frame through the F_QUIT path used for a lost peer (back to the menus).
- Opt-out `PSPRECOMP_TTPAUSE_OFF=1` (Start does nothing as before). Logs: `[TTPAUSE]`.
- **Tests** (two copies, LAN, `~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttnpause/np.py`): open + Resume on both machines mid-fight: NETSYNC 2398 frames, 0 mismatched; guest forfeit (f1) and host forfeit (f2): both machines applied it at the same frame (1444 / 628), the forfeiter ends in the main menu (no white screen / hang), the other machine goes to the victory / results flow. Not tested: 3 humans, a side that goes on after the forfeit (the KO-mark path), a device.

### Batch forty-four (26 Nov, tree ttnpause, branch tt-netpause): connection notices (direct / relay) and sturdier hole punching
- Toast per other player of the group (psp_hle_adhoc.cpp `conn_toasts`, once a second): "Connected directly to <name> (LAN, ping N ms)" in LAN mode; in Internet mode "Connected directly to <name> (same network | Internet, ping N ms)" when the relay-introduced punch came up (same network = the path is the reported LAN address), "Playing via relay with <name>: <reason>" with the reason from what happened: no reply from <pub ip:port> in 8 s (NAT/firewall), direct path silent for 3 s (also the mid-match switch, and again "Connected directly" when it returns), direct connections off (`PSPRECOMP_ADHOC_DIRECT=0`), server too old for direct connections (relay version < 2), or no introduction within 25 s.
- Punching: window 6 -> 8 s; after 1.5 s the punches also sweep the ports next to the reported public one (+1..+16, -1..-4, four per 100 ms round: symmetric NATs usually hand out sequential ports; a punch from any port of an introduced player is accepted and becomes the path). LAN address first / both addresses at once, 500 ms keep-alives and the retry every 15 s were already there. IPv6 is not attempted (the protocol carries IPv4 only).
- Test aid `PSPRECOMP_ADHOC_DIRECT_DROP=<s>`: direct packets are ignored from <s> seconds on (0 = all).
- Tested with two copies: LAN (toast with ping), Internet through the local relay (direct up via the LAN address: "same network"), forced failure (8 s reason toast), forced drop mid-session (direct, then "silent for 3 s" via-relay toast). Real NAT success rates cannot be measured on this network (both copies and the desktop share one router); the port sweep is untested against a symmetric NAT.

### Batch forty-six (26 Nov, tree ttcfx, branch tt-chasefx): chase slow motion for the chasers only - the rest of the global-step readers
User: during chases the effects and timers (hit / particle effects of the others, summon / assist timers, the battle clock, EX / assist gauge fill, HUD animations, sounds) still slowed for everybody; only the two chasers' own things should be slow, 1-on-1 exactly retail.
- **Cause.** Batch thirty-seven only compensated the actor step (`FUN_08838300`). 131 other functions (146 sites; found by scanning the generated code for `lui 0x089D / +24236`) read the global step `0x089D5EAC` directly or take it as the `dt` they hand on: the battle main `FUN_0888C048` (it advances the battle clock, `bs + 96`, and runs the finish machine), the battle controller `FUN_08886C88` (side modules, hit handling, EX / assist gauge handlers), the fighters' state machines (`08B37604`, `08B37BCC`, `08851974`, `0880A9E8` ...), the gauge ticks, timers (`08AE0D70`, `08AE0E0C`), the scene / 2D / effect managers (`088A2324`, `088A6028` effect handle, `088A973C`, `08851D30..0885B010`) and so on. All of them ran at 0.05 / 0.133 of normal speed for the whole battle during a chase (measured: the battle clock advanced +0.05 / +0.133 per frame instead of +2.0).
- **Fix** (`tagteam.cpp`, "chasefx" block next to `chase_other_scale`). Those functions are hooked (`kGsAddr`, one template hook per address, installed at battle setup next to the lock hooks, overlay addresses delegate to the menu / extra overlay when the battle overlay is not resident). While a chase runs and the option is on, a call whose subject is not a chaser runs with the global step written to `other` (what the step would be without channel 1, `chase_other_scale`), then the retail value is written back. Subject = the first argument, or its words +0 / +4 / +8 (handlers keep their owner at +8, objects their actor at +0), followed up to three master links (`+0x1108`), compared with the two chasers and their assist actors by address range (`gs_inside_member`, an actor object is 0x1400 bytes); anything inside the chase controller's own memory is a chaser's. A chaser's call nested inside a swapped call gets the retail step back for its duration (`g_gs_depth`, `g_gs_slowG`); `dissidia_tt_chase_actor_scale` returns slow / normal against the live step so an actor's step is the same inside or outside a swap. Effect handles (`088A6028`, `088A62A8`, no owner word): normal step when within 3.5 m of a fighter that is not a chaser (a hit / aura / trail of that fighter), else retail (the chase's own effects: speed lines, camera-bound ones). Battle state only (chase controller, positions, channel values, the host's option): the same on every machine, lock-step safe; nothing runs when `chase_other_scale` is 1 (no chase, option "Everyone (retail)", not a tag battle), so 1-on-1 is untouched. Not hooked on purpose: the cameras, the chase controller, the EX Burst code (hooking them stalled the intro; they keep reading the live step).
- **Opt-out.** `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_CHASEFX_OLD=1` = batch thirty-seven behaviour (only actors compensated). The lobby option "CHASE SLOW: Everyone (retail)" turns the whole thing off as before.
- **Tests / aids.** `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_CHASEFX_RATE=1`: per frame in a slow state, `[CHASEFX] rate t= ch1 clock +<ticks>` (battle clock advance); `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_CHASEFX_LOG=1`: at the end of each chase a table per hooked function (calls | kept retail as a chaser's / run at the normal step / kept retail inside a swapped call | retail step, normal step | calls that advanced the clock) and the first decision for every effect handle (`effect handle ... nearest fighter ... m -> ...`); `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_CHASEFX_PROBE=1` the same table (older probe name). Test: `~/dissidia/tt/s2/chase_run.sh`-style forced chase (`/tmp/cfx_run.sh`: `FORCECHASE=enemy2 FORCECHASE_HUMAN=1 FORCECHASE_AT=10,18`, `CHASESTEPLOG`), headless 2v2.
- **Measured** (`~/dissidia/tt/cfx_ba_old` = `CHASEFX_OLD=1`, `cfx_ba_new`): battle clock per frame in the slow states: old 0.0500 x 22, 0.1333 x 150, new 2.0000 x 70 (all). Fighters (`[CHSTEP]`): chasers in the chase 0.05 / 0.133 (chased) and 2.0 (clock-raised chaser) in both; fighters outside 2.0 in both. Function table (`cfx_new5`): `0888C048` 31 / 31 run at the normal step, effect handle / fighters' machines swapped for the non-chasers and kept retail for the chasers (`08B37604`, `0880A9E8`, `08851974` 50 / 50), gauge handlers kept retail inside for the chasers. State timeline of the chase controller as before (2 -> 4 -> 5 -> 7 -> 8; durations 0.033 / 0.1-0.27 / 0.33-1.0 / 0.067-0.13 s in old and new runs alike; the fights differ from run to run, the AI is not deterministic). Screenshots: `~/dissidia/tt/cfx_before_after.png` (top before, bottom after, 8.4 s - 9.1 s into the second chase; different fights).
- **Not verified / open:** sounds (no function of the sound engine reads the step in the generated code, so they were not slowed by this; not listened to); effects spawned by a non-chaser at more than 3.5 m from every fighter, or by a chaser away from the pair, are classified by position only (an owner word was not found); a hit effect of the others was not produced in the headless runs (the AI of the other pair stood still during the forced chases), only the decision for the chase's own effect handle was logged; 60 / 120 fps logic (`other / G` is exact only with the 30 Hz logic step, as in batch thirty-seven); no device, no online two-copy run beyond the regression.

### Batch forty-eight (26 Nov, tree tt136c, branch tt-issue136c): issue #136 leftovers, the clone KO-swap NaN (camera + static) has a root cause and a fix
- **Root cause of the camera / sound NaN with a clone partner.** Chain, found with the new debug aids below: (1) `swap_slot_with` of two clones is the content exchange (`content_swap_raw`): the actor block and every owned heap block of H and P are exchanged word by word at EQUAL OFFSETS.
  (2) The big owned block (0x9860 bytes, the character's animation data: 83 clips x 48 bytes table + clip data) has a different INTERNAL layout in the two clones: the table struct sits 16 bytes apart (`0CD85B00` = block +0x3320 in H, +0x3310 in P; 5 of 6 swaps, `[CLIPSNAP]`).
  (3) The fighter's graphics entry (`actor +0x394`, 0x13C bytes in the shared graphics pool 0x08C00000, so it "stays with its address") holds the pointer to that table (+12). After the exchange the entry still pointed at the old offset, where the other clone's bytes now were:
  table count 0 / 252, base 0 / FFFFFFFE, clip entries all 0 (`[CLIPSNAP] after`). (4) `FUN_0886B344(anim ctx, id)` computes the clip's playback rate 60 / length * scale: an all-zero entry gives 60/0*0 = NaN (`[CLIPNAN]`), stored as the motion player's end / length
  (`+0x1A0 / +0x1BC`, FFC00000), then root motion and the fighter's position (+0x110..) turn NaN (`[NANWATCH2]`: first writes by the motion setup 0882F4E4 -> 0886B344 -> 089B0F44 / 089B1848, then 089A3868 for the transform), the lock block and the camera copy it, the positional audio reads the same transforms
  (full-scale static). Only the clone path is affected (distinct characters are rebuilt, never content-exchanged), and only when the two animation blocks' layouts differ (most swaps: 4 of the first 6 with the fix showed a 16-byte shift) and the swapped-in fighter then starts a clip through the broken entry (a fighter position NaN in 16 of 64 swaps counted in the old-build logs, `[FIGHTER] pos=nan`, a lower bound: the repair step hides some).
- **Fix** (`tagteam.cpp content_swap_raw`): the graphics entry's pointers INTO the swapped blocks belong to the content: they are exchanged with it, each translated by the usual offset-keeping rule (`[TAGTEAM] swap: graphics entry +C: 0CD86F40 / 0CDBB7C0 -> 0CD86F60 / 0CDBB7A0`), so the table pointer follows the data. No effect when the layouts are equal.
  `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_NOSWAPGFX=1`: old behaviour. The guards (`nan_guard`, `nan_repair_step`) stay as a net but never fire now.
- **Test aids** (all debug, off by default): `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_NANWATCH2=1` arms 13 words per fighter (position, motion player end / length ...) in the runtime's new NaN watch list (`psp_nan_watch_add`, `[NANWATCH2]` = word value + the function-entry ring at the first frame it is NaN; needs NANFIX on, the arming sits in `nan_repair_step`);
  `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_CLIPDBG=1` (`[CLIPNAN]` hook on FUN_0886B344 = the rate NaN with anim ctx / table / neighbouring entries / owner; `[CLIPSNAP]` before / after of the swap: the anim tables of H and P, block pairs with differing words, where the table lies in its pair).
- **Verified (host, clone partner, `KOLIST=slot0:20 KOLIST_NAT=1`, headless)**: old build, clone KO swaps in `~/dissidia/tt/s2/tt136c/{n,w,a..m}*`: 16 of 64 swaps with a NaN fighter position; with the fix 0 of 12 (`p*` and `q*` run with both guards off, `NOCAMNAN=1 NONANFIX=1`, so a NaN could not be hidden; most of them with a shifted table), no `[CLIPNAN]`. PCM dump of a shifted-layout run (`au1`, `tt136c/au1.pcm`, 90 s): no noisy second (flatness > 0.55 with rms > 3000: 0; the old `tt136b/koa.pcm` has 13), no `[NANFIX]` / `[CAMNAN]` line (`tt136c/pcmflat.py`).
- **Issue 3, lock-on switching.** The L cycle was run (`lc60.txt`, an L tap every 2 s, `lcrun.sh`, logs `tt136c/lc*`): 2v2 foe -> other enemy -> foe all the way (lcA, 12 of 12 presses answered when the fighter is free), after a slot KO swap (lcB..lcB7), with the enemy partner KO'd while the lock is on him
  (`PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_TESTLOCKOTHER=<s>` puts the lock on the other enemy at <s>, `KOLIST=enemy2:<s+1>`: the selector goes back to 0 and the foe words are written back within a frame, `lcE3`), with one enemy left (lock / release alternate, as retail), 3v3 (lc3: foe <-> other enemy, no stuck state). **No case where the cycle sticks was found**
  in the L-handling itself. What the traces show (`PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_LOCKTRACE=1`: `[LOCKTRACE]`): the L handler `FUN_08B3AFD4` is called only from the character handler's L release (FUN_08B3526C ...), which is not reached while the fighter is in a state that takes no input; after a KO swap the swapped-in fighter
  sits in such a script (750 / a few seconds idle) and L does nothing for 6 - 18 s, as does every other button (it is the swapped-in partner's state, not the lock cycle). The known real cause of "L never works again" - a LOCK_SET override (+252 != 0) after a rebuild - is fixed in `rebuild_lock` already (see there). Not changed.
- **Issue 2 (video 2, wrong victim for the HP attack).** Tried again with two independent attackers (`HPMATRIX=10089 HPM_PAIRS=6` = slotC -> extraP, `HPM_B=3:0:10000:0.3` = extraE -> the human at the same time, `HITAUDIT=1 HITREGLOG=1`, `tt136c/hb1`, 15 windows): the HP move did not connect in any window
  (the victim's BRV moves, the HP stays; the B attacker's BRV hits land on the human), so there was no HP booking to check; one natural HP hit booked on its victim (`[HPDMG]`). Not reproduced; `[HPLATE]` and the diagnostics stay.
- **Issue 4 (video 1, assist call, Jecht disappears, slow motion forever).** Forced calls (`PSPRECOMP_TTLOCK_FORCECALL=0:14:19:24:30:36:42:48:54:60`, partner Tidus `PARTNER_CHAR=19`, enemy 2 Tifa, `ASSIST=1` and `0`, AI enemies fighting, `tt136c/as1`, `as2`): 18 calls at all kinds of moments, the human is always on stage (position, `[FIGHTER]` lines),
  the slow motion of the calls ends every time (the longest slow stretch in the runs is a chase waiting for the mash, 20 s at 0.05, a different item). "Jecht disappears" not reproduced; the slow-motion watchdog stays.
- **Regression**: `PSPRECOMP_CLOUD=0 python3 tools/tagteam_test.py --work ~/dissidia/work_tt136c --baseline --out ~/dissidia/tt/s2/reg_i136c`: PASS (`~/dissidia/tt/s2/reg_i136c`). Two copies (`mp_slot.py` rig adapted, `~/dissidia/tt/s2/mp_slot_i136c.py`, clone KO at 20 s): NOT run to the end - other sessions' rigs were on the host at the same time and the copies met their peers (ports 9311 / 9312, UDP 27312, `the battle never started`). The change is battle-state-only code run identically on both machines (same swap, same blocks), but a two-copy NETSYNC check is still to do.


### Batch forty-nine (26 Nov, tree ttffsame, branch tt-ffasame): Free-for-all result keyed by fighter, not by character
- **Cause.** The result data of batch forty-seven (`g_ffa_stats`, the KO ledger's `(team, char)` member / last-hit map, `ffa_result_build`) were all keyed by CHARACTER, and the card list came from `dissidia_tagteam_vs_lineup`, whose team 0 is THIS machine's side. Two humans on Lightning were one stats row, the placing tie-break fell to the list order (own card first), and "You" was the first card: each machine put its own player first / as the winner. The header also named only the character.
- **Fix** (`tagteam.cpp`, `tagteam_result.cpp/.h`). Identity = game side + position, the same on every machine (the human's side is not): `ffa_fid_of(actor)` = 0 / 1 slot fighter of game side 0 / 1, 2 / 3 extra of side 0 / 1 (first sight keeps it for the body); `ffa_key_of` = 100 + fid (single player keeps the player's main character as key, unchanged). Every stat is booked on that key: damage (`hp_hit_indicator`), the ledger's fallen fighter (`KoRec.vkey`; the ledger's member inside `ledger_step` / `ledger_hp_hit` is `char + 64 * (1 + fid)` in a Free-for-all, so two fighters on one character, also on one game side, stay two) and his killer (`KoRec.akey`, from `g_last_hp_akey`), alive / HP left. `ffa_result_build` builds the rows from the line-up by (team -> game side, role) in key order (the line-up lists the local side first), so the placing (alive first: KOs, damage, HP left, then the fall time, ties by key, never by character or local order), the winner and the P1..P4 tab (P1 / P2 = slot fighters of game side 0 / 1, P3 / P4 = their extras) are computed from lock-step battle state only. "KO'd by" / victims faces are looked up from the keys. The header reads "LIGHTNING (P1) (you) wins", so two identical names are told apart. `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_FFA_SAMECHAR_OLD=1`: old (character keys, local order). Log: `[FFARES] ... | 1. P1 LIGHTNING <who> ... | you won`.
- **Damage.** Kept as HP damage dealt: retail's own result (the Tournament / party result scene, see `compare_retail_vs_ours.png` in ttfftal) shows no damage figure at all, only placing / level / names, so there is no retail BRV damage to follow.
- **Tested** (2 linked copies, `~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttffasame/mp_same.py`, ports 9561 / 9562, `PSPRECOMP_ADHOC_PORT=27560`, KOLIST `extra0:25,extra1:35,slot1:55`): `s1` both Lightning: A and B both log `1. P1 LIGHTNING ... 2. P2 LIGHTNING ... 3. P4 TIFA 4. P3 WARRIOR OF LIGHT`, A "you won", B "you did not win", the screens agree (`s1_compare.png`: P1 wins on both, "You" is on P1 on A and on P2 on B). `s2old`: the same run with the opt-out (the bug). `s3diff`: different characters. The KO ledger's killer faces were exercised only by code (KOLIST sets HP, so no killer); `[NETSYNC]` untouched (view only). Not verified: 3+ humans, devices.

### Batch fifty (26 Nov, tree ttffbrk, branch tt-ffabreak): FFA, a broken slot fighter hit again by a same-side fighter
- **Report.** User, single-player 4-way FFA on the RP6: "broken multiple times, every BRV hit, no cooldown". Logs `desk_logs/rp6_ffa_break_1126_083*.log`: the human (Kain, game side 0, with extraP) shows assist-gauge -5000 breaks at 44.0, 87.8, 118.7, 181.9 s only. The 54.83 s "BRV 0" of the human is his own HP attack (BRV spent), not a break; the "BREAK" word at that time is extraP's (on the right panel, correct).
- **Likely cause (partly verified).** Retail decides "the victim is already broken" in the damage handler of the attacker's opponent (the other game side's slot fighter). In FFA a same-side attacker (extraP on the human) hits a fighter of its own side, so the check looks at the wrong handler: a BRV hit during the refill (handler state 4) takes BRV and can take it to 0 again, and the reaction runs a new break (state 4 -> 3, new "Bravery Break!", new bonus to the attacker). Seen headless (FFA 4 clones, `HPMATRIX=10000 HPM_ALL=1 HPM_PAIRS=666.. HPM_VBRV=5`, run `r6`): extraP > slotH, slotH state 3 -> 4 at 20.2 s, then 4 -> 3 again at 39.2 s with BRV 0 (BRV 397 -> 120 -> 0 over hits in the refill); the same run with a cross-side attacker (`r3`, slotC > slotH) never re-broke. NOT reproduced in the later clean runs (`o6/w6/x6`: VBRV only on the first window; and `o6b`, old flag): there the same-side path behaved like the cross-side one, so the difference only shows with a fighter at very low BRV in the refill; the exact user sequence is unconfirmed.
- **Guard** (`tagteam.cpp`, `sbreak_guard`, `sbreak_same_side_hit`, `hitreact2_hook`, frame hook after `breakshot_poll`). In a free-for-all, while a SLOT fighter's own handler is in state 3 / 4: (a) the friendly-path reaction (`booked_friendly_slot_handler`) is skipped (`[HITREACT] hit on X during its break: no new break`, no new bonus), (b) a BRV loss in state 4 within 8 frames of a hit by a fighter of its OWN game side is given back and added to the refill (the extras' rule, `xbreak_guard`; log `[BREAKGUARD]`). Cross-side hits stay retail's. State-based only (no clock / random), so lock-step safe; not run two-copy here. `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_FFA_BREAKGUARD_OLD=1` = old.
- **2v2 "broken without being hit"** (`rp6_break_nohit_1126_0845.log` t=171.52): human assist gauge 10000 -> 0 and extraP 750 -> 0 in the same frame. The human's line shows `machine state 0/1`, `+5B6 00` (a break shows `3/0`, `+5B6 04`), so this looks like an assist call (both gauges spent), not a break. Not verified on a device.
- **Test aid.** `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_HPM_VBRV_FIRST=1` applies `_HPM_VBRV` only in the first window. Runs: `~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttffbrk/run.sh NAME SECS "ENV"`.

### Batch fifty-two (26 Nov, tree ttbdsy, branch tt-bandesync): the "early banter" lock-step desync - two view-dependent writes into simulation state
- **How it was found.** The desync check only hashed the two slot fighters, so it saw a split only once it reached them. `PSPRECOMP_NETSYNC_WIDE=1` (both players; diagnostic) adds the
  game's rand() word, both slot fighters' CPU brains and lock blocks (0x600 bytes, +0x124 = the local "shown" byte left out) and, per extra (spawn order), flags / position / script / HP,
  the struct in four hashes, its brain and lock block; it also keeps the last 64 frames of every fighter (struct, brain, lock block) and the camera manager and logs the first mismatching
  frame and the two before it word by word (`[NETDUMPX]`; diff the two logs, e.g. `~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttbdsy/xdiff.py <run dir>`). `PSPRECOMP_NETSYNC_SPAWNDUMP=1`: every extra's
  actor / brain / lock block right after its constructor (`[XCTOR]`) and when it starts (`[XSPAWN]`). `PSPRECOMP_NETSYNC_LBWATCH=<slot>:<hex off>`: a memory watch on that word of the
  slot fighter's lock block (logs the writer's call ring). The runtime's report now also prints, every 150 mismatched frames, which fields still differ (a fixed word or a spreading split).
- **Cause 1: the chase camera step followed THIS machine's player** (Batch thirty-seven). `cam_dt_hook` (framerate.cpp) scales the step of every camera FUN_08B3B4FC runs - the fighters'
  lock blocks, which are simulation state (a fighter's stick is turned into a world direction with its lock block's camera) - by the chase slow-motion compensation when the LOCAL fighter
  is outside the chase. In a chase between a slot fighter and an extra the machine whose player stood outside stepped every lock block camera, the chasing slot fighter's included, x40 /
  x15: dumps of runs `eo3` / `eo7` / `eo8` show the chaser's lock block camera player (+0x1E0) with step +0x280 = 80 against 2 on the other machine and its eye / look-at split in that
  frame (chase state 4); positions followed when that player walked. Slot-vs-slot chases (both players inside) and the forced slot0 <-> slot1 chases of Batch thirty-seven never showed it.
  **Fix:** the compensation follows the camera's owner (lock block +0xF8, a fighter whose own block it is): the camera of a fighter outside the chase runs at normal speed, a chaser's keeps
  retail's look, the same on every machine (`dissidia_tt_chase_cam_scale(cam, ticks)`, tagteam.cpp). `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_CHASECAM_VIEW_OLD=1` = old.
- **Cause 2: HUD portraits made for the local view only.** The big panel shows the enemy this machine's player is locked on to; `portrait_for` made an extra's portrait (sprite + ~17 KB
  picture, from the game's model pool, which also holds the fighters' files) the first time this machine's view needed it. The two pools then differed (`model pool free 20401` /
  `20418 KB` at the next call-in in `fx5`, 19996 / 20013 in `ew2`): the call-in's assist file and motion buffers landed elsewhere and its AI acted differently from its first frame
  (`fx1` / `fx5` / `ec10`: the call-in at 41.7 s attacked at once on the machine on its side, stood on the other; positions split a few seconds later). In runs without the extra portrait
  (`fx2`) both pools stayed equal. **Fix:** every character on the stage gets its portrait as it comes in (spawn, slot rebuild, and a sweep in the slot fighter's tick), from battle state
  only (`portrait_prepare` / `portrait_prepare_all`); the view only picks one. `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_PORTRAIT_LAZY=1` = old.
- **Why it looked like the early banters:** neither cause is in the banter code; both need a slot fighter's chase with an extra / a lock-on to an enemy extra followed by a call-in, which the
  early start (partners fighting from the intro on) made more frequent in the rig's 60 s fights. The late order had 0 of 13 (but its runs only hashed the slot fighters). Ruled out on the way:
  the undo snapshot (the extras' constructor dumps `[XCTOR]` are identical on both machines), the intro hold / waits (lag + jitter 30 + 0..50 ms: 3 of 3 clean), the banter line lengths.
- **Online guard removed:** online runs the early banters again (the `comms_battle()` condition and `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_BANTERNET` are gone); `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_BANTERLATE=1` = the late order.
- **Test aid:** `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_FORCECHASE_FOE=extra<i>` (the i-th extra in spawn order, the same on every machine) besides `slot0` / `slot1`.

- **Tested (host, two copies, `~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttbdsy`, `mp_bn.py` team2 with fill, KO of slot 0 at 20 s, 60 s, early banters online, all with `NETSYNC_WIDE=1`, i.e. stricter than the default check):**
  before the fixes 7 of 19 completed early-mode runs diverged (`ew*`, `eb*`, `ec*`, `eo*`); with only the chase fix 4 of 7 (`fx*`, all the portrait / call-in case); with both fixes
  `fy1`..`fy18`: 15 of 18 with 0 mismatched frames (1693 - 1800 frames each; `fy6` had three slot-fighter-vs-extra chases). The three others: `fy10` 6 frames of one byte of an extra's
  brain (+0x73C, transient), `fy14` one byte of a lock block (+0x444, 0x7F / 0xFF, like the lock-on cursor fade; nothing followed), `fy18` a split at 47.4 s after a "full retail
  finish" at 41.6 s (the KO test aid left the team mate at HP 1; at 47.4 s each machine KO'd its own player: the retail finish path, not the banters; seen once before in `ew1`).
  With the default check (slot fighters only) 17 of 18 are clean. Forced chases slot 0 -> enemy extra 1 at 25 / 30 / 35 s (`chab.sh`): `CHASECAM_VIEW_OLD=1` 2 of 2 diverge
  at the first chase (`co1` frame 817: the chaser's lock block step 80 against 2), new 2 of 2 clean (`cn1` / `cn2`). Every extra portrait is now made on both machines
  (`portrait of char` lines identical in every `fy` run). `tagteam_test.py --baseline`: PASS (`reg_bdsy1`).
- **Open:** the full-retail-finish case above (`fy18`); the lock block +0x444 / +0x584 bytes (probably the lock-on cursor fade of the shown block, not checked); a device.

### Batch fifty-three (26 Nov, tree ttffexb, branch tt-ffaexb): FFA human frozen after a KO with an EX Burst chance, lock-on afterwards
- **Report (RP6, FFA, `desk_logs/rp6_exburst_frozen_1126_0837.log`, `rp6_exburst_nolock_1126_0838.log`, tag-team detail log off).** Human (slotH, char 24) in EX Mode, P2 Lightning broken (t=215.63); the human pressed the burst button at 216.90: the log shows only an assist call (assist gauge -5000, machine state 3, script 10021, the same as every earlier ordinary assist call at 87 / 118 / 181 s), no burst. The human then did nothing for ~22 s (gauges unchanged), `[TTLOCK] slot 1 rebuilt as char 27` (Laguna, P2's tag-in) at 239.8, hit and acting again from 244.4; the user could not lock on.
- **Measured on the host** (FFA through the real menus, `~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttffexb/t3.py` / `t4.py`, new log `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_FROZENLOG=1`: every 0.5 s the human's phase `bs+72`, the finish's decided byte `+0x126B`, lock block `+0x126`, `exb_busy` and why): a normal mid-battle KO of P2 (`KOLIST=slot1:19`) freezes the human with the finish marks (decided byte 1, lock-on byte 0, phase 4) from the KO until "KO flow done" (finish + 3.2 s call-in + rebuild): 9 s (`c2`, `a1`: 19.0 -> 28.1, 31.9 -> 43.1); the marks are put back and lock cycling works on the rebuilt foe (`c3`: L presses at 40 / 42 s cycle slotC / extraE / extraP, `[LOCKMODE]`). With the human in EX Mode (pad R+Square, gauge written) and a burst chance flag (`+0x5B2` bit 0x10) up at the KO (aid `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_EXBFORCE5=0:17`): `exb_busy()` (the KO flow / call-in gate) stayed true through the whole finish phase (`b5` / `b6`: phase 4, decided byte 1, no call-in for 40+ s; the aid re-sets the flag every frame, in the game the 660-tick cut of `exb_busy` limits it to ~11 s: 9 + 11 is about the report's 23 s). The flag is set by the lethal HP hit on the frame the finish starts; the EX manager and retail's per-frame flag clear do not run in phase 4, so nothing ends the chance and our KO flow waits for it.
- **Fix** (battle state / battle ticks only: lock-step safe): (1) `finstart_hook`: at a mid-battle KO every fighter's burst chance flag is cleared (`[EXBKO]`); (2) `exb_busy()` ignores the chance / EX Mode entry part while `bs+72 == 4` (the KO finish; a running burst still counts); `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_EXBKOCHANCE_OLD=1` = old for both; (3) `frozen_fix()`: in the plain fight phase (phase 3, nothing running) a pad-driven slot fighter that keeps the decided byte or the lock block's lock-on-off byte for 3 s gets them back (`[FROZENFIX]`); `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_NOFROZENFIX=1` = off. Test aids: `FROZENLOG=1`, `EXBFORCE5=<slot>:<s>`.
- **Test**: `c2` (fix): KO 19.0, call-in 28.0, marks back 28.13 (same setup before the fix, `b6`: stuck, decided byte 1 at 60 s). `a1` (EXBAT burst on P2 killed by the burst, EX Burst freeze rule): burst 25.0 - 33.97, KO flow done 43.1. Regression `tagteam_test.py --baseline`: see the commit message / report.
- **Not verified**: the natural sequence (the human's HP hit killing P2 in EX Mode, then the button) was not reproduced; in the report's log the press became an assist call, so why the human was frozen that long is inferred from the host runs above, not seen. The RP6 was not in `adb devices` (only the Shield) and no APK was built: no device check. A lock cycle with only one foe left was not run.


### Batch fifty-four (26 Nov, tree ttffbrk, branch tt-ffabreak2): one break rule for every fighter, and a break log that is always on
- **Correction of batch fifty.** The AGAUGE `-5000, machine state 3/0, +5B6 04` lines are an assist call (`[AO8] ... the call is played by partner ...` at the same time), not breaks, so they say nothing about breaks. The user confirms the repeated breaks were real (banner, animation); the cause is still not shown by the logs we have.
- **Break log** (`brk_poll`, `brk_hit_log`, `brk_note_skip`, tag battles, ON by default, `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_BREAKLOG=0` off; independent of `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_LOG`; not limited by the BREAKSHOT shot cap; at most 1500 lines a battle):
  `[BRKEVT] t mode (2v2|3v3|ffa) BREAK|BRV0 victim role:char sN (HUMAN) attacker role:char sN (hit N frames ago) BRV before -> after handler state before -> after already_broken_or_refill 0|1 [REPEAT|SAME-SIDE] {all BRV / HP}` for every fighter (the human too, 2v2 included; `BRV0` = taken to 0 by a hit without the handler's break state);
  `[BRKHIT]` one line per registered hit (at most one per attacker/victim pair per 4 frames) on a fighter at BRV 0 / broken / in the refill; `[BRKEND]` the break is over (state back to 0); `[BRKSKIP]` a reaction the rule dropped; `[BRKHUD]` the break animation (type 2 / 3) started on a big panel with every fighter's handler state at that moment (this is what to read for a break animation nobody caused).
- **General rule** (every mode, `sbreak_guard`, `hitreact2_hook`, frame hook): a slot fighter whose own handler is in state 3 / 4 gets no new break reaction from ANY hit (same side, other side, CPU, human): the redirected (friendly) reaction and the reaction in its own handler are skipped while its BRV is 0; a loss that would take it to 0 in the refill is given back; a same-side loss is given back and added to the refill (as the extras always had). Extras keep `xbreak_guard`. `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_BREAKRULE_OLD=1` (or the older `_FFA_BREAKGUARD_OLD=1`) = old behaviour. Pure state, no clock / random: lock-step safe, not run two-copy.
- **2v2 break nobody caused** (rp6_break_nohit_1126_0845, t=171.52): from that log the human's BRV word was 7543 (not 0) with the assist gauge 10000 -> 0 and the partner (extraP) in script 10100, so what the user saw is not explained by a break of the human's handler. One candidate is covered: a reaction in a slot handler while NO hit registered on that fighter in the last 10 frames but one landed on another fighter (the retail reaction of an enemy hit on the partner arriving in the human's handler, `brk_unhit_reaction`) is dropped when the handler is in state 0 with BRV > 0 (`[BRKSKIP] ... nobody hit`). Not seen in a headless 2v2 (enemy BRV attacks on the partner, `HPM_PAIRS=7`: partner broke, human untouched, no BRKSKIP), so unproven.
- **Tested** (`~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttffbrk/{v1,f1,p7}`, FFA with extraP > slotH repeated BRV hits `HPM_PAIRS=6`, 2v2 natural AI 150 s, 2v2 extraE > extraP): the log lines above, FFA: first break `SAME-SIDE`, later hits `[BRKHIT] ... IN BREAK/REFILL` and `[BRKSKIP] ... friendly-path reaction`, no repeat break; 2v2: the human's only break logged with the attacker. Regression `tagteam_test.py --baseline` PASS (`~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttffbrk/reg2`). Not done: RP6 / device (held by another job), two-copy.

## Kill camera follow-up #4 (26 Nov, tree ttkc5; headless only)
- **EX Burst KO**: the retail finish of a KO taken inside a burst starts at the burst's end (headless `EXBAT=s0:15 KOLIST=slot1:16`: finish 0 ticks after `EX Burst over`), while the fighters are being put back; the user (RP6 26 Nov) had the enemy out of frame. Now a mid-battle finish that starts during / within 2 s after a burst re-aims the camera at the victim 12 ticks later (look-at + program 0x898 as the extra kill camera; `[KOCAM] finish camera re-aimed`). `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_NOEXBKCAIM=1` = off. The exact RP6 case (positions) was not reproduced headless: the repro shows the victim in frame after the re-aim.
- **Lock after the kill cam**: when the KO swap replaced a slot's fighter, `finsnap_restore` skipped the slot ("lock block replaced: left") and the new lock block kept the zeroed +0x126 the finish had left in the old one (no reticle). The slot's saved +0x126 now goes to the new block when it is 0 (`[KOCAM] slot N replaced fighter`; `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_NOREPLRESTORE=1` = off). The target words are not touched (tt-lockfix's). The extra kill camera has no retail finish and clears nothing of the lock.

## Kill camera follow-up #5 (26 Nov, tree ttkc6; headless only)
- User (RP6 / Deck, tag / FFA): two enemies killing each other zoomed the kill camera in on the human. The retail finish camera and the extra kill camera frame the victim / the opposing slot fighter. Now `ko_killer_subject(victim)` (last HP hitter of the victim from the hit book, `g_hp_killer`, fed by `ledger_hp_hit`; lock-stepped data) names the killer when neither killer nor victim is the local human's slot fighter: a mid-battle slot finish re-aims the camera at the killer 12 ticks after the finish start (`[KOCAM] finish camera: killer ...`, `finish camera re-aimed at`), `xkocam_start` uses the killer as look-at / program subject (`extra kill camera frames the killer`). Match-ending finish untouched (retail). `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_NOKILLERCAM=1` = old. Headless: `KOLIST=cpu:25:<partner char>` (HP 0, killer char) with PARTNER_CHAR=3: re-aim at the partner extra. The extra path was not triggered headless (no natural hit KO; code shared). Not verified on a device.

### Batch fifty-five (26 Nov, tree ttmodesel, branch tt-modesel): Mode Select cursor lag
- **Cause** (`~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttmodesel`, `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_MSLOG=1` logs `[MSLAT]`): `modesel_frame` ran from the start menu's sub-list tick and, every frame, rebuilt the full-screen layer in software (`modesel_draw`: background gradients and glows, serif title, five bars, help text, then float -> RGBA conversion, upload). Host cost 18 ms (idle) to 33 ms (loaded machine) per frame, so the menu ticked at 50 ms (20 fps) instead of the game's 33 ms and every press waited for that frame plus its draw; on the phone's CPU this is several times worse. Input itself was read each tick (no debounce, no animation, no file reads); but a held key did not repeat at all (only edges moved the cursor).
- **Fix** (`tagteam_menu.cpp`, `menu_layer.*`, `psp_ge_draw.*`): the baked image of each cursor row (x online x scale) is cached (`bake()` / `publish_baked()`); an unchanged frame only extends the layer's life (`ge_draw_game_layer_touch()`, no raster, no upload; `ge_draw_game_layer_serial()` detects another module's layer), a move publishes the cached image, and the other rows are baked one per idle frame after the screen opens (a press before that bakes synchronously). The frozen redraw after a choice uses the same cache. Held Up/Down repeats like the retail lists (first after 400 ms, then every 100 ms; the real held key, nothing injected). Look unchanged. `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_MSLAG_OLD=1`: old (per-frame raster, no repeat).
- **Measured** (host, one copy, game at 30 fps, `ttmodesel/go.sh`; logs `old/run.log`, `new/run.log`): layer cost per frame 18.0 ms -> 1.1 ms average (0.3 ms on a cursor move; first draws 28 ms while the rows bake); menu tick gap 33 ms in both at this load (50 ms before when a frame took 33 ms); press -> new image published, same tick, 17.7 ms old vs 0.3-0.9 ms new, i.e. the press-to-image delay is now just the wait for the next tick (<= 33 ms at 30 fps, <= 17 ms at 60 fps). Held Down for 2 s: 16 repeats (new), none (old). Not measured on the RP6 (no APK install while other agents had it).


### Batch fifty-six (26 Nov, tree ttlockfix, branch tt-lockfix): lock after a KO, assists as lock target, same-side break misroute, extras' repeat break, lock indicator
- **1. Lock-on after an enemy dies (found, reproduced).** Headless FFA, `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_KOLIST=cpu:25 KOLIST_NAT=1` (the human's locked foe, slotC, KO'd at 25 s): with the old build NOTHING touches the human's lock afterwards (`PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_LOCKGOV_OLD=1`: no `[LOCKCHG]` line after the KO; lock block target, `+0x2FC`, `+0x300` and the camera foe `+0x8B4` all stay on the dead fighter, so facing / attack target / camera are on the corpse until the player cycles). Retail has no answer in FFA. `aim_fix` only fills a ZERO target of a pad-driven fighter and the camera sync only follows a living other-side foe.
- **Fix** (`lock_govern`, `lock_word_bad`, frame hook after `ai_target`): for every pad-driven fighter the lock block's answer, `+0x2FC`, `+0x300` and the override `+252` are checked each frame; a target that is dead / down / off the stage (|x| or |z| >= 1000, y < -20) / an ally in a team battle / an assist actor / a parked Assist Off partner is replaced by the previous valid lock (`g_lockmem`; for a parked partner its assist actor X), else the NEAREST living enemy (retail's own choice is unknown). `+0x2FC`, `+0x300`, the cycle state, the mode handler selector and the local human's camera foe are written together; a bad override is cleared so L / R work (`[LOCKFIX]`). Not during an EX Burst, a chase, a rebuild. Host (`~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttlockfix/k_new` vs `k_old`): KO at 25.00 s -> `[LOCKFIX] ... is bad (dead) -> extraE` and `[LOCKCHG] ... agree 1 ... reason governor` in the same frame, camera moved with it. `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_LOCKGOV_OLD=1` = old.
- **2. Assist actors as the lock target (NOT reproduced).** In 2v2 headless (human locks, calls assists with R+CIRCLE; Assist Normal `n1`, Partner = `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_ASSIST=0` `o1`) the human's lock never moved onto an assist and `[LOCKCHG]` never showed one (the human's lock did not change at all in those runs, so this is weak evidence). Covered instead: the governor treats an assist actor (`+0x542 != 0`) as invalid; an Assist Off stand-in X is valid ONLY when the player's remembered lock is its parked partner (the user's rule: the lock goes to X only if he was locked on the partner and back with it; `ao8_retarget` moves it, the governor is the backstop); the L / R cycle (`other_enemy`, `ffa_others`) no longer offers a parked partner (`lock_parked_hidden`) unless the cycle is on it right now (before, the 2nd candidate was the parked partner's assist actor X). `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_LOCK_PARKED_OLD=1` = old. Open: a retail path that writes an override on an assist (never seen): the next device log shows it in `[LOCKCHG]` (`ASSIST`, `reason`).
- **`[LOCKCHG]` log** (always on, `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_LOCKCHG=0` off, 800 lines a battle): `t who (local human): lock a->b (kind) tgt2FC a->b (kind) foe a->b (kind) cam a->b override a->b mode cyc | agree 0|1 facing-err deg | reason`; kind = foe / ASSIST / standin-assist / DEAD / PARKED / ALLY / none; reason = what our code noted since the last poll (`L-press`, `target-refresh`, `ao8-follow`, `our-lock-mode`, `governor`) or `retail/unknown`.
- **3a. The extras' "REPEAT" breaks were a log artefact.** `brk_poll` read `g_xbroken` AFTER the hit hook had marked the extra in the frame of the break, so a first break printed `already_broken_or_refill 1 REPEAT` (rp6_lock_assist_1126_1354 t=26.11: BRV 210 -> 0 from state 0; t=53.08: 7 -> 0 after a full recovery to 1065 at 40.08 = two real, separate breaks). Now the previous frame's mark / handler state decide.
- **3b. Rule for extras.** `xbreak_guard` also treats an extra whose handler is in state 3 / 4 with BRV below base as broken (marks it, gives hits' BRV loss back) even if no mark exists. `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_XBREAK_STATE_OLD=1` = marks only. Slot fighters: batch fifty-four's rule.
- **4. A same-side hit broke the OPPOSING slot fighter (rp6_chaos_break_1126_1359 t=164.98, "I attack Emperor and Chaos breaks on every hit").** The reaction of a hit on a same-side extra arrives in the handler of the attacker's opponent side (slotC) 1-2 frames BEFORE the hit registers (`[BRKEVT] ... attacker - (hit -1 frames ago) BRV 1030 -> 1030`), so `booked_extra_victim` found nothing and retail's handler broke Chaos. Reproduced headless: FFA, human locked on his same-side extra (`PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_TESTLOCKOTHER=12 PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_TESTLOCKSAME=1`, CIRCLE spam `q_hit.txt`) plus `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_TEST_NOBOOK=1` (the booking misses the hit): old (`BREAK_SAMESIDE_OLD=1`, run `m_old`): Chaos broken at 59.17, 62.17, 64.93 with BRV unchanged, attacker `-`, extraP `BRV0 SAME-SIDE` in the same frame = the user's lines; new (`m_new`): `[BRKSKIP] reaction in slotC's handler routed to extraP (its attacker slotH hit it 1 frames ago, same side)`, only extraP breaks. Fix (`brk_samesideX`, `hitreact2_hook`): a reaction in a slot handler with no registered hit on its owner in 10 frames, while an attacker of the other side hit a fighter of its OWN side (an extra with a handler) within 16 frames and was not aiming at the owner, is booked on that extra (its own handler, the extras' break rules). `hit_attackers` now also lists the called assists (kind 1: the slot fighters' `+0x1108`, the extras' own) so their hits are attributed (`PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_ASSISTHIT_OLD=1` = old list). `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_BREAK_SAMESIDE_OLD=1` = old. Without `TEST_NOBOOK` the natural headless hits were booked right (`s_new` / `s_old`), the user's timing (reaction before registration) is what the aid forces. The user's assist (called 3 s earlier) was not the cause by itself; an assist hitting the same-side extra was not run separately.
- **5. Lock indicator ("who is targeting you") in 2v2** (`lockind_update`): an enemy now counts when its target word `+0x2FC` OR foe word `+0x300` names the player's fighter (or his slot fighter while another is on the big panel). The cause of "only after my partner dies" was NOT found (headless natural 2v2 with the partner alive shows `[LOCKIND] 2 enemies have the player's fighter as target`); the broader read is the attempted fix. `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_LOCKIND_OLD=1` = `+0x2FC` only. Verify on a device.
- **Test aids**: `TESTLOCKSAME=1` (with `TESTLOCKOTHER`), `TEST_NOBOOK=1`. Runs in `~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttlockfix/`. All new code reads battle state only (no clock / RNG): lock-step safe by design, no two-copy run. Not done: device.

### Batch fifty-seven (26 Nov, tree ttffcust, branch tt-ffacust): Customization from the FFA Player Select

- **Cause.** In the Quick Battle app (1-on-1 route) Triangle in Player Select goes state 5 -> 6 with next state 0x32 (50, the Customization app); retail runs Customization and puts the app back at state 5 (the same Player Select) when it closes (state poll: `5 -> 6/32 -> 7 -> 32 -> 33 -> 34 ... -> 5/4`). `qb_frame_hook` treated every next state except 8 / 0xC as "left without a pick" (QB_RETURN), whose trip cover draws white while the app does not tick (it does not tick during Customization) and waits for the list: white over Customization for as long as it ran (reproduced headless: 8 shots of pure white, 255.0 mean).
- **Fix** (`tagteam_menu.cpp`). New mode QB_DETOUR: next states other than 8 / 0xC (pick) and 0x30 / 0x31 (Circle, left) are a detour: nothing of ours draws, the pick goes on when the app is back at state 5 (QB_PICK again). If a detour ends on the list instead, `dissidia_tagteam_ffa_ps_return` takes it as "no pick" (players screen), not the Mode Select. Mode Select / list-confirm hooks fire only once at the start of the trip (the `[MENUSET] mode select: chosen` lines in the Deck log are the trip's own start, not a second firing). `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_FFA_CUSTOLD=1`: old.
- **Test** (`tt/s2/ttffcust/c1.py`, c3.py): old build `old1`: white Customization; new `new1`: Customization shown, Circle back to the same Player Select, Circle again -> players screen (`next state 48`); `new3` (FINAL=pick): Customization, back, pick char 30 -> `YES on char 30 (look 2)` -> players screen with the pick. 2v2 (Mode Select 2 vs 2): retail Party Select has Edit Party (Triangle) and CPU Select has no Customization key, the lobby is ours and ignores Triangle; no Player Select there, unchanged. Not tested on the Deck.

### Batch fifty-eight (26 Nov, tree ttffexb, branch tt-ffaexb2): FFA second KO of a player without a tag-in froze the human for good
- **Report (RP6, `desk_logs/rp6_stuck_chaosko_1126_1403.log`, screenshot `rp6_stuck_chaos_hp0_1126.png`).** FFA, the human kills Chaos (slotC, P2, whose tag-in was used earlier in the match); the death animation plays, Chaos stays on the stage with HP 0000 / BREAK on the panel, the human cannot move or pause; the log's gauges and hits stop (battle clock runs). (The first 20 s freeze at 180.6 s of that log, an extra's KO, is the extra call-in delay `kCallInDelaySec` = 20 s and not a freeze of the input as far as the log shows.)
- **Cause (reproduced, host `~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttffexb/d1`: `KOLIST=slot1:19,slot1:60`, P2 has one tag-in).** The first KO is fine (tag-in, "KO flow done" 9 s later). The second KO has no tag-in left: `[FFA] slot 1 is out; the others fight on` (`g_ffa_down`, the body stays down at HP 0 for the rest of the match) and the retail finish phase (`bs+72 == 4`, human: decided byte 1, lock-on off, no pause) was never put back: the "KO flow done" step (`ko_oneround`) waits for "no slot fighter in a KO state / at HP 0 / swapping", which the held-out fighter never satisfies. `d1`: phase 4 from 60 s to the end of the run (120 s, and the RP6 log 360 s).
- **Fix.** (1) A slot fighter in `g_ffa_down` does not count as "still in a KO" (`PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_NOFFADOWNFIX=1`: old). (2) Watchdog: the finish phase on for more than 900 ticks (15 s) with no call-in / rebuild pending and no burst running ends the KO flow whatever still looks like a KO (`[P4WATCHDOG]`; `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_NOP4WATCHDOG=1`: off). Battle ticks and game state only (lock-step safe).
- **Test.** Same setup with the fix (`d2`): second KO at 60.0 s, "KO flow done" at 65.93 s, human decided byte back to 0, phase 3. `d1` was the first repro (stuck); P2 needs to have no side mate: later runs with a mate took the slot instead. Forced (`CALLIN_DELAY=200 KOLIST=slot1:19,extra0:30,extra1:32,slot1:60`): old (`e1`, both opt-outs) phase 4 stuck from 60 s to the end (80 s+), fix (`e2`) human not frozen. The watchdog alone (`e3`, `NOFFADOWNFIX=1`) was not seen firing (that run ended in phase 6, match decided). Regression `tagteam_test.py --baseline`: PASS (`~/dissidia/tt/s2/reg_ffaexb2`).
- **Not verified**: devices; the extra-KO case (P3 / P4) with no tag-in (not run); why the screenshot shows Chaos "standing" at HP 0 (the defeat hold keeps a held-out body in its fall pose; not looked at on screen).


### Batch fifty-nine (26 Nov, tree ttlockfix, branch tt-lockfix2): the lock governor fought the player (EX core taken for an assist)
- **Regression of batch fifty-five** (rp6_cantswitch_1126_1452): `lock_word_bad` / `lock_kind` took every actor with `+0x542 != 0` for an assist; the EX core is kind 6 (`+0x542 == 6`, see framerate.cpp), retail's own lock target (selector 2), so while the lock block pointed at a core the governor rewrote the lock every ~0.2 s and the L / R switch was overridden. Now: kind 1 only is an assist; any other non-fighter kind (cores, objects) is left to retail; the governor stays away for 1 s after an L / R press (`g_lock_press_t`, set in `lock_mode_hook`); it corrects a given bad target once and, if the same bad word is back, stops for that target and logs `[LOCKFIX] ... the correction did not stick` once.
- Test (`~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttlockfix/c2`): `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_TESTLOCKCORE=<hex core actor>` puts the human's lock block on the core at 30 s (override, then selector 2 from 59.9 s): `[LOCKCHG]` shows `non-fighter` targets, 0 `[LOCKFIX]` lines (the old test would have fired every 0.2 s). The L / R press itself was not run through a pad here. Opt-out of the whole governor: `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_LOCKGOV_OLD=1`.

### Batch sixty (26 Nov, tree ttffstart, branch tt-ffastart): FFA froze on "Starting the battle..."
- User (RP6): single player FFA froze on the start card; the log ended at `[FFA] enemy fighter of round 1` with only `[FPS]` lines after.
- **Cause**: the Mode Select hosted flow starts the FFA battle by an autostart that calls Enter Battle on the setup screen's first tick (`g_ffa_autostart`, waits for `list && !g_dlg_open`). `g_rearm` ("the flow was backed out of: reopen the lobby once the setup screen is back") is set by Circle on the lobby / players screen and is only consumed by the next setup-screen tick. After a normal tag battle + Circle back out of the setup screen, the flag was still set when the FFA start brought the setup screen up: it reopened the players screen over the start (`[TTLOBBY] the setup screen is back after backing out: the lobby again`), whose legacy prefill overwrote P1 with the setup rows (20 / 15 instead of the picks) and the open dialog blocked the autostart. The Quick Battle app sat in state 0x1D (sub 2), waiting for the setup screen's result, under the "Starting the battle..." card, which hides the screen and eats the presses.
- Reproduced with the aid `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_TEST_REARM=1` (flag set and last setup tick 10 s old, as after a back-out): `tt/s2/ttffstart/r4` = frozen card, app state 0x1D sub 2 forever; same flow with the fix `r5` = battle runs.
- **Fix** (tagteam_menu.cpp): starting the FFA battle clears `g_rearm` / `g_lobby_pending` / the dialog; a re-arm or lobby request arriving while a start is under way is dropped; if a dialog is still open when the setup screen is up, the walk closes it. Every walk step is logged: `[FFAWALK] start / state 16 -> 28 / setup screen is up / Enter Battle called / app state change / STALL (every 5 s)`. `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_FFAWALK_OLD=1`: old behaviour.
- Test: single player FFA (t4.py 4 players) with and without the aid; online FFA, two copies over a local relay in `net_mode=internet`, own ports (`mp_ffa.py`): in battle, NETSYNC 1762 frames, 0 mismatched.

### Batch sixty-one (26 Nov, tree ttnoinj, branch tt-noinject): no injected presses left in the tag menus, `[INJECT]` proof line
- **Always-on proof.** `dissidia_tagteam_menu_pad` and `dissidia_training_pad` (framerate.cpp's pad chain) compare the pad before / after: any bit they ADD logs `[INJECT] <filter> adds pad bits XXXX to the player's pad (a -> b): <reason>` (once per change). The default paths log nothing; `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_INJECT_OLD=1` shows the reason of each old injection (seen: `Add CPU: Cross for the setup screen (INJECT_OLD)`). The scripted Party Select / CPU Select pass (FFA_PSOLD / KEEPPARTY / PREOLD only; JOB=ffastart's path) logs `[INJECT] scripted ... pass active` when it starts. Swallow-only filters (Square / Start / Circle / Up / Down blocks, `g_col_fix == 1`, the dialog hold) only remove bits and are not injections.
- **Replaced.**
  - Add CPU (L on a free row, was `g_inject_cross`, a Cross for the screen): `add_cpu_direct` in `setup_tick_hook` runs the screen's own Cross step (found in the generated code, ovl_menu `FUN_08AAEF00` at 0x08AAF010): on the Communications screen (flags `screen + 0x7CC0` bit 1, no pending word) `FUN_08AAA608(screen, +0x7CC8)` must accept (else sound 4 as retail), flags |= 8, M + 4 = 5, the cursor object's +8 / +12 = the screen's +0x7CC4 / +0x7CC8, `FUN_08AAB0B8(screen)` and sound 1; the plain path (single player screen, 0x08AABD1C): sound 1, `FUN_08AA9634(screen)`, M + 4 = 3 and the row animation steps. Not on its list (state 2 / 7) = logged, nothing done.
  - FFA result screen (`tagteam_result.cpp`, stage 2: a Cross pulsed at the retail screen under the fading result screen, ~3 of 10 polls): gone. The fade is 0.45 s, then the retail "Return to Battle Setup" list is visible and the player's own Cross takes it (one more Cross than before).
  - `sp_back_direct` invalid-pointer fallback (`g_inject_circle`): now logs `[TTLOBBY] back from the setup screen: ... nothing done` and does nothing.
  - `g_hop_more` / `g_hop_at` hops: dead code (nothing ever set them), removed.
  - Already behind INJECT_OLD, kept, now logged: round dialog Down, `g_col_fix == 2` Right, `g_inject_late` / `g_inject_circle` replays, Training's `dissidia_training_inject_cross` (menu_settings.cpp only calls it with INJECT_OLD), the script pass.
- **Tested** (host, 30 fps, driver `~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttnoinj/ctl.py` + `mpadd.py`, real menus, screenshots `~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttnoinj/*.png`): Team 2 vs 2 (`f1`: Party Select, CPU Select, lobby, lobby Circle back to CPU Select, lobby again, setup screen, Enter Battle, battle, pause > Forfeit, "Return to Battle Setup", setup screen again), Team 3 vs 3 (`f3`), FFA (`f2`, `f5`: players screen, Player Select open and Circle back, pick, DONE, lobby, lobby Circle, battle, forfeit, result screen, retail list, players screen), Training row (`f4`), Communications Group Battle with two copies (`mp1`: register own character, Add CPU open + Circle cancel, Add CPU + pick = `row 2 (char 30) added as a CPU`): 0 `[INJECT]` lines in all of them. A/B with `INJECT_OLD=1` (`mp_old`): `[INJECT] ... Add CPU: Cross ...` twice, same Player Select. A first FFA run found one more injection (the result screen's Cross: 2 `[INJECT]` lines in `f2`), which is what this batch then removed (`f5`: 0). Regression `tagteam_test.py --baseline`: PASS (`~/dissidia/tt/s2/reg_noinject`).
- Not tested: Android / RP6, Steam Deck, the FFA battle-start script path (still there behind its env flags), Add CPU on the single player screen's plain path (only the Communications path ran).


### Batch sixty-two (26 Nov, tree ttlockfix, branch tt-lockfix3): lost crosshair after both enemies were KO'd (rp6_lostlock_1126_1538)
- **Log reading.** `09D8E420` is the human's OWN partner's assist actor X (Assist Off call, `[AO8] ... the call is played by partner ... own assist 09D8E420`): the call put it in the lock block's override `+252` (correctly cleared by the governor, "an assist is never the target"). At 166.81 / 180.91 the enemies died; at 185.31 `tried[P]` held the bad word of the last fix, so the governor stopped for "the target" and the new fighter was never picked; retail released the lock at the KO and did not lock again.
- **Fix** (`lock_govern`): (a) no valid enemy right now -> wait, nothing is recorded; (b) "did not stick" is keyed on (bad word, replacement) so a newly arrived valid enemy is a new key and is locked on at once; (c) a stale override alone is cleared (at most every 20 ticks, no give-up); (d) if the lock mode dropped to 0 although the player did not press L (retail's release at a KO) and a valid enemy exists, the lock mode goes back to 1 on the remembered / nearest valid enemy (`[LOCKFIX] ... released by retail ... locked on ... again`, at most once per 2 s). The player's L press is recognised by the return address (`lock_mode_hook` called from the L handler FUN_08B3AFD4, 0x08B3AFD4..0x08B3B0B4; before, any lock-mode call counted as a press, which also silenced the governor for 1 s after retail's own release). `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_RELOCK_OLD=1` = no relock (the rest stays); `LOCKGOV_OLD=1` = governor off.
- **Test**: aid `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_TESTRELEASE=<s>` (retail-style release of the human's lock, mode 0, no press): `r_new`: `[TESTRELEASE] ... mode now 0` then `[LOCKFIX] ... released by retail ... locked on slotC again (mode 1)` in the same tick. FFA with `KOLIST=enemy2:24,cpu:30 KOLIST_NAT=1` (`f_new`): lock moved to a valid fighter at the KO. NOT reproduced: the natural sequence (two KOs a few seconds apart with 2v2 tag-ins, Assist Off call before them): the headless 2v2 has no reserves and the retail release did not happen on those KOs (mode stayed 1), so the relock is tested with the aid only; the return-address range of the L handler is inferred (LOCKMODE log of `ra` can confirm: `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_EXBCAM=1`). Not verified on the device.

### Batch sixty-three (26 Nov, tree ttaspos, branch tt-assistpos): Assist Off partner stays where the assist ends; dismissed assists parked
- **User reports (Partner mode).** (1) "Golbez got called as an assist. When it was over, he got sent back to where he was. He should be exactly where the assist is." (2) "Squall called himself as an assist and now it is not disappearing."
- **Cause 1.** Batch nineteen (25 Nov) read the older TODO "the CPU does not come back exactly where it left from" and made `ao8_finish` return the partner body to its departure spot (the round 8 hand-over became opt-in). The user's intent is the opposite: the body is where the assist actor is when the call ends.
- **Fix 1** (`ao8_finish`, `tagteam.cpp`): the hand-over is the default again for every end path. The partner takes the assist actor's position, facing and ground / air state (air: script 102 and falls from there; ground: script 1), is locked on the assist's foe, and fights on as a normal fighter from there (Partner mode parks the body only DURING the call; nothing re-parks it afterwards). A spot off known floor becomes the nearest known floor within 12 m; the assist's height is checked against the stage floor under it (`oob_floor` = `stage_floor_y`): below it is put on the floor, on it means standing. `oob_tick` still fixes a body outside the wall later. Log `[AO8POS] left from (..), assist ends at (..), partner now (..)`. Battle state only, so lock-step safe. `PSPRECOMP_TTCAM_AO8RETURN=1`: the batch nineteen return to the departure spot (`_AO8HANDOVER=1` is now the default; `_AO8BACK=1` still the older PLACE-only return).
- **Report 2, what the log shows** (`~/dissidia/tt/desk_logs/rp6_selfassist_1126_1548.log`). The call at 445.94 was side 1's: caller slotC 09D27750 (the ENEMY CPU slot fighter), its partner extraE 09D5AFA0 had just been rebuilt as char 15 (Squall, 442.1 s, `[XAS] extra ... char 15`). The user's own partner Squall (extraP 09D693F0, char 15, script 700 then) took no part. So no human path was skipped: the human's side (side 0, slotH) never called, and the human-as-assist path (`ao9_call`: human teleported in, slow motion, full control) runs when an extra calls its slot fighter (side 1 did at 252.08 and 379.21). Two Squalls on stage (own partner and the enemy's) look alike. extraP's gauge was 2319 (< 5000) at 445.98: no call of the human was due.
- **Cause / fix 2.** A forced assist actor (the partner's own assist, `xas_spawn(forced)`) stands at (0,0,0) once made (harness: `[AO8] dismissed assist .. was at (0.0,0.0,0.0)` 7.8 s into the battle) and after a call was left only in script 1 where it ended. Now `ao8_park_x` PLACEs a dismissed assist at (5000, y, 5000) like the partner's body on every end path of `ao8_finish` (attack over, hit, caps), and `ao8_tick` parks any idle forced assist (no call running, not in a hit undo) that stands on the stage for 0.5 s. The controller places it again at the next call (three later calls ran as before, attack over after 3.37 s). `PSPRECOMP_TTCAM_AO8XPARK_OLD=1`: old.
- **Test** (host, headless 2v2 clones, `ASSIST=0 TTLOCK_FORCECALL=1:14,1:26,0:34,1:44,0:56`; `~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttaspos/n1`, `n2` new, `o1`, `o2` old flags): `[AO8POS]` shows the partner exactly at the assist's end point, far from its departure; `n2`: assists parked at 7.77 s and after each call, later calls normal. Not tested: an air end of a call, the device, online lock-step (battle state only).


### Batch sixty-four (27 Nov, tree ttdblko, branch tt-doubleko): finish marks left on an extra (invulnerable "ghost"), always-on KO log, KO safety net
- **Report.** RP6 FFA 4-way, single player: "I killed Lightning and Emperor with one HP attack, Emperor still moves and attacks but nobody can hit him"; later "Feral Chaos is in the same state". Device logs `desk_logs/rp6_doubleko_1126_1513.log`, `rp6_doubleko_live_1126_1514.log` (tag-team detail log off), live reads over the debug socket.
- **Live read (RP6, paused).** Emperor (extraP 09D64460): HP 2835 (alive, never at 0), `+0x380 = 20002000`, `+908 = 3` (victory state), decided byte `+0x126B = 1`, lock block `+0x126 = 0`: exactly what retail's finish start (FUN_08B09D88, FUN_08B34E98(fighter, 3)) writes to the fighters it marks. The slot fighters had them put back by `finsnap_restore`; Emperor never did. Feral Chaos: `+0x380 = 20000000` on an alive fighter.
- **Cause (host, `~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttdblko`, new always-on `[KOEVT] finish snapshot / finish start` lines).** The finish start marks the human AND the human's FOE (`+0x2FC`), not "both slot fighters" as the old comment said: `KOLIST=slot1:17` with the human's foe set to extraP (`KOLIST_HFOE=1`): `marked (+380 bit 0x20000000): slotH extraP`, and at `KO flow done` (22.9 s) the old code left extraP at `+380 22000002, +908 2, decided byte 1` (log `h_new`: `[KOFIX] ... carried the finish marks of a slot KO (+380 22000002 -> 02000002 ...)`). In Free-for-all the human's foe is any of the three others, so an extra gets the marks whenever a slot fighter is KO'd while the human targets an extra (natural runs `k_14`, `k_17`, `k_23`: foe extraE every time). A tag-in rebuilt in the marked body (Feral Chaos took the body of the fallen extra) keeps the bit too. Retail never leaves phase 4 mid-battle, so nothing clears it. The marked fighter keeps its AI (moves, attacks) but the decided state makes it ignore hits (inferred from the report: the HP matrix could not show an HP loss on a marked extra in either build, see below).
- **Fix.** (1) `finsnap_take` also snapshots every started extra's decided byte / lock `+0x126`; `finsnap_restore` (KO flow done) puts the marks back on every living extra (`+0x380` bit 0x20000000, `+908` bit 2, decided byte, lock byte) `[KOFIX]`; `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_NOEXTRAFINFIX=1` = old. (2) Net: a living extra (not in the finish phase, a burst, an entrance, a rebuild) that carries `+0x380` bit 0x20000000 for 2 s gets bit, victory state and decided byte cleared `[KOFIX]` (covers the rebuilt tag-in; test aid `MARKX=<extra index>:<s>` puts the marks on an extra: `m_new` cleared after 2.0 s, `m_old` kept them for good, `[MARKXW]` shows the words). (3) Net: a fighter with HP <= 0 that still acts (no fall / landing script, not rebuilding, no burst) for 1 s has the fall asked again and its KO booked (an extra not yet down goes on the down list, a slot fighter's KO flow runs again) `[KOFIX]`. (2)+(3): `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_NOKOFIX=1` = off. Battle state only: lock-step safe.
- **Double KO by one HP attack: not a bug here.** `HPM_ALSO_HP=<n>` (test aid) sets the second victim's HP: slotH's HP attack on slotC + extraP at 300 HP (`NOSURVIVE=1`, `d3`): two `[KOEVT] LETHAL HP hit` lines at 19.03 s (first / further victim), `[HPBOTH]`, extraP `BOOKED ... down` at 19.07 s, slotC `BOOKED slot 1` at 22.53 s after its fall (team mate extraE took the slot), `KO flow done` 22.63 s; with the retail survive effect left on, slotC stays at 1 HP (`d2`). Each fighter is booked by its own path; no fighter was left alive at HP <= 0.
- **Always-on `[KOEVT]` lines** (device logs without the detail log): every lethal HP hit (victim, attacker, HP before / after, first or further victim of the attack), every booking (slot KO flow / extra down), and at each mid-battle finish the snapshot of all fighters' `+0x380 / +908 / decided byte / lock +0x126 / foe` and who carries the marks after the finish start.
- **Not verified.** That bit 0x20000000 / the decided state is what blocks hits (the host matrix gave no HP loss on marked or unmarked extras with the sweep setup, so it is inferred from the live state + report); RP6 / Deck not run with this build; the 1 s HP<=0 net re-issues the fall for fallen extras that stand up before they are parked (seen in `k_17`: script 700/101 on a down extra) - harmless but logged.

### Batch sixty-five (26 Nov, tree ttnowalk, branch tt-nowalk): the Free-for-all battle start is a direct hand-over, not a menu walk
- **User**: "I don't want there to be a menu walk." After our Mode Select / players screen / lobby the single player Free-for-all went on through retail: list confirm > Quick Battle app (state 2 > 16 > forced 28) > the setup screen's own list tick > `g_ffa_autostart` waited for `list && !g_dlg_open` (watchdog, re-arm / lobby-pending guards of Batch sixty) > `sp_enter_battle`; after the battle `sp_draw` counted a 2 s gap on the setup screen's tick to find the way back.
- **What retail does (found this batch)**. The battle start is the Quick Battle app's finaliser `FUN_08A9D72C` (called from its state 0x30 / 0x31 teardown, flag `P + 0x8058` = 1 = "start the battle"): `FUN_08A9BD8C`, the line-up copy `FUN_08AB24B8(P + 0x82E8)` into the battle-setup object `*0x089D8508` (`FUN_0891B8C0` / `FUN_0891B96C`), `FUN_08AA1FA8(app, mode)` + `FUN_08AA2628` (the round tables in the menu globals at `0x09B6EFB0 + 772 + {240 stage, 260 judgement, 280 rules}`, 5 words each, stage -1 = random), then the scene change through the mode table at `0x08AA3F30 + mode * 4` (`FUN_0888964C`). The per-round data reaches `P + 2500 + 5852 * i` from the setup-screen object (`FUN_08AAB5B4` copies the screen's round blocks `screen + 0xA58 + 0x16DC * i`; `FUN_08AAB630` = the cursor row) in state 29's Enter Battle branch (`FUN_08A9B9C0`, `FUN_08AA199C`).
- **Experiments** (aids, removed again): (1) state 16 straight to 48 with `P + 0x8058` = 1, no setup screen at all: **the battle does start** (battle setup, TTVS page with the 4-fighter line-up, still running 8 s later), but with default round data: the menu globals' stage / judgement / rules words stay 0, the rules record in the battle-setup object is empty (the screen builds its UTF-16 name and parameters from the rules index on its ticks), CPU strength tier 0 (group `+0xF24`), level 95 instead of 100, AI tables of the weakest tier. (2) screen built by state 28, `FUN_08A9B9C0` + `FUN_08AA199C` called by hand and state 48 set at the first state-29 frame: same empty globals (the per-round existence words that the real state 29 sets were not there yet). So a start with no retail object needs the rules table (index -> record), the strength tier tables and the round words rebuilt by us: not done (risk: saves / outfits / tag-ins are read from the same records; the walk's output is the reference).
- **What is direct now** (default, `tagteam_menu.cpp`, `qb_frame_hook`): the Mode Select's confirm no longer arms `g_ffa_autostart`; at state 16 the party records are written and the state set to 28 as before; at the FIRST state-29 frame whose screen list is up (`M + 4` = 2) the hook writes the lobby's stage / rules / judgement / CPU strength into the screen's round blocks (`dissidia_tagteam_sp_write_round`) and calls the screen's own Enter Battle step (`sp_enter_battle`): nothing is waited for on a draw tick, no dialog / re-arm / lobby-pending state is consulted, no key is pressed or injected, no cursor is moved, the setup screen is never drawn (the start card covers). `[DIRECTSTART]` logs what was handed over (screen, CPU strength). After the battle the app re-enters state 29: the same hook calls the screen's teardown (`sp_back_direct`) at its first frame and the players screen opens (`[DIRECTBACK]`), with no gap heuristic. `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_MENUWALK_OLD=1`: the old autostart / gap logic.
- **Still touches retail, and why**: (a) the Quick Battle app and the setup screen OBJECT run hidden (states 2 > 16 > 28 > 29 > 30 > 31 > 48 take ~0.6 s + 0.5 s; nothing of them is drawn, the white / start card hides the app's own fades): they build the `P + 2500` round blocks, the rules record, the strength tiers and the menu-globals words the battle reads (experiments above). (b) After the battle the app leaves to the Battle Mode list under the white fade, then our players screen (retail's own way out; the list is the start menu we run over). (c) Team modes (2v2 / 3v3 / PvE), Training and Communications keep retail's user-driven Party Select / CPU Select / Quick Battle (1-on-1) / room screens and Enter Battle; they are screens the player uses, not a background walk, and were not changed. (d) Online Free-for-all starts from the room screens: untouched.
- **Tested** (host, 30 fps, `~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttnowalk/`, drivers `f2.py` / `t5.py`, real menus): FFA start > VS page > battle > pause > Forfeit > result screen > back to the players screen > start again, twice (`n1`: `[DIRECTSTART]` / `[DIRECTBACK]`; between the result screen and the players screen only retail's white fade is on screen); the old walk (`n_old`) for comparison. Same data as the walk: with picks (LOOK Alt 2 for the human, Alt 2 / 3 for the others) the battle block (charIds 30 / 28, looks 3 / 3, models 594 / 586, team structs), the battle-setup object and the menu globals are equal to `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_MENUWALK_OLD=1` except random CPU picks (`p_old` / `p_new`). Two linked copies online (`mp2`): see the report. Regression `PSPRECOMP_CLOUD=0 tagteam_test.py --baseline`: PASS (`~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttnowalk/reg1`).


### Batch: big panel BREAK word follows the shown fighter (26 Nov, tree ttpanel, branch tt-panelbreak)
- **User:** 2v2 single player, RP6: "Terra is showing as broken, but I don't think she is. Her partner was broken, then died, and when it auto-retargeted it must have carried it over."
  Log `desk_logs/rp6_terra_breakhud_1126_1554.log`: extraE (char 5, enemy side) broken at 80.54 s (`[BRKEVT]`), `[BRKHUD] ... break animation (type 2) ... group side 1` at 81.61, extraE KO'd at ~82.57 (`LOCKCHG ... (DEAD)`), lock on to slotC (Terra, never broken, handler state 0) at 82.61.
- **Cause.** With the lock on an extra, the big panel shows the extra and the break word (the break sub-object's UI elements, `FUN_08ADFC84` at break state 4) is let onto it. Only the broken fighter's break end (`FUN_08ADFCC4`) takes it down. An extra KO'd inside its break never gets there, so the word stayed over the next fighter on the panel. `steady_break_sync` / `_reconcile` only look at the steady BREAK byte (number group +35), not at the word elements.
- **Fix** (`tagteam.cpp`, view only): `brkshow_hook` / `brkhide_hook` track per side which break sub's word is up (`g_word_sub`). `break_word_reconcile(side, P)` runs each hud update after `steady_break_reconcile`: word up while the panel fighter's damage handler is not in state 4 -> hidden through the sub that showed it (the owner's own later end is dropped); word not up while the panel fighter IS in state 4 (a slot fighter whose show was kept off while an extra was on the panel) -> shown. Log `[HUDBREAK] ... break word hidden / shown`. Side generic (2v2, 3v3, FFA: every panel in `hudref_hook`). `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_PANELBREAK_WORD_OLD=1` (or `_PANELBREAK_ANY=1`): old.
- **Reproduced / verified headless** (`~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttpanel/run.sh`, party walk 2v2, `TESTLOCKOTHER=8 XHSTATE=enemy2:12:3 KOLIST=enemy2:16 KOLIST_NAT=1 AGESHOTS=<dir>:10:30:1 AGESHOTS_WIN=1`): before (`r1`, `m_old.png`): red "Break" over Lightning's number from 16 s to past 20 s, gone by 24; after (`r2`, `m_new.png`): hidden at 16.00 s (`[HUDBREAK] t=16.00s side 1: break word hidden, the panel shows slotC`), clean at 17, 18, 20 s.
- **Not done:** the one-shot burst animation (type 2/3, `hudanim_hook`) that starts ~1 s after a break is not cut when the panel changes meanwhile; the show path (slot fighter broken while an extra is on the panel, panel returns) and the human's panel with a broken partner are untested (no aid breaks a slot fighter on demand). Regression `tagteam_test.py --baseline`: PASS (`~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttpanel/reg`).
