### Batch sixty-seven (26 Nov, tree tthudsm, branch tt-hudsmooth): HUD marks smooth at 60 / 120 fps
- **Cause.** The layer is drawn every frame, but a fighter's position in guest memory changes only on gameplay frames (30 Hz logic) while the view the
  marks are projected with (`ge_draw_last_view_proj`) is the renderer's frame-interpolated one. Measured (120 fps, frame-count paced, `REC` frames,
  `~/dissidia/tt/s2/hudsm/base120`, `track.py`): the x-step of the lock-on chevron and of an overhead eye was -4.2 -3.8 -4.2 +15.2 px, repeating (a crawl
  back with the camera for 3 frames, a jump on the 4th). Retail's lock-on ring stepped every 3rd-4th frame: `ge_draw_set_hud_fixed_tex` holds 0xC33070 /
  0xC7EA30, but the ring texture is at 0x81D0F0 now (1v1 and tag team alike; hash below), so psp_ge_draw.cpp's 2D follow (IP2D, which moves such a draw with
  the blended fighter) never matched it. (Side effect of the stale address: the ring was not kept on the picture on tall windows or moved by the FOV follow
  scale either.)
- **Fix (view only, no battle state).** (1) `psp_ge_draw.cpp`: `ge_draw_last_view_proj_tag` = (gen, phase) of the display list the last view / projection came from.
  (2) `tagteam_hud.cpp` `tagteam_hud_pos`: a followed actor's feet are recorded per gameplay frame (`dissidia_hud_gen`, framerate.cpp = the interpolation tag's gen of
  the frame that just ran) and blended between the frame before that list's and the list's own by its phase, as the renderer does (>3 m = teleport, no blend;
  `PSPRECOMP_INTERP=0` / `2` as the renderer). Used by the overhead bars, the lock-on eyes and chevron, the entrance FX (`tagteam_fx_frame`). (3) The
  chevron's pulse / bob run on a clock that advances by wall time x the slow-motion rate (product of the channels of `*0x08A62280`, idle 2.0 each; 1.0 in
  normal play), so assist / chase slow motion slows them; normal play is the same speed as before. (4) `framerate.cpp`: `ge_draw_set_hud_fixed_tex_hash` finds
  the ring by content (FNV-1a of 256 bytes, 0xe5465917458e8746), so it moves with the blended fighter (IP2D) and is pinned / FOV-scaled as intended.
  Damage numbers and the screen-edge pulse already ran on wall time; the numbers' camera now follows the same blended view.
- **Flag.** `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_HUDSMOOTH_OLD=1` = the old behaviour (raw positions, wall-clock pulse, ring not matched). `[HUDSMOOTH]` line every 240 frames with
  `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_LOG=1` (gen, slow-motion rate).
- **Test.** `~/dissidia/tt/s2/hudsm/rec_run.py` (tag team, player walks, `REC 120` at 120 fps): before `base120` (chevron dx -4 -4 -4 +15), after `new120` / `new120b`
  (chevron +0.5 .. +3 per frame, every frame; eye jitter 1-2 px from its pulse colour); IP2D lines per frame with `PSPRECOMP_INTERP_TRACE=3` after the ring match
  (0 before). Regression `tagteam_test.py --baseline`: PASS (`~/dissidia/tt/s2/reg_hudsmooth`).
- **Not verified.** On a device; the slow-motion rate in a real chase / assist (rate was 1.000 in play); retail's own rotation animation of the ring is still 30 Hz (only its
  position is blended); the off-screen target pointer texture (0xC7EA30 in the old table) was not located, it stays unblended; vsync-bound frames where the layer and the picture land one frame apart.

### Batch sixty-eight (26 Nov, tree ttferal, branch tt-feralexb): Feral Chaos' EX Burst leaves the stage broken; Free-for-all never freezes the fighters outside a burst
- **Report (RP6, FFA 4-way, lobby "EX Burst freeze", `desk_logs/rp6_feral_exburst_1126_1621.log`):** "Feral Chaos' EX Burst still doesn't work. I can't move. All players should be able to move in this EX Burst, but it should only affect the player who took it." Live read (paused): the victim (the human) floating at (0, 10, 11) in the pink space, script 1, burster in a normal move, no control. Later: the first part of the animation is done on the victim, then "it brings you to a battlefield where you must lower Chaos' BRV".
- **What the lobby rule means.** "EX Burst: freeze" (default) = the fighters outside the burst do nothing until it ends (AI gated, pad dropped, held where the burst put them, as retail hides them); "keep fighting" (`exb_rule_fight`, `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_EXBURST=fight`) = they play on, on the stage. So the user's statement conflicts with "freeze" in Free-for-all; implemented as the user said (below). Team modes (2v2, 3v3) keep the lobby rule.
- **Cause 1 (the report's state).** Feral Chaos' burst has a second part: at 17.2 s the burster's script machine (`0x08A4F454`) sets the stage's sub-stage word `S + 1232` to 2 (org97, the pink space) and the world flag (`FUN_0889991C(0)`, world +528 = 0), and hides the stage object (`FUN_08A500D0(0)`). The burst controller then ends (`+0x278` = 0) on retail's special path (`0x08A3F448` with the burst id 0x2136, burster record byte 6 = 0x13): it skips the `FUN_08892F08(S, -1)` reset (normal bursts: `-1` at the end, seen with `EXBFN`). Nothing else resets it, so after the burst the sub-stage word stays 2 for ever (the stage is not drawn, stage collision off) and the world flag stays 0: nobody can move on the stage (script 2 = run, position unchanged for 30 s; the human restored to the stage still ran in place), the victim stays where the burst scene put it (y 10). Reproduced headless (`EXBAT=x0:15:s0`, Feral Chaos as `ENEMY2_CHAR=32`, FFA 4, human victim: `~/dissidia/tt/fe_old*`, `fe_f*`), also with the lobby rule on `fight`/`freeze`; non-Feral bursts (char 4, 11) reset to -1 at 24.3 s / 27.9 s and everybody moves afterwards (`fe_c4`, `fe_n4`).
- **Fix** (`tagteam.cpp`): (1) `exb_on` / `exb_p0` / `exb_p1` / `exb_field`: after the controller's end, the burst counts as running while the sub-stage word is 2 and the burster still plays a burst script (8000..8999) for at most 1800 ticks, burster / victim read from controller `+0x1C8` / `+0x1CC` (all former `+0x278` / `+0x26C` / `+0x270` reads use them). (2) At the burst's end, if the sub-stage word is still 2: `FUN_08892F08(S, -1)`, `FUN_0889991C(-1)`, `FUN_08A500D0(1)` (the undo of the machine's calls), and the slot fighters of that burst are put back on their spots like the extras in it (`exb_note_in`). `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_EXBFIELD_OLD=1`: old.
  Result (`fe_n2`): the human, victim of Feral Chaos' burst in FFA, is restored at 20.5 s, falls to the floor, runs / attacks / is hit for the rest of the run (x -10 .. +9, z up to 30 m, then -21 .. +23); before the fix it stayed within 0.4 m of one spot.
- **Free-for-all keeps everybody moving** (`exb_ffa_fight()` inside `exb_rule_fight()`): in FFA (`g_ffa`; online the host's roster flag bit 2) the keep-fighting handling always runs, whatever the lobby says: outsiders are put back on the stage, never gated / held, pad not dropped, the park script refused. `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_EXBFFAFREEZE_OLD=1`: the lobby rule decides in FFA too. The keep-fighting hooks are now installed from the battle step when the rule turns on (`exb_fight_hooks_install`), not only at start-up, and `colloff_hook` / `action2_hook` check the rule themselves. Only the two in the burst (burster, victim) take the burst's effect; the end restore puts the victim back.
- **Screen of a player outside a burst** (view only, `stage_draw_hook` on `FUN_08892584`): while that player is outside under the keep-fighting handling the stage draw sees sub-stage word -1, so he sees the normal stage, not org97 / org98 / org99 (`[EXBVIEW]`, screenshots `fe_o2/battle_gl_017.tga`, `_019.tga`: normal stage with fighting at 17.5 and 19 s while Feral Chaos bursts the CPU slot fighter). `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_EXBSTAGEVIEW_OLD=1`: old (sub-stage on every screen).
- **Tests** (host headless, `~/dissidia/tt/s2/feral/run.sh ttferal NAME quick_battle_walk.txt "ENV" walk.txt`, FFA 4 + `CLONES=1 ENEMY2_CHAR=32`): `x0:15:s0` (human victim) old `fe_old*` / `fe_f*` vs new `fe_n1`, `fe_n2`; `x0:15:s1` (CPU victim, human outsider walking at 13 s .. 29 s): human z 9 -> 42 during the burst (16-20 s), `fe_o1`; 2v2 freeze rule (no FFA) `fe_t1`: held fighters back, human restored and moving. Debug aids: `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_EXBCTLLOG=1` (+ `EXBCTLFAST=1`): `[EXBCTL]` controller words, sub-stage word changes, every fighter's position / script. Regression `tagteam_test.py --baseline` PASS (`~/dissidia/tt/s2/feral/reg`).
- **Not verified:** on the RP6 (the retail battlefield part "lower Chaos' BRV" was never reached by the headless runs: the controller ends 3.6 s after the pink space starts and the burster's script leaves 8502 at the same moment, so the interactive part, if any, is not visible in the CPU-burster runs); online lock-step (battle state only, `exb_field` / flags read battle memory and the roster flag), 3v3, other bursters' sub-stages with the view hook.

### Batch sixty-nine (26 Nov, tree ttmenufps, branch tt-menufps): every custom menu at ~10 fps on the Deck
- **Cause** (user, Steam Deck build e86c471: "all the custom menus you made, like Mode Select, are running at 10 fps"): batch fifty-five fixed only the Mode Select. Every other screen built on `menu_layer` (lobby / battle lobby, FFA players screen and picker, Party Select overlays and dialogs, the Free-for-all result, the VS page, the Training overlay and options panel, the Settings start-menu rows, the battle HUD with the online pause menu) cleared and rasterised its whole 960x544 float layer, converted all of it to RGBA and uploaded all of it on every frame, whether or not anything had changed. The game's frame waits for that (it runs on the game thread), so a menu ticks at the layer's cost.
- **Fix** (`menu_layer.*`, `psp_ge_draw.cpp`, call sites only name and tag their layer; look unchanged, no injected presses):
  - **Frame cache.** Every primitive (`band`, `glow`, `image`, `text`, `serif_caps`, `copy`, a screen's own `blend` loops via `note()` / `want_raster()`) folds its parameters into a running hash (bands: rectangle plus the colour at a 9x9 grid, text: string, em, position, colour, images: source address, rectangles, five texels). A layer with `frame_cache` first makes a *dry* pass when its last frame was settled: the draw code runs but nothing is rasterised; same hash as the shown image = only the layer's life is extended (`ge_draw_game_layer_touch`), a hash seen before = the cached finished image is published, a new hash = the next frame is rasterised (one frame after the change). Settled states (the same hash twice) are kept (24 images / 64 MB, least recently used out).
  - **Animated screens** (FFA result: rows, banner, then the pulsing "Cross: Continue"): the running hash after each primitive is compared with the last frame's; from the first primitive that differs, the canvas state before it is snapshotted once, and from then on the unchanged start is skipped (its hashes are checked, a mismatch drops that one frame and backs off) and only the rest is drawn on the restored canvas. The battle HUD does not use this part (`incremental = false`: its first parts move every frame).
  - **Cheaper layer**: only the rows / columns the last frame wrote are cleared and converted (bounding boxes), no per-frame 8 MB clear / allocation, opaque and empty pixels skip the blend divisions, a one-colour band (a dim, a base) has no per-pixel colour call, text widths are cached on the exact inputs (bit for bit the old result). `ge_draw_set_game_layer` compares the new image with the held one and copies / uploads only the differing rectangle (`GL_UNPACK_ROW_LENGTH` sub-image), nothing when identical.
  - **Held direction** repeats (400 ms, then every 100 ms, the retail lists' way) in the battle lobby, the FFA players screen and the pickers (`dir_repeat`, tagteam_menu.cpp); the CPU dialog already had its own left/right repeat. View only: nothing here touches the lock-step.
- **Flags**: `PSPRECOMP_MENUFPS_OLD=1` = old (every frame rasterised, converted and uploaded whole); `PSPRECOMP_MENUFPS_LOG=1` = one line a second per screen (`[MENUFPS] layer:screen ticks/s, rasterised frames (avg / max ms), unchanged, cached, layer cost avg / max, prims / skipped / area / publish ms`); `PSPRECOMP_MENUFPS_VERIFY=1` = test aid, always rasterise and report a frame whose hash matched the last one but whose pixels did not; `PSPRECOMP_MENUFPS_INC_OFF=1` = no incremental frames; `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_MENUREPEAT_OFF=1` = no key repeat.
- **Measured** (host, one copy under `taskset -c 8,9` = 2 cores, game 30 fps, host load average ~13 from other jobs; `~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttmenufps`, scripts `go2.sh` (menus -> FFA players -> lobby -> battle with forced KOs -> result), `go3.sh` (UI states); logs `g_old` = `PSPRECOMP_MENUFPS_OLD=1`, `g_new3` = new, summarised by `summ.py`). Layer cost per frame (begin -> published), old -> new, menu tick rate (calls/s, the game's cap is 30):

  | screen | old | new | ticks/s old -> new |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Settings start-menu rows (title) | 2.7 ms | 0.02 ms | 28 -> 28 |
  | FFA players screen | 34.6 ms | 0.4-0.6 ms (0.07 idle; a change frame is rasterised: 20-30 ms once) | 19 -> 26 |
  | Battle lobby (FFA flow) | 34.9 ms | 0.4 ms | 20 -> 27-29 |
  | Start card / fade to white ("Starting the battle", trip) | 27 ms | 0.7-4.7 ms (a 10 frame fade to white) | 14 -> 16-21 |
  | FFA result (rows, banner, pulsing prompt) | 37.8 ms | 3.0 ms with the intro, 0.4-1.6 ms settled | 18 -> 28 |
  | Battle HUD (hud:battle, every battle frame) | 2.75 ms | 1.3 ms | 28 -> 29 |
  | Training overlay | not measured old | 0.01 ms | 30 |
  | VS page | not measured old (about the size of the result screen) | 0.08 ms | 30 |

  Pixel check (`go3.sh`, 16 UI states: Mode Select moves, FFA players moves, lobby, back) old vs new vs `VERIFY`: max pixel difference 0 in all 16, no VERIFY mismatch. The result screen's 8 consecutive frames change only in the prompt's rectangle (211,259)-(268,264) both old and new (no trails). Regression `tagteam_test.py --baseline`: PASS (`~/dissidia/tt/s2/reg_menufps2`).
- **Not covered / not measured**: the Settings screen proper and its report-issue page are not on `MenuLayer` (psp_settings.cpp renders a `psp_sddialog::Canvas` per frame with its own adaptive interval / scale), the connection notices and toasts are `ge_draw_toast` (a GE text box, no layer): neither was changed. Not live-measured (same code path, no scenario on the host): Party Select overlays / CPU dialog / picker, the Training options panel (the Select panel did not open in the headless Training run), the online pause menu (drawn on the HUD layer, which is measured; its full-screen dim is the one-colour band fast path), sp_setup. Not tried on the Deck / RP6 (the user is testing there).

### Batch fifty-nine (26 Nov, tree ttlockfix, branch tt-lockfix5): is lock block `+0x444` the crosshair's alpha? (rp6_reticle_1126_1650) - investigation, no code change
- **`+0x440` / `+0x444` is a lock-ACQUIRE flourish, not the crosshair's visibility.** In the device log every new lock (L press, 29.48 s, 33.47 s ...) starts it: `+0x440` = a float timer (358.0 -> 0 in steps of 4 per 30 Hz tick) and `+0x444` = a byte that follows it (255 -> 0 in about 2 s); with no lock change both stay 0 (5.44 s, 13.48 s, 35.44 s, 49.88 s). In healthy headless battles (`q2`, `q3`) the byte is 0 while the cyan ring is drawn; so the ring is not drawn from it. The 255 -> 0 ramp at ~60.9 s is the re-acquire flourish after the KO flow restored `+0x126` / pair `+88/+89`, i.e. the cursor coming back, not going away. (Its writer is a generic effect object at lock block `+0x440` (ctor `FUN_08A86C90`, sub-object of the block constructor `FUN_08AB2EF0`); no `sb` of `+0x444` from the block base exists in the generated code, so I did not find the call site.)
- **Retail does draw the ring on a same-side target.** Headless FFA, the human's lock put on his own-side extra (`PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_TESTLOCKOTHER=12 TESTLOCKSAME=1`, screenshot `ls1_34.png` vs the other-side lock): the cyan ring is on the target either way, so "an ally to retail" does not hide it. Writing the finish marks (`+0x380` bit 0x20000000 on the human or the target, `+0x126B` = 1) onto a healthy battle did not remove the ring either (ring pixel counts 10-25 vs baseline 13-20, within the noise; the detector counts near-cyan pixels above the HUD, so this is weak evidence).
- **What the device log does show** (`rp6_reticle_1126_1650`): from 49.84 s (Emperor, extraP, KOs Lightning, slotC; the human's lock is on extraP) to ~60.9 s the lock block has `+0x126` = 0 and pair `+88/+89` = 0 / 0 (the finish marks), mode stays 1 and the lock words are on extraP, nothing for our code to correct (no `[LOCKCHG]` / `[LOCKFIX]` after 47.11 s). The crosshair is therefore absent for about 11 s of the KO flow and flourishes back at 60.9 s. That is the retail finish plus the kill-cam code's restore time (the `[KOCAM]` flow, another session's), not a lock or target problem; a user who pressed Pause or quit inside that window would have seen "gone". NOT proven that it stays gone afterwards: the log ends at ~65 s, the next `[RETICLE]` snapshot (every 20 s) did not come.
- Open / next: a device log that runs on for at least 30 s after the KO, with the `[RETICLE]` snapshots (they include `+0x126`, pair bytes, the camera foe `+8B4` / flag `+8C0`). If `+0x126` or the pair bytes are back to 1 / 1 and the crosshair is still missing, read the camera manager `09AE8C70` live.

### Batch seventy (26 Nov, tree ttlockfix, branch tt-lockfix5): FFA big panel on the 3rd lock target; camera manager `+6D4` after a KO
- **Big panel in FFA** (user: "the main display doesn't switch when I switch to the 3rd target only"): `hud_panel_fighter` followed only an extra of the opposing SLOT's own game side; in FFA the 3rd lock target is the human's own-side extra (a foe under our rules), so the panel stayed on the slot fighter. The paused device state of lostlock2 had `+0x110` / `+0x114` = 1 and `+0x184` = 2. Host writes of those words did not hide the ring (the game rewrote them or they are not the gate). So the `+0x110` / `+0x114` pair stuck at 1 after a finish that LOCK_SETs the human's block (probably the finish camera's look-at at the killer) is the best lead; not proven, not changed. Next: `[RETICLE]` already logs `+0x110` / `+0x114` on change; a device repro with the human's block dumped at the moment the crosshair is missing (`PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_RETICLEDUMP`) would show whether `+0x114` is the only difference.

### Batch seventy-one (26 Nov, tree tthudsm2, branch tt-hudsmooth2): lock-on ring ran ahead and snapped back
- **Cause (batch sixty-five made it visible: before, the ring was not matched at all).** `ge_draw_through_ip` gave every piece of the ring the offset (blended - newest) of the nearest ROOT BONE of
  any skinned draw within 90 px. A fighter has dozens of draws (body, weapon, parts) and there are several fighters: pieces of one ring took different anchors, the choice flipped between
  frames, and a root bone sways with the animation by 10-20 px per tick while the ring (placed by the game on the target's position) does not. Log `[IP2D]` on the host
  (`~/dissidia/tt/s2/hudsm/n5`): the chosen root went 246 -> 263 -> 256 -> 251 -> 237 px while the ring stayed at 259; piece offsets differed by up to 21 px; 121 of 1160 frames had a jump (second difference > 5 px).
- **Fix.** The game module hands the renderer the world position (feet) of the ring's target (the human's lock target, actor +0x2FC) for each gameplay frame and the one before
  (`tagteam_hud_follow_target` -> `ge_draw_set_follow_world`, keyed by the interpolation gen). The renderer's offset is that point projected with the blended camera and blended position minus
  projected with the newest camera and position (the game's own placement): the same offset for all pieces, no bone, sign = blended - newest (no extrapolation; >3 m teleport, > 60 px cut = none). No
  target given (or `PSPRECOMP_HUD_FOLLOW_NEAREST=1`): the old nearest-root behaviour. The chevron / eyes / bars do not share this (they blend positions by the list's phase, `tagteam_hud_pos`).
- **Test.** `rec_run.py` 120 fps, `PSPRECOMP_INTERP_TRACE=3`: piece-offset spread 0.00 (one offset), jump frames 30 of 1647 (was 121 of 1160 / 91 of 1628); the rest are the game's own ring easing (the ring itself moves
  10-20 px in one tick when the target dashes; only that tick's step remains). Regression `tagteam_test.py --baseline` PASS (`~/dissidia/tt/s2/reg_hudsmooth2`).
- **Not verified.** On the device; a target that is an assist body / parked partner (mapped with `ao8_body_of`, not exercised); non-tag 1v1 uses the player's actor.

The per-frame ones keep their own env flags (`PSPRECOMP_FIGHTER_LOG`, `..._FROZENLOG`, `..._EXBCTLLOG`, `..._LOCKTRACE`, `..._CAMX_LOG`). Cap 400 lines per battle (`PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_RETDUMP_MAX=n`, `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_RETDUMP=0` off); the old `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_RETICLEDUMP=<s>` periodic dump still works. Read: diff the `KO flow done` / `+10 s` dumps against a healthy one (mode 1, answer = a foe, +252 0, +0x126 1, `+8B4` = the target); the first dump where `+0x110` / `+0x114` stay 1 shows who set them (match the line before it in `[LOCKEV]`).
  - `[LOCKEV] t= <fn> human's block <L> a1 (role) a2 ra <caller> own|retail | before +252 +0x110 +0x114 mode +0x126 | after ... | phase`: every call of retail's lock-block functions on the HUMAN's block: `LOCK_SET` (FUN_08B3B0B4, writes +252 / +0x114), `MODE3_ENTER_a/b` (FUN_08B3AE14 / 08B3AEB4: save the old mode in +0x110, go to mode 3), and `LOCK_MODE` (FUN_08B3B3EC: `mode old -> new`). `ra` is the caller's return address (retail code, e.g. `08B0A564`) so the function that sets +0x110 / +0x114 during a finish is named; `own` = called while our code is inside a guest call. Cap 300 per battle.
  - `[EVT] t= ...` one line per event, found by diffing every frame (so it works whichever code path caused it): `battle phase a -> b`, `slot k: old -> new` (a rebuild / swap / tag-in), `the human's fighter old -> new`, `fighter appears` / `left the fighter list` (call-in, park), per fighter `<role> <actor> c<char> s<side>: ko 0->1 down 0->1 marks 0->1 frozen(+908 b1) 0->1 parked 0->1 in-EXB 0->1 started 0->1 decided+126B 0->1 char a->b | hp brv script +380 +908 position` (`ko` = HP <= 0 or KO state, `marks` = +380 bit 0x20000000 = the finish marks, `frozen` = +908 bit 1), `EX Burst START / END` with the sub-stage word and the controller's +278, `EX Burst sub-stage word a -> b`, `human control words (held 0.5 s): +380&20000002 +908&2 decided+126B lock+126 pad_driven`, and `human FROZEN?: stick (x,y) held but ... has not moved or changed script for N s: script +380 +908 ... exb_busy (why) finish_busy` (stick held >= 2 s of battle time, phase 3, fighter alive) with `human moves again` when it ends. Cap 900 lines + 150 control lines per battle.
  - `[STATE] t=10.0s phase P human A exb finish extras N cost X ms in C calls | [role actor cCHAR sSIDE (x,y,z) hp brv scr script +380 dec decided-byte lock <role> <target> down parked ov pad] ...`: every 10 s of battle time, every fighter (`ov` = a lock override +252 is set, `pad` = pad-driven, `lock` = its +0x2FC target). `cost` is the wall time all the morelog code has used so far.
  - Already always-on from earlier batches (now also with the default LOG): `[KOEVT]` (lethal hit, booked KO, finish start with the marks), `[KOCAM]`, `[KOFIX]`, `[TAGTEAM] ... KO of slot / tag in / CALLIN / rebuild`, `[BRVALL]` + `[BRKEVT]` / `[BRKEND]` (break start / end, handler state), `[AO8]` / `[TDASSIST]` / `[AO9]` / `[XAS]` (assist call start / end with the actors), `[OOB]` (stage out-of-bounds moves), `[HUDBREAK]`, `[RETICLE]` (changes + a snapshot every 20 s), `[LOCKFIX]` / `[LOCKCHG]`, `[EXBKO]` / `[XREV]` / `[EXBHIT]`.
- **Cost** (host, `~/dissidia/tt/s2/morelog/b1`: 300 s battle, forced KOs `slot0:40,extra1:90,slot1:150,slot0:210`, default env): the morelog code used 37 ms of wall time in 10653 frames (3.5 us a frame, ~0.01 % of a 30 fps frame); the game's own lines (everything except the test harness's `[FIGHTER]` per-frame dump, which is not on in play) are 583 KB for the battle, 102 `[RETDUMP]` lines (~100 KB), 32 `[EVT]`, 36 `[STATE]`. Well under 5 MB.

### Batch seventy-four (26 Nov, tree ttlockfix, branch tt-lockfix6): the crosshair lost after a finish - cause found, fixed
- **Reproduced headless.** FFA, `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_TESTLOCKOTHER=12 PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_TESTLOCKSAME=1` (lock on the human's own-side extra) + `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_KOLIST=slot1:30` (HP 0 on slotC = the retail finish): the cyan ring is drawn before the finish and is gone at 45 s / 70 s (`fz1_sheet.png`, `fz0_sheet.png`). The human's lock block (`+0x110` / `+0x114` / `+0x126` / `+252` / mode / handler words 0..0x200) is identical before and after, so it is not the lock block.
- **Cause.** A live diff of the camera manager (`09AE8C70`, debug socket `R` before / after the finish, `cap.py` / `exp.py` in `~/dissidia/tt/s2/ttlockfix/`): the finish clears the halfword **`mgr+0x878`: `0x0101` -> `0x0001`** (byte `+0x879` = the lock cursor's enable), sets `+0x8C0` = 2 and the director's `+8 / +0x20 / +0x38` (`0.707 / -0.707 / 10.0`); `+0x6DC` goes to 0. Writing the OLD `+0x878` back on the running game brings the ring back at once (`exp_sheet.png`: left no ring, right ring), writing the director words / `+0x8C0` / `+0x6DC` alone does not (`+0x8C0` is re-derived every frame). `+0x879` is re-armed by a new lock-on, so a lock held through the finish on a target that is not re-acquired (the own-side extra in FFA, the 3 device logs: killer extraP twice, the human's double KO once, lock on extraP) stays without the ring; KOs of an extra (no finish) never cleared it.
- **Fix** (`cam_snap` / `cam_restore`, the same save / put-back as the camera director, so it also covers the extras' kill camera): the camera manager's `+0x878` halfword is saved with the director at the finish start and put back at "finish over" (`[RETICLE] t=35.90s restored: camera manager +0x878 0001 -> 0101 (finish over: ...)`). Host after the fix: the ring is drawn at 45 s and 70 s (`fy1_sheet.png`). `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_CURSORRESTORE_OLD=1` = old. The earlier `+0x114` lead of batch sixty was a side effect of the finish camera's LOCK_SET (not the gate). Not run on a device; the retail finish of a match-ending KO does not run `cam_restore` (nothing to put back).

### Batch seventy-five (26 Nov, tree tthpsame, branch tt-hpsame): HP damage booked twice, EX Burst break on the wrong side, bogus slot breaks
- **1. "Chaos did HP damage to me, but it also said Laguna did" (`desk_logs/rp6_hpdmg_1126_1811.log` t=217.32 / 217.39; same pattern at t=55.34 / 55.54).** After an extra's HP hit on the human (extraP, extraE, correct, `[HPBRV]` + `[TAGTEAM] ... goes to the fighter it hit`) a SECOND plain HP step came 3-12 frames later in the name of the human's slot opponent (slotC: `[HPBRV] slotC ... hits slotH: attacker BRV before 1305, HP damage 301`, slotC's BRV unspent, damage not its BRV: retail's own step with the module's default victim). slotC had no registered hit in that time. The retail source of that step was NOT found (not reproduced by itself headless: natural FFA runs, `_HPMATRIX` pair extraP -> slotH, with `_HPM_B`, show only the right step); the guard rests on the data: every genuine step of a slot fighter in the logs / headless runs has a registered hit 1 frame old.
- **Fix** (`hpstep_core`): a plain step (not an extra's own damage step, not a further victim of `[HPBOTH]`) whose attacker is a slot fighter with NO registered hit in the last 8 frames, against the victim another attacker's HP step booked in the last 20 frames, is skipped like a whiff (`[HPPHANTOM]`: the attacker keeps its BRV, nothing booked, no `[HPDMG]`). An HP attack's damage is applied once, to the fighter hit, with the attacker's own BRV; cross-side and same-side extra / human hits and `[HPBOTH]` go through the same code as before (the guard needs "no hit registered by the attacker"; the second victims of one attack are `forced`, untouched). `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_HPPHANTOM_OLD=1` = old.
- **Test aid** `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_TEST_PHANTOMHP=1`: after an extra's HP step a plain step is forced in the opposing slot fighter's name on the same victim (the RP6 pattern). FFA `_HPMATRIX=10089 _HPM_ALL=1 _HPM_PAIRS=6 _HPM_SWEEP=6 _HPM_NODOWN=1 _HPM_VBRV0=1` (extraP -> slotH), runs `~/dissidia/tt/s2/tthpsame/p_old` (`HPPHANTOM_OLD=1`): `[HPBRV] slotC ... hits slotH ... HP damage 3000` + `[HPDMG] slotC > slotH -3000` (slotH 7624 -> 4624, KO at the 2nd), `p_new`: `[HPPHANTOM] ... skipped, attacker BRV 1060 kept`, slotH stays 7624, slotC BRV unchanged 1060. The extra's own hit (2220) and the second hit are unchanged.
- **2. EX Burst on the human's extra broke the human (`rp6_exb_samebreak_1126_1813.log` t=262.53).** The burster (cross side) took the extra on the human's side to BRV 0; burst hits are not in the hit registry, the reaction arrived in the human slot fighter's handler (the side's slot fighter, held outside the burst): `BREAK victim slotH attacker extraP SAME-SIDE`. Fix (`brk_exbX` in `hitreact2_hook`): a reaction in a slot handler whose owner is not in the running burst, while the burst's victim (controller +0x270 / `exb_p1`) is an extra of the owner's side, goes to that extra's own handler (`[BRKSKIP] ... routed to ... EX Burst`). `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_EXB_SAMESIDE_OLD=1` = old. Test aid `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_TEST_EXBREACT=1` (the retail reaction is delivered to the human's handler while a burst on extraP runs; the headless burst itself deals no hits): `EXBAT=s1:30:x1 SETBRV=partner:29.9:20`: old (first run, retail path) `BREAK victim slotH (HUMAN) ... SAME-SIDE` at the burst; new: `no new break` on extraP, slotH untouched. (The replay through the hook crashed the old-path run once with stale arguments, so the old line comes from the call-through run.)
- **3. Bogus breaks on slotC (`rp6_nobreak_1126_1839.log` t=74.65, 76.18).** `attacker other:18 s2` (the human's ASSIST actor, side 2) hit extraP; the hit was registered under the assist actor only, a reaction then appeared in slotC's handler and `BREAK victim slotC BRV 1375 -> 1375` followed every `WOULD SKIP (log only)`. Fixes: `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_BREAK_UNHIT_GUARD` is now ON by default (`=0` log only: the reaction of a fighter nobody hit, while a hit landed on another fighter within 10 frames, is dropped, `[BRKSKIP]`), and an assist actor's hit is also registered for its caller (`[ASSISTHIT]`, `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_ASSISTHITREG_OLD=1` = old) so the same-side routing (`brk_samesideX`, `booked_extra_victim`) sees a fighter of the right side. Not reproduced headless (no assist hits in the runs).
- **4. Break sound / slow motion on hits on an already broken Emperor.** Headless re-hit in the break (state 3; `_HPM_B` second attack 1.2 s after the break, `SNDLOG=1` new sound-request log, `SLOWLOG=1` / `SLOWSETLOG` slow-motion log): the break's own presentation is `SNDREQ id 10011` (ra 089E9DC4) + `id 100096` (ra 08ADF74C) and hit stop on channel 3 (ra 08ADF7B0 / 08AE010C) inside the reaction; the re-hit in state 3 plays NONE of them (only the normal hit sounds 2410040 / 2400011 ...), because the dropped reaction is not run. The break SE / slow of the user's log is therefore explained by the bogus slotC breaks of item 3 (74.65, 76.18, the break reaction run in an innocent handler), not by the re-hit rule; with the guard on they are gone. Verify on the device. Debug aids added: `PSPRECOMP_TAGTEAM_SNDLOG=1`, `_SLOWLOG=1`.
- Lock-step: the guards read battle state and the hit registry only (no clock / RNG); no new local state. Regression `tagteam_test.py --baseline`: see the commit message / report.
